looks.name: Vault Wall
looks.oneLine: The gold shelf laid out flat in a twelve-cell lattice on a pale vitrine, dropped sixty percent into aubergine, with CASH FOR / GOLD in stencil and the money band as the only accent on the card.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' (retheme_lab.mjs:2886, the lookGround branch wins before every rotation), so this theme is on its ground on every seed. W=H=1080, COLS=4, ROWS=3, gap=28: cells are 235 x 322.67, and each cutout is fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box and then scaled 0.96, so it occupies at most 202 x 287 of its cell -- about 86 per cent, not 0.96 of the cell. Shadows are rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offset 10/16. `light` = lum(c1)>0.55 ? c1 : lum(c2)>0.55 ? c2 : '#eceef2'; nn10 c1 #2c1c37 (L 0.016) and c2 #1e0925 (L 0.006) are both deep, so the lattice always lands on the hard-coded #eceef2 and takes scrimColor = c1 at 0.6 (lum(dark) < 0.4). A pale vitrine dimmed 60 per cent: bright metal survives it, which is why gold gets a wall. The panel pass (2963) then fills every stat tile with rgba(#2c1c37,0.9) and sets its copy #ffffff, so no small type sits on the lattice. Colour chain, all engine: the money band takes th.accent (1047, locked); the phone plate takes th.support because the accent is already spent (1573); the kicker plate and the double hairline frame take SIG.gold.tone2 = support (1596, 1604). On nn10 that is #f5ba08 over #b68b1b; on jw02 #fec674 over #c39550 -- every plate on the card is a gold, on a violet ground. TYPE WARNING, measured: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed. CASH FOR (8) and GOLD (4) are safe; PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE (24) is not, so on layouts that set the price line in the display face it prints in the substitute -- accept it, or let the money word 95% carry the band.
looks.imagery: The wall is built by the engine, not chosen: cand = the gold deck prefixes plus the gold subject shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Simulated against the current approved list that is exactly twelve objects for twelve cells, no repeat: gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single. gold-bars-fan, gold-bars-row and gold-bracelet-pair are MULTI-dropped; gold-pocket-watch, gold-rings-scatter, gold-scale-weighing, gold-scrap-mixed, gold-teeth-dental and gold-watch-luxury fall past the slice. Two cells are low-res originals -- gold-bars 461x326 and gold-jewelry 511x226 -- both drawn down to at most 202px wide, so they are soft-safe but shallow; gold-jewelry is a wide, short pile and leaves its cell looking empty top and bottom. ONE PRODUCT SITS OVER THE WALL: the placement search (3169) pushes a 'Hero Product' cutout on any card that has none, and none of this theme's four layouts authors one. It is drawn from the gold deck pool (all 21 approved gold- cutouts) and evicted if it overlaps any text box (3160). mustShow/neverShow govern that one layer -- they cannot see the wall cells, which are painted into the ground canvas. Marks: addElements places one or two, corners and the money word's flanks; ELEMENTS.gold colours are the fixed golds #f2c14e / #c9950f / #fff1b8, and two marks in five are iOS emoji from the gold list (money bag, gem, ring, watch, coin) -- the look cannot switch emoji off, so the watch glyph is the one to discard by eye.
looks.copy: The pawnbroker with the shutter down, counting stock. Flat, exact, no adjectives. Headline: CASH FOR / GOLD -- two lines, one sentence, Big Shoulders Stencil Display in ink on both, never a colour change on line two. Selling points (the deck's own, at least two print by the minimum-information pass at 3559): TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU plus WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. Money band: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, money word 95% -- a number a seller can check, which is the whole point of not saying top prices. ITEMS LINE, THE ONE ENGINE EDIT THIS THEME NEEDS: CATEGORY_COPY.gold.items still ships '10k - 14k - 18k - Scrap & Dental - Cuban Links - Rolex - Cartier - Tiffany - Yurman'; no approved cutout can back Rolex, Cartier, Tiffany or Yurman, and neither Scrap nor Dental reaches this wall. It should read '10k - 14k - 18k - Cuban Links - Chains - Class Rings - Earrings - Mixed Lots', where every noun has a cell. Kicker: GOLD BUYER (KICKERS.gold[0]; the rotation is seeded, TOP BUYER / FAST CASH / TOP RATED / WE PAY MORE are the other draws and none repeats a word on the card). Sticker: ON THE SPOT. Rating is 4.9 with five stars wherever stars appear. Badges render LICENSED / DISCREET / PRIVATE -- the engine already swaps INSURED to DISCREET off the cars deck (1385), so no rule is needed for it. Two of three seeds also draw the gold signature frame: a double hairline in the support gold at inset 22/34.
variations: Full shelf (reference build) -- the twelve cells the engine draws, one product over them from the same shelf
Bars in the corner -- the hero placed at a corner spot is gold-bars-stack or gold-bar-single, which reads as bullion over a jewellery case
Gold on aubergine (nn10) vs gold on violet (jw02) -- the same lattice, the scrim hue is the only change
Challenge cut -- WE BEAT / CASH4GOLD or WE TOP / THE PAWN SHOP replaces the opener on one seed in three; the WE MATCH draw prints without an object and is discarded
fixesApplied: Cell list replaced with the twelve the engine actually draws; the three MULTI-dropped and five past-the-slice assets are named as unreachable instead of listed as cells
Cell geometry corrected to 235 x 322.67 with a 211 x 298.67 fit box scaled 0.96 (max 202 x 287), not '242x322 fitted at 0.96'

faces.num DM Mono removed -- it is stripped on the jw02 half at 1578; the engine's own pairing rule sets num = support when the display face is not plain, and stencil is not plain, so the number is Satoshi

Lock 5 bound where it can be: the cash- cutout prefix is barred; the line-art cash and dollar MARKS cannot be barred from a look (neverShow only reads cutout layer names), so the imagery names the emoji and icon pools instead of pretending a rule catches them
Items line rewritten so every noun has a cell -- Rolex, Cartier, Tiffany, Yurman and Scrap & Dental cannot be pictured by any approved gold cutout
seal:INSURED deleted: retheme_lab.mjs:1385 already swaps it to DISCREET off the cars deck; the rule was redundant, not a catch

Beyond the audit: the variation 'Bars only' is gone (only three bar assets survive the wall filter), and the false claim that no hero sits over the wall is replaced by the truth -- the placement search adds one on every card
looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: eight cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else. Ten were written; two are gone and the reasons are in droppedThemes.

FIVE LOCKS, ALL MEASURED IN THE REPO
1. GROUND VALUE. Seven palettes, every c1 under L 0.06: nn10 #2c1c37 0.016, nn02 #241f3b 0.017, jw02 #3e3577 0.049, jw01 #1f3e7a 0.051, jw09 #054666 0.054, jw05 #044a51 0.055, jw07 #054e2f 0.057. Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. But the card does not stop there: because the accent is spent, the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT (1573), and the kicker plate and the category's signature frame take SIG[cat].tone2 (1596, 1604). A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Phones take jw09 and jw01. Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. The old 'two lit plates is the fault' rule was describing something the engine does on purpose; this is the version that holds.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Cuban Cast
looks.oneLine: One piece of worn gold drawn huge into the ground under a single diagonal window shadow, the money word across the lit left third.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='cast' forces dg='cast' on every seed (2886). Ground fills jw02 c1 #3e3577 (L 0.049), then a white 0.10 -> 0 linear from the top-left corner. The hero is fitted k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) = min(669.6/w, 993.6/h), translated to (712.8, 561.6), rotated -0.12 rad, drawn at alpha 0.92 with shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.35), blur 40, offset 24/30. Then the window shadow: a 26px-blurred rgba(8,10,16,0.5) wedge from 0.62W to the right edge plus a 60px-blurred penumbra at 0.25 from 0.5W, so the light is upper-left and the shadow falls across the hero's right two-thirds. Finally scrimColor = c1 at 0.22. lum(c1) is far under 0.55, so the pale branch (ink body, 0.58 shadow, 0.30 scrim) cannot fire; if a pale palette is ever substituted the theme is invalid. Panels over the cast go solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with white copy (2963). Colour chain: money band = accent (jw02 #fec674, nn02 #feb263), phone plate = support (#c39550 / #cd7c0e), kicker plate and the double frame = support again -- every plate a gold on a violet ground. THE RULE THIS GROUND BREAKS: at 3428 the engine deletes every 'Hero Product' and 'Lineup Product' layer on a cast card -- the product IS the ground -- so this card carries no cutout layer at all, and lookFaults (2536) therefore checks mustShow against nothing and neverShow against nothing. On this theme the two lists are documentation, not a gate; the only real guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645). There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc, so the hero is a uniform seeded draw, use[(sd*7+3) % 21], over the whole approved gold shelf: nine of the twenty-one are admissible here, about two cards in five, and the rest are discarded on the contact sheet.
looks.imagery: Admissible heroes, all verified by opening the file: gold-bracelet-cuban (1484x1184, a real Cuban link bracelet, the lead), gold-necklace-single (1314x1591, a heavy rope chain), gold-chains-pile (2048x1718), gold-chains (624x457), gold-class-ring (846x1232, a gold ring with a coloured stone), gold-bracelet-pair (1294x1041), gold-rings-scatter (2048x2048), gold-earrings-pile (1054x838), gold-jewelry-mixed (2048x1734). Every one of them downscales into the 669 x 993 cast box. Discard the other twelve draws: both watches (gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch -- this collection has no watch card and a watch hero is a watch card), gold-teeth-dental, gold-scale-weighing (that is Under One Lamp's subject and a near-white body), gold-coins-pile and gold-scrap-mixed (the loose-gold themes' subjects), and the four bar assets plus gold-jewelry (511x226, which the cast fit would upscale 1.3x). gold-jewelry cannot be barred by prefix without also barring gold-jewelry-mixed, so it is a discard rule, not a neverShow entry. No second product: the cast ground is the picture. Marks: one or two, corners and the money-word flanks at 118px, from ELEMENTS.gold in its fixed golds; two in five are iOS emoji and the watch glyph is discarded.
looks.copy: The written-offer voice: we test it, you watch, you decide. Headline: CASH OUT YOUR / GOLD -- one face, one colour, both lines. Selling points: WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE plus TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU. Money band: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, money word 95%. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Items line, matched to what this card can show: '10k - 14k - 18k - Cuban Links - Rope Chains - Bracelets - Class Rings - Necklaces'. Kicker: GOLD BUYER. Badges render LICENSED / DISCREET / PRIVATE. Challenge cut on one seed in three names household targets only -- WE BEAT / CASH4GOLD, WE TOP / THE PAWN SHOP, WE OUTBID / EZPAWN; the WE MATCH draw prints as WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object (2841) and is discarded, because the standing rule is that WE MATCH always takes an object. Copy sits on the LIT left third; nothing sits over the bracelet, and the engine enforces it -- a cutout overlapping any text box is evicted at 3160.
variations: Bracelet lead (default) -- gold-bracelet-cuban, the piece the copy names
Necklace lead -- gold-necklace-single, the same one-object premise on a vertical silhouette
Shadow left -- mirror the wedge so the light falls from the right; one card in three, so a page is not all the same diagonal
Amber on violet (jw02) vs amber on near-black violet (nn02), where the bracelet is the only bright object on the card
fixesApplied: The false claim 'Hero is HERO.gold[0]' is gone: HERO is only consulted when there is no deck, and CATEGORY_COPY.gold is always a deck, so the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % 21] over the whole gold shelf

The hero is now a closed list: nine admissible names in mustShow, and every other gold asset that could pass -- both watches, teeth, scale, coins-pile, scrap and the four bar assets -- named in neverShow
The 'president-watch lead' variation is deleted and gold-watch-luxury moved from mustShow to neverShow: no card in this collection may be built on a watch

The cast-to-tile fallback is stated where it is real (dgKinds = ['cast','tile'] at 2858) and the ground tokens now use the only values the matcher understands: tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab, flat
Alternates re-ordered to the engine's own HERO.gold order and, more usefully, replaced by a verified admissible list with pixel sizes

Beyond the audit: on a cast ground the engine deletes the product layer (3428), so mustShow and neverShow are inert here -- the guard is the manifest product field, and the theme says so instead of implying a gate that does not exist
Beyond the audit: arcCrown dropped from the layouts -- its crown spot places a product that the cast pass then deletes, after the money word has already been pushed down to make room for it

looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. The kicker plate and the single-rule silver frame take SIG.silver.tone2 = accent2, a near-white (#ffedea / #feecf2), on two seeds in three (1596, 1604). Verified by opening them: silver-flatware (364x587) is a tied bundle of antique forks and spoons, silver-bars (519x476) three plain poured bars, silver-coins-tube (1513x1586) a clear tube of Washington quarters with two loose coins -- the 90% coins the copy names. silver-tea-set and silver-serving-tray are rejected cutouts and can never appear. Marks: one or two from ELEMENTS.silver in its greys and whites; two in five are iOS emoji from the silver list (medal, cutlery, ring, coin).

looks.name: Coin Tray Wall
looks.oneLine: Eleven coin holdings -- trays, rolls, tubes, jars, albums, loose piles -- laid out flat on a dimmed green felt lattice under WE BUY / COINS.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. jw07 is the highest-scoring Jewel palette (50 per cent) and its ground #054e2f is a deep bottle green -- the coin-tray felt colour, which is why it leads. Both c1 (L 0.057) and c2 #003928 (L 0.031) are deep, so the lattice lands on #eceef2: 4x3, 28px gaps, cells 235 x 322.67, each cutout fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box then scaled 0.96 (at most 202 x 287), shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16, then scrimColor = #054e2f at 0.6. Panels solid at rgba(#054e2f,0.9), copy white. Colour chain: money band = accent (jw07 #e1c2fe lilac, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach); phone plate = support (#9eb666 olive on jw07, #53b9e0 sky on jw01); kicker plate and the dotted coins frame = accent2, a near-white, on two seeds in three. On jw07 the olive sits in the ground's own family, which is why a green palette can carry an olive plate without reading as a third colour. THIS THEME MUST NEVER INVOKE THE SLAB FRAME: slabFrame() is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ (3429), the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only, and ground:slab is in neverShow.
looks.imagery: The engine's wall, simulated against the current approved list: eleven objects for twelve cells, so exactly one repeats. The last three come from SUBJECTS.coins, whose cut regex is /^(coin-|silver-coins|gold-coins)/ and whose never list does not exclude gold- or silver- -- they are coins and they belong on a coins wall, and they are painted into the ground where no rule can see them, which is why gold- and silver- can still be barred as a product layer. FOUR ASSETS CANNOT BE CELLS and are not named as such: coin-slab (144x144) and coin-single-large (223 wide) fail the width>=240 filter, and coin-graded-fan-three (-fan) and coin-silver-dollar-pair (-pair) are MULTI-dropped; coin-single-large is also excluded by name in the MULTI regex. I opened coin-slab: it is a 144px photograph of a raw circulated portrait coin, not a slab of any kind, so nothing on this card may call it one. I opened coin-slabs-stack: three graded holders with real coins in the windows and BLANK WHITE LABELS -- acceptable as one cell among twelve at 202px, never as a row and never as the hero. looks.name: Closing Time Wall
looks.oneLine: The device wall from the shop's own site after hours: twelve single iPhones in an even lattice, dimmed sixty percent into petrol blue, with the opening hours running under the money band.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. jw09 c1 #054666 (L 0.054) and c2 #023153 are both deep, so the lattice lands on the hard-coded #eceef2: 4x3, 28px gaps, cells 235 x 322.67, each cutout fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box then scaled 0.96 (at most 202 x 287), shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16, then scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. Panels over the wall go solid at rgba(#054666,0.9) with #ffffff copy, which is what keeps UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY off the lattice. Colour chain: money band = accent (jw09 #fdc0b7 coral, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach); phone plate = support (#3ebfc9 cyan, #53b9e0 sky); kicker plate = SIG.phones.tone2 = support again; SIG.phones has no frame, so this is the only card in the collection without a signature rule around it. SET THE DECK EXPLICITLY TO DEVICE_DECKS.iphone: p.cat 'phones' rotates the Apple lines over ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'] (2792), so half the seeds are an iPad or a MacBook card. Those are caught by neverShow ('ipad', 'mac', 'qs-') as a product fault, but the fault does not change the deck on the retry, so they are discarded rather than repaired.
looks.imagery: The twelve cells are fixed by the engine, not chosen. Simulated against the current approved list -- deck prefixes plus SUBJECTS.iphone, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12) -- the wall is exactly twelve distinct objects with no repeat: iphone-15-pro-back-black, -blue, -gold, -white, iphone-15-pro-front-on, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-hand-back-offer, iphone-in-hand-screen-on, iphone-screen-on-glow, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, own-apple-cosmic-orange-06. I opened all twelve. Six are clean bright backs (gold, white, silver, blue, and the two 17 Pro bodies), two are orange press renders (-02 a phone on a black plinth at 311px, -06 a close crop whose lower body is cut), two are screen-on units, and two are hand shots -- iphone-hand-back-offer is a champagne back whose left edge is scalloped where the fingers were removed, and iphone-in-hand-screen-on is a blank white screen with fingertip fragments at the left edge. Both are on the owner's approved list, and neither can be excluded from a wall: the cells are painted into the ground canvas where no mustShow or neverShow can reach them. That is the honest census, and it is why the census replaces the old rule about six bright cells, which no set of approved assets could satisfy. ONE PRODUCT SITS OVER THE WALL and that one IS governed: the placement search draws it from the iPhone deck pool of 22, and only the six clean backs are admitted -- six of the twenty-two, so about one card in four keeps its hero and the rest are discarded -- the two hand shots, both screen-on units, iphone-pair-front-back, the ip-group lineups, the four qs-iphone-17 press composites and all five own-apple singles are barred (the orange ones are 311-380px or carry a second object or a lit galaxy screen). Marks: ELEMENTS.phones in the palette tones; two in five are iOS emoji from the phone list.
looks.copy: The shop itself, not a pitch -- this is what is on the counter tonight. Headline: SELL YOUR / iPHONE. Selling points: CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED plus SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME. Money band: UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY, money word $1,100 -- bounded and checkable. The hours line carries the theme's name: OPEN 7 DAYS - 9AM-8PM - WALK-INS WELCOME. Items: iPhone 17 - 16 - 15 - Pro & Pro Max, which is the deck's own line; note that the library has no approved 16 cutout, so the wall shows 15 Pro and 17 Pro bodies under it -- every one of them is above the iPhone 12 floor, and the shop does buy the 16. Kicker: APPLE BUYER. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Cities: LONG BEACH - LAKEWOOD - DOWNEY - CARSON - TORRANCE. Payment line: CASH - ZELLE - VENMO - WIRE, YOUR CHOICE. Sticker: PAID TODAY. Badges render LICENSED / TRUSTED / LOCAL (the engine swaps INSURED to TRUSTED off the cars deck). Rating 4.9, five stars. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Blue Pen Estimate
looks.oneLine: A cream ruled sheet with three punch holes down the left, an offer typed out in indigo ballpoint, one yellow highlighter across the money line, and a single Apple unit laid on the page with its own shadow.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:ruled — #fbf7ea stock, 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px from y=150, a 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes down the left at 18/50/82% of height, fibre noise and a 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10) to 0 binding shadow at the head. Painted as bg {type:'image', src:'paper:ruled', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001} so the palette never tints the paper; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. THIS RECORD MUST CARRY key:'written-quote-blue-pen-estimate' and sheet:'paper:ruled', and needs the four collection-wide engine changes (key lookup, categories ring, look.sheet at line 2650, a paper branch in groundNow at 2525); without them the look never applies, the stock rotates on seed%5 and every card self-audits as a ground mismatch. PALETTES BY THE NAME THE OWNER SEES: lp01 Indigo Cash, accent #084f88, and lp08 Indigo Trade, accent #0c42ab — deep indigo ballpoint, not navy-the-adjective. THE PEN IS THE ONLY COLOUR: pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f on kicker, sub, items, CTA, badges and website. The engine assigns headline ink by layer parity at 2691, which on bandKnockout puts both headline lines on #26231f and never shows the pen; assign by headline order instead — opener in ink, money word in pen. ONE HIGHLIGHTER, AND IT IS THE LAYOUT THAT GUARANTEES IT: checklistHero's only convertible rect is the 760x194 CTA card and bandKnockout's is the 1012x252 knockout band (a money plate at 1047, so it clears the 210px height test). Stroke at 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle plus or minus 0.8 degrees, with the Marker Overrun twin beneath at 0.30 opacity, 22px longer, angle minus 0.6, so the ends run past the words. Squares under 130px become solid pen boxes with white numerals; circles — checklistHero's three tick discs and trust()'s check — take the pen, which is right here. THE SNAP MUST MOVE THE ROW: line 2684 snaps single-line text to the 54px grid and leaves the tick disc behind, landing the three Point rows on 632/686/794 against discs at 566/662/758 with an uneven 54/108 gap. Until the snap carries circle, number box and label together, bandKnockout is the only safe layout on this stock, and checklistHero ships only after that fix. PALE VS DEEP: both palettes are pale (c1 #ecf4fd, #eef4fe) and the sheet is drawn rather than derived, so a pale palette changes nothing; a deep one would leave the cream cream and only darken the pen. The sheet is never inverted.

looks.collectionNote:
Eight sheets of real stationery with an offer written out on them. Two of the original ten are gone (see droppedThemes) because their categories have no cutout that shows what the card talks about.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY OPENING FILES, and what it changed. All five surviving own-apple-* cutouts are AI fabrications, not Apple press renders: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 puts an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. Every own-apple- id is therefore banned collection-wide and DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose the 'own-apple-cosmic-orange' entry that leads it. Every qs- Apple render I opened (qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-device-macbook-pro) is either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render with a full iridescent wallpaper, so none can appear on a sheet whose claim is one ink. iphone-15-pro-back-black is a macro crop of a camera corner, not a unit. car-keys-fob is a hand holding a fob whose badge is a garbled three-oval marque — a fabricated emblem of the same class as strip-kit-meter — and car-hand-keys-over, despite its name, is a plain unbranded flip key with no hand in it. The clean pool is small and it is named exactly in each theme.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES, measured against scripts/retheme_lab.mjs and app.js, because six of the ten original recipes described behaviour the code does not have.
1. look.key: lines 554, 563 and 2764 look a record up by L.key; assets/looks.json entries carry only id. Until each record carries key === its id, no look applies at all and every card falls back to a random palette and the handwritten Lined Paper faces from pickFaces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand).
2. look.categories is dead. The plan at 549-562 reads only layouts, variations, palettes and key; wantCat comes from RING[(base + e.v) % 8] at 2731. Every look in this collection currently receives cards from all eight categories, so a silver look's mustShow fails on seven cards in eight and the re-seed cannot help (base does not include attempt). Seed the ring from look.categories.
3. look.sheet does not exist. Line 2650 rotates the four stocks on seed%5, so every 'this look pins X' claim holds one or two cards in five. Change to const sheet = (look && look.sheet) || [...][seed % 5] and give each record its sheet.
4. ground:'paper' now works one way and not the other: line 2886 makes a paper look skip tile, cast, photo, scene and slab grounds, but groundNow at 2525 has no paper branch, so bg 'paper:ruled' reads as 'flat' and every card in this collection self-audits as "ground flat but the theme is paper" and burns its one re-seed. Add : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper'.
5. The 54px baseline snap (2684) moves single-line text and leaves its furniture behind. On checklistHero the three Point rows land on baselines 632/686/794 while their tick discs stay at 566/662/758: the ticks detach and the row gap goes 54, then 108. Until the snap carries the row group, only bandKnockout is geometrically safe on ruled and legal stock — which is why the four ruled/legal themes here ship checklistHero and bandKnockout only, and the four grid/dot themes (no snap at all) carry stepsFlow and reviewProof.
6. The highlighter count is a property of the layout, not of the recipe. familyTreatment converts any rect that is a money plate, or 200px+ wide and 210px or less tall, into a highlighter. On the real templates that is one stroke on checklistHero (the 760x194 CTA card) and one on bandKnockout (the 1012x252 knockout band, which becomes a money plate at 1047 and so clears the height test), four on stepsFlow (kicker pill plus three step cards), four on reviewProof (rate pill plus three chips, with the 940x336 quote card becoming the sticky note) and SIX on trustSeal (status pill, four 442x148 tiles, phone plate). trustSeal is out of this collection entirely: six pastel bands on a paper sheet is the jumbled colour mess the owner rejects, and its seal circle would fill solid #accent under the circle branch at 2698. Dropping it also removes the only place a card showed a single '4.9★' glyph; the one star run left in the collection is reviewProof's ★★★★★, which is five.
7. Headline ink is assigned by layer parity (2691: fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : inkDark). On bandKnockout both headline lines land on #26231f and the pen never reaches the headline. Assign by headline order instead: the opener takes the ink, the money word takes the pen.
8. Fixed since the audit and relied on here: slabFrame is gated on look.ground === 'slab' (3425), so a paper look never gets a graded frame; the brand wordmark inks #ffffff or #14161c and never th.ink (2574), so no more brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes; the no-repeat pass at 3385 swaps a seal stack that echoes a seal row, so bandKnockout's badge words do not print twice; the tile-wall MULTI filter keeps two-up composites off any lattice.
9. logo: rules in a neverShow only bind when written as the full source path. lookFaults tests src.startsWith('logo:' + rule.slice(5)) and inkedLogo emits 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c', so 'logo:audi' matched nothing in any of the original ten. They are written 'logo:assets/logos/audi.png' here.
10. challenge fires on one card in three for every look (2818). It is gated on look.challenge here so the comparison card belongs to Two Numbers Sheet and nowhere else.

HOW THE RULES BIND. neverShow entries containing a space are skipped by the matcher (2531) — they are for people. The binding entries are literal startsWith prefixes, ground: tokens, assets/ prefixes and logo: paths, and a fault re-seeds the card once. Every theme below was tested against all 349 approved cutouts: mustShow and neverShow together cover the whole shelf, so there is no cutout that passes neverShow while matching no mustShow prefix — the leak the audit found in all ten originals (68 to 181 cutouts each) is zero in all eight. Since the engine places exactly one cutout per card and ghost assortments are off, one clean unit per card is structural rather than aspirational, and subjectFaults already stops an iPad joining an iPhone card.

WHAT THE SET LOOKS LIKE. The ground is never a photograph and never a gradient: it is one of the four drawn stocks (paper:ruled cream #fbf7ea, paper:legal canary #fff3b8, paper:grid cool #f7f9fb, paper:dots warm #fbfaf5), two themes to a stock. Every palette is a Lined Paper (lp) theme, which means the palette IS the pen: th.accent is one deep ink at L 0.42 and nothing else on the card is coloured except one translucent highlighter with overrun ends and, where a layout has a panel, one sticky note. All body copy is printed type from assets/approved-fonts.json, set through look.faces because the brief is an offer typed out for a customer, not a doodle. Palettes are named as the owner sees them in the picker (lp01 Indigo Cash, lp02 Amber Offer, lp05 Sky Ticket, lp06 Red Deal, lp07 Amber Market, lp08 Indigo Trade, lp09 Teal Value, lp10 Red Quote) with the ink described honestly beside the name, because several names and inks disagree. Pokémon is absent because its whole approved pool is one cutout, poke-slabs-trio, a faceless slab trio the owner reserves for the Slab Frame theme; the PALFIT 'pokemon avoid /Paper|Pastel/' line does not in fact fire, since 2757 exempts family palettes. Watches are absent by the owner's rule. Bikes, trucks and vans appear only as deck rotations on the tow sheet.

'a second highlighter colour' and 'a second pen hue' banned nothing, since familyTreatment picks one HIGHLIGHT and one pen per card by construction: replaced with 'more than one highlighter stroke on a card', and the layouts are cut to the two that actually produce exactly one — bandKnockout and checklistHero. trustSeal, which produces six, is dropped.

looks.collectionNote:
Eight sheets of real stationery with an offer written out on them. Two of the original ten are gone (see droppedThemes) because their categories have no cutout that shows what the card talks about.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY OPENING FILES, and what it changed. All five surviving own-apple-* cutouts are AI fabrications, not Apple press renders: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 puts an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. Every own-apple- id is therefore banned collection-wide and DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose the 'own-apple-cosmic-orange' entry that leads it. Every qs- Apple render I opened (qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-device-macbook-pro) is either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render with a full iridescent wallpaper, so none can appear on a sheet whose claim is one ink. iphone-15-pro-back-black is a macro crop of a camera corner, not a unit. car-keys-fob is a hand holding a fob whose badge is a garbled three-oval marque — a fabricated emblem of the same class as strip-kit-meter — and car-hand-keys-over, despite its name, is a plain unbranded flip key with no hand in it. The clean pool is small and it is named exactly in each theme.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES, measured against scripts/retheme_lab.mjs and app.js, because six of the ten original recipes described behaviour the code does not have.
1. look.key: lines 554, 563 and 2764 look a record up by L.key; assets/looks.json entries carry only id. Until each record carries key === its id, no look applies at all and every card falls back to a random palette and the handwritten Lined Paper faces from pickFaces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand).
2. look.categories is dead. The plan at 549-562 reads only layouts, variations, palettes and key; wantCat comes from RING[(base + e.v) % 8] at 2731. Every look in this collection currently receives cards from all eight categories, so a silver look's mustShow fails on seven cards in eight and the re-seed cannot help (base does not include attempt). Seed the ring from look.categories.
3. look.sheet does not exist. Line 2650 rotates the four stocks on seed%5, so every 'this look pins X' claim holds one or two cards in five. Change to const sheet = (look && look.sheet) || [...][seed % 5] and give each record its sheet.
4. ground:'paper' now works one way and not the other: line 2886 makes a paper look skip tile, cast, photo, scene and slab grounds, but groundNow at 2525 has no paper branch, so bg 'paper:ruled' reads as 'flat' and every card in this collection self-audits as "ground flat but the theme is paper" and burns its one re-seed. Add : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper'.
5. The 54px baseline snap (2684) moves single-line text and leaves its furniture behind. On checklistHero the three Point rows land on baselines 632/686/794 while their tick discs stay at 566/662/758: the ticks detach and the row gap goes 54, then 108. Until the snap carries the row group, only bandKnockout is geometrically safe on ruled and legal stock — which is why the four ruled/legal themes here ship checklistHero and bandKnockout only, and the four grid/dot themes (no snap at all) carry stepsFlow and reviewProof.
6. The highlighter count is a property of the layout, not of the recipe. familyTreatment converts any rect that is a money plate, or 200px+ wide and 210px or less tall, into a highlighter. On the real templates that is one stroke on checklistHero (the 760x194 CTA card) and one on bandKnockout (the 1012x252 knockout band, which becomes a money plate at 1047 and so clears the height test), four on stepsFlow (kicker pill plus three step cards), four on reviewProof (rate pill plus three chips, with the 940x336 quote card becoming the sticky note) and SIX on trustSeal (status pill, four 442x148 tiles, phone plate). trustSeal is out of this collection entirely: six pastel bands on a paper sheet is the jumbled colour mess the owner rejects, and its seal circle would fill solid #accent under the circle branch at 2698. Dropping it also removes the only place a card showed a single '4.9★' glyph; the one star run left in the collection is reviewProof's ★★★★★, which is five.
7. Headline ink is assigned by layer parity (2691: fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : inkDark). On bandKnockout both headline lines land on #26231f and the pen never reaches the headline. Assign by headline order instead: the opener takes the ink, the money word takes the pen.
8. Fixed since the audit and relied on here: slabFrame is gated on look.ground === 'slab' (3425), so a paper look never gets a graded frame; the brand wordmark inks #ffffff or #14161c and never th.ink (2574), so no more brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes; the no-repeat pass at 3385 swaps a seal stack that echoes a seal row, so bandKnockout's badge words do not print twice; the tile-wall MULTI filter keeps two-up composites off any lattice.
9. logo: rules in a neverShow only bind when written as the full source path. lookFaults tests src.startsWith('logo:' + rule.slice(5)) and inkedLogo emits 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c', so 'logo:audi' matched nothing in any of the original ten. They are written 'logo:assets/logos/audi.png' here.
10. challenge fires on one card in three for every look (2818). It is gated on look.challenge here so the comparison card belongs to Two Numbers Sheet and nowhere else.

HOW THE RULES BIND. neverShow entries containing a space are skipped by the matcher (2531) — they are for people. The binding entries are literal startsWith prefixes, ground: tokens, assets/ prefixes and logo: paths, and a fault re-seeds the card once. Every theme below was tested against all 349 approved cutouts: mustShow and neverShow together cover the whole shelf, so there is no cutout that passes neverShow while matching no mustShow prefix — the leak the audit found in all ten originals (68 to 181 cutouts each) is zero in all eight. Since the engine places exactly one cutout per card and ghost assortments are off, one clean unit per card is structural rather than aspirational, and subjectFaults already stops an iPad joining an iPhone card.

WHAT THE SET LOOKS LIKE. The ground is never a photograph and never a gradient: it is one of the four drawn stocks (paper:ruled cream #fbf7ea, paper:legal canary #fff3b8, paper:grid cool #f7f9fb, paper:dots warm #fbfaf5), two themes to a stock. Every palette is a Lined Paper (lp) theme, which means the palette IS the pen: th.accent is one deep ink at L 0.42 and nothing else on the card is coloured except one translucent highlighter with overrun ends and, where a layout has a panel, one sticky note. All body copy is printed type from assets/approved-fonts.json, set through look.faces because the brief is an offer typed out for a customer, not a doodle. Palettes are named as the owner sees them in the picker (lp01 Indigo Cash, lp02 Amber Offer, lp05 Sky Ticket, lp06 Red Deal, lp07 Amber Market, lp08 Indigo Trade, lp09 Teal Value, lp10 Red Quote) with the ink described honestly beside the name, because several names and inks disagree. Pokémon is absent because its whole approved pool is one cutout, poke-slabs-trio, a faceless slab trio the owner reserves for the Slab Frame theme; the PALFIT 'pokemon avoid /Paper|Pastel/' line does not in fact fire, since 2757 exempts family palettes. Watches are absent by the owner's rule. Bikes, trucks and vans appear only as deck rotations on the tow sheet.

looks.name: Graph Paper Quote
looks.oneLine: An engineer's grid sheet in cool white with a deep teal technical pen, figures set in DM Mono, and one Mac or iPad laid on the lattice with its screen dark.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:grid — #f7f9fb cool stock with a 1.4px #b9cbe2 lattice every 48px in both axes, no margin rule, no punch holes, the same fibre noise and the same 70px binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:grid', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Record fields: key:'written-quote-graph-paper-quote', sheet:'paper:grid', challenge:false, plus the four collection-wide engine changes. PALETTE: lp05, which the owner's picker calls Sky Ticket; its accent is #06585c, a deep teal, and the record says both so the name and the description meet. NO LATTICE ALIGNMENT IS CLAIMED. familyTreatment's only geometry is the baseline snap at 2684 and it is gated on /ruled|legal/; grid and dot stocks get none. The original recipe's '48px lattice does the aligning' had no code path, and it is gone. What the grid stock does buy this look is the opposite and it is worth more: with no snap running, the layouts whose single-line type sits inside a panel are safe here, which is why stepsFlow and reviewProof live on this sheet and not on a ruled one. stepsFlow gives four highlighter bands — the 300x64 kicker pill and three 912x138 step cards — all in the same HIGHLIGHT pastel, with the three 84x84 step-number boxes in solid teal pen and white numerals: highlighted rows in a list, which is the sheet's own idiom. reviewProof gives four bands (the 660x92 rate pill and three 280x74 chips) and turns its 940x336 quote card into the one sticky note at 0.96 opacity, tilt plus or minus 1.2 degrees, shadow blur 22 offset 4/10. checklistHero gives one band, the 760x194 CTA card. Every stroke carries the Marker Overrun twin at 0.30 opacity, 22px longer, angle minus 0.6 — on grid stock the overrun is what stops a stroke reading as a printed rectangle. Pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f on everything else, assigned by headline order rather than by the layer parity at 2691. PALE VS DEEP: lp05's c1 is #e9f7f7 and it never reaches the paper, because the grid stock is drawn; a deep palette would darken the pen and leave the lattice colour untouched.
looks.imagery: One machine, flat on the grid, lower right, clear of the type, with a real drop shadow — and its screen dark, because this card's whole claim is one ink. Mac: mac-pro-open-front is the hero, which I opened — a space-grey MacBook Pro seen front-on, screen off, function-row keyboard, uniform-thickness body, the only approved Mac cutout that can be dated to the M-series and so the only one that honestly carries the M1-through-M5 items line. mac-half-open-glow is the alternate, a dark rear three-quarter of an open machine with the screen off. iPad: ipad-with-keyboard, one iPad in a Magic Keyboard shot from the side, screen off, uniform bezels and no home button; ipad-with-pencil as the alternate, an iPad corner with an Apple Pencil beside it, screen off. Everything else in the Mac and iPad shelves is out for a reason I checked: own-stock-macbook-open is an Intel-era keyboard topcase with a Touch Bar and no screen and is rejected; own-stock-macbook-stack is a pile of six tapered closed bodies; mac-pair-open-angle is two machines, not one; mac-air-open-angle and macbook-open are rejected relics; ipad-front is rejected for its home button; and qs-device-macbook-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5 and qs-ipad-air-11-m3 are screen-on renders and two-up composites carrying full iridescent wallpapers — a complete second colour system on a one-ink card. This record needs cuts overrides ['mac-pro-open-front','mac-half-open-glow'] and ['ipad-with-keyboard','ipad-with-pencil'] so the deck cannot reach the rest. Marks are the macbook and ipad sets in pen — bolt, check, dollar, battery, tag — one or two in free corners, following the Apple line rather than the category, so no iPhone mark on a MacBook card.
neverShow: more than one cutout layer on a card, or a cutout whose filename does not start with one of this theme's mustShow prefixes
an iPad on a card whose headline says MACBOOK, and the reverse — subjectFaults already enforces this from the deck
a screen-on render or any cutout carrying a wallpaper
a product cutout over any line of type
a claim that type lands on the lattice: grid stock has no snap and none is asserted
handwriting faces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand, Shadows Into Light, Gloria Hallelujah, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Amatic SC, Cabin Sketch)
trustSeal, whose six converted panels would put six highlighter bands on the sheet
a curved headline, a gradient fill, a glass rim, a neon glow, a vignette or a grain layer
looks.copy: Technical and unfussy — a spec sheet that happens to be an offer. This is the Mac and iPad sheet: the copy comes from whichever Apple deck the card draws, and the headline and the picture are therefore always the same subject. MacBook: SELL YOUR MACBOOK, selling points WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE / BATTERY OR SCREEN FAULTS FINE / SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME, items MacBook Air • Pro • M1 through M5, money UP TO $1,900 PAID TODAY under the stroke, CTA GET YOUR OFFER, sticker SAME DAY. iPad: SELL YOUR iPAD, items iPad Pro • mini • Air • Regular • with Pencil, money UP TO $850 PAID TODAY, and CRACKED GLASS STILL PAID as a selling point. On stepsFlow the headline takes the money word in line one — SELL YOUR MAC / IN 3 STEPS — because CASH IN / 3 STEPS names nothing. This record carries challenge:false.
variations: Three steps — stepsFlow, 1 / 2 / 3 in teal pen boxes on three highlighted rows, mac-pro-open-front hero
Review — reviewProof with five stars in the pen, the quote on the one sticky note, and a Lakewood reviewer line
iPad Pro — ipad-with-keyboard with SELL YOUR iPAD and CRACKED GLASS STILL PAID
Checklist — checklistHero with the single stroke on the CTA rather than the money line, ipad-with-pencil in the corner

Generic undatable iPads passed: ipad-angle-, ipad-back-, ipad-front-, ipad-mini-, ipad-pair-, ipad-stack- and ipad-with-stylus are all in neverShow, leaving only the two modern screen-off iPads. The 138-cutout leak is now zero across all 349 approved cutouts.
categories named macbook and ipad, which match no donor template: set to ['phones'], with Mac and iPad described as the deck rotation the engine performs at 2791.
ground:'paper' pinning: sheet:'paper:grid' on the record plus the line-2650 and groundNow changes named in groundSpec.

looks.name: Dotted Appraisal Note
looks.oneLine: A warm dot-grid page written in crimson with an Instrument Serif hand, a Cuban bracelet or the jeweller's scale laid on the paper, quiet as an appraisal.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:dots — #fbfaf5 warm stock with 2.2r #b3bbc7 dots on a 44px pitch from x=30,y=30, no rules, no margin rule, no punch holes, the same fibre noise and the same 70px binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:dots', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Record fields: key:'written-quote-dotted-appraisal-note', sheet:'paper:dots', challenge:false, plus the four collection-wide engine changes. The dots are neutral grey, which is why gold sits on this stock and not on the canary legal pad: warm white plus grey dots leaves the yellow metal the only warm thing in the frame, and the canary ban is only enforceable once sheet is pinned — until then line 2650 hands this look a canary sheet one card in five. PALETTE: lp10, which the picker calls Red Quote; its accent is #90043c, a deep crimson, and the record says both. NO 44px RHYTHM IS CLAIMED: the original recipe said the type was set on a 44px vertical rhythm, and the engine has no such pass — dot stock simply gets no snap, so the type keeps the template's own vertical spacing, and that is stated rather than dressed up. That absence is the reason reviewProof is safe here: with no snap, its rate pill, chips and quote text stay inside the bands they belong to. LAYOUT MATH: checklistHero gives one highlighter (the 760x194 CTA card) and three solid crimson tick discs; reviewProof gives four bands (660x92 rate pill, three 280x74 chips) and turns its 940x336 quote card into the one sticky note at 0.96 opacity, tilt plus or minus 1.2 degrees, shadow blur 22 offset 4/10. Strokes at 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle plus or minus 0.8, each with the 0.30 overrun twin 22px longer. Squares under 130px become solid pen boxes with white numerals. Pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f on everything else, assigned by headline order rather than the layer parity at 2691. Serif display only on CASH FOR GOLD and never on a wrapped line. THE SEAL IS GONE: trustSeal is out of this collection because it converts to six highlighter bands and because the circle branch at 2698 fills its seal disc solid with the pen, swallowing the seal words; the trust the theme wants comes from the five-star review card instead. PALE VS DEEP: lp10's c1 is #fdf0f1 and never reaches the paper, which is drawn; a deep palette would leave the page warm white and only deepen the pen.
looks.imagery: Jewellery, one piece or one coil at a time, laid on the page with a real cast shadow, lower right, clear of every line. I opened the heroes: gold-bracelet-cuban is a single gold Cuban-link bracelet; gold-chains-pile is one coiled curb chain; gold-necklace-single is a single looped gold necklace; gold-scale-weighing is a precision jeweller's balance with small gold pieces on the pan, which is the picture the copy's TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU is actually promising. The rest of the shelf follows: gold-bracelet-pair, gold-class-ring, gold-rings-scatter, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-scrap-mixed, gold-bars-stack. Watches are out of the imagery and out of the sub-deck: gold-watch-luxury and gold-pocket-watch are banned by prefix, because SUBCATS.gold[3] rewrites a card into WATCH BUYER / GOLD WATCHES and this collection carries no watch theme. Marks are the gold set in pen — gem, ringMark, chain, sparkle, coin — one or two, corners only, and always in th.accent and th.ink rather than a gold swatch, because the pen is the only colour on the card.
neverShow: more than one cutout layer on a card, or a cutout whose filename does not start with gold-
the gold-watches sub-deck (SUBCATS.gold key:watches), which rewrites the card into WATCH BUYER / GOLD WATCHES
canary legal stock: yellow metal on yellow paper reads as mud
more than one highlighter stroke on checklistHero; on reviewProof the rate pill and the three chips are highlighted rows and the quote card is the one sticky note
a product cutout over any line of type
a heavy display face on a long or wrapped line
handwriting faces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand, Shadows Into Light, Gloria Hallelujah, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Amatic SC, Cabin Sketch)
trustSeal, whose seal circle fills solid with the pen and whose panels give six bands

looks.copy: Quiet and exact — an appraisal written out, not a shout. Headline: CASH FOR GOLD, opener in ink and money word in the crimson pen. Selling points: TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU / WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE / ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY. Items, overriding CATEGORY_COPY.gold.items so the line stops leaning on watches this theme will not picture: 10k • 14k • 18k • Scrap & Dental • Cuban Links • Bangles • Tiffany • Yurman. Money under the highlighter: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE — checkable, and never a promise to beat an unnamed offer. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Sticker: FREE QUOTE. Badges are LICENSED · INSURED · PRIVATE, never INSURED alone, which is a car-buyer seal. Review copy sounds like the trade — spot rate, scrap weight, estate lots — and the reviewer line is a pin plus a first name, an initial and a city. This record carries challenge:false.

Scale hero — gold-scale-weighing beside TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, so the picture shows the promise
Chains hero — gold-chains-pile with the gold-chains sub-deck items: 10k • 14k • 18k • 22k • Cuban links • rope chains

Money under the highlighter: UP TO $15,000 CASH, and the spin-off decks change the money word as well as the number — WE BUY TRUCKS at $25,000, WE BUY WORK VANS at $20,000, WE BUY MOTORCYCLES at $12,000, never WE BUY CARS over a bike. Bike items string, overriding CATEGORY_COPY.bikes.items to drop a make that is not on the owner's list: Harley • Honda • Yamaha • Kawasaki • Dirt Bikes • Scooters. Brand line: WE BUY TOYOTAS with Camry • Corolla • Tacoma • RAV4 • 4Runner on the items line and the Toyota wordmark inked #14161c in the best free corner. This record carries challenge:false.

looks.name: Stamped Coin Sheet
looks.oneLine: A canary legal sheet in oxblood pen where the money word is struck in a stencil face at a hand-set tilt, with graded coins and Morgan dollars laid on the page.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:legal — #fff3b8, 2.2px #8fabd6 rules every 54px from y=130, a 2.2px #d97f7f margin rule at x=118, no punch holes, fibre noise, 70px binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:legal', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Record fields: key:'written-quote-stamped-coin-sheet', sheet:'paper:legal', challenge:false, plus the four collection-wide engine changes. PALETTE: lp02, which the picker calls Amber Offer; its accent is #920524, a deep oxblood, and the record says both. THE STAMP IS THE FACE, NOT A DRAWN BOX. The original recipe asked for a rotated stencil stamp inside a 4px hairline rule box at minus 8 to minus 14 degrees; nothing in the engine draws a rotated hairline box, and trustSeal — which was to carry it — is out of this collection because it converts to six highlighter bands and its seal circle fills solid with the pen at 2698. What the engine really does, and what this look uses instead: look.faces is honoured at 2769, so Big Shoulders Stencil Display sets the display face; familyTreatment gives every headline a hand-set tilt of plus or minus 1.2 degrees at 2691; and the money word takes the oxblood pen. That is a stamped word, drawn by code that exists. The stencil face appears on the money word and the sticker word only, never on more than two words, never on a curve, and every other line is Satoshi or Oswald. bandKnockout leads: its 1012x252 knockout band is caught as a money plate at 1047 and becomes the one highlighter at 0.55 opacity with the 0.30 overrun twin 22px longer, so the stamped word sits struck through a marker stroke. checklistHero is second and ships once the 54px snap carries its rows. Squares under 130px become solid #920524 pen boxes with white numerals. Pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f everywhere else, assigned by headline order rather than the layer parity at 2691. CHALLENGE MUST BE GATED: at 2818 the competitor swap fires on one card in three for every look, and CHALLENGE.coins names THE COIN SHOP, THE PAWN SHOP and THE MAIL-IN BUYERS — a third of this theme's cards would stop being stamped payout sheets. The record carries challenge:false and the engine line becomes const challenge = CH && pairOK && (sd % 3 === 0) && (look ? look.challenge === true : true). PALE VS DEEP: lp02's c1 is #fdf0ef and never reaches the canary.
looks.imagery: Coins on the page, one group at a time, with a real cast shadow, lower right, clear of the type. I opened the heroes. coin-graded-fan-three is a fan of slabbed coins with a real Washington quarter in the window and BLANK grading labels, which is exactly right: it reads as graded without carrying a fabricated PCGS or NGC wordmark. coin-silver-dollar-pair is two Morgan dollars with the 1898 date legible — the picture the MORGANS variation is talking about. coin-collection-tray is a full coin tray, the picture for whole collections and estates. coin-stack is stacks of quarters, junk silver by weight. The rest of the shelf follows: coin-slabs-stack, coin-slab, coin-rolls-paper, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-stack-silver, coin-coins-tube via coin-silver-dollar-pair's neighbours, and coin-album-pages for the estates line. coin-single-large is a hero only: the tile-wall MULTI filter names it explicitly, and this look has no wall anyway. The SLAB FRAME treatment stays off: the owner set that frame for Pokémon and sports cards only, slabFrame is now gated on look.ground === 'slab' at 3425, and this card's frame is the sheet. Marks are the coins set in pen — coin, ingot, medal, dollar, star5 — one or two, corners only.

more than one highlighter stroke on a card
the stencil face on more than two words, or on a curve
more than one stamped word on a card
