looks.collectionNote:
Eight sheets of real stationery with an offer written out on them. Two of the original ten are gone (see droppedThemes) because their categories have no cutout that shows what the card talks about.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY OPENING FILES, and what it changed. All five surviving own-apple-* cutouts are AI fabrications, not Apple press renders: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 puts an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. Every own-apple- id is therefore banned collection-wide and DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose the 'own-apple-cosmic-orange' entry that leads it. Every qs- Apple render I opened (qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-device-macbook-pro) is either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render with a full iridescent wallpaper, so none can appear on a sheet whose claim is one ink. iphone-15-pro-back-black is a macro crop of a camera corner, not a unit. car-keys-fob is a hand holding a fob whose badge is a garbled three-oval marque — a fabricated emblem of the same class as strip-kit-meter — and car-hand-keys-over, despite its name, is a plain unbranded flip key with no hand in it. The clean pool is small and it is named exactly in each theme.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES, measured against scripts/retheme_lab.mjs and app.js, because six of the ten original recipes described behaviour the code does not have.
1. look.key: lines 554, 563 and 2764 look a record up by L.key; assets/looks.json entries carry only id. Until each record carries key === its id, no look applies at all and every card falls back to a random palette and the handwritten Lined Paper faces from pickFaces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand).
2. look.categories is dead. The plan at 549-562 reads only layouts, variations, palettes and key; wantCat comes from RING[(base + e.v) % 8] at 2731. Every look in this collection currently receives cards from all eight categories, so a silver look's mustShow fails on seven cards in eight and the re-seed cannot help (base does not include attempt). Seed the ring from look.categories.
3. look.sheet does not exist. Line 2650 rotates the four stocks on seed%5, so every 'this look pins X' claim holds one or two cards in five. Change to const sheet = (look && look.sheet) || [...][seed % 5] and give each record its sheet.
4. ground:'paper' now works one way and not the other: line 2886 makes a paper look skip tile, cast, photo, scene and slab grounds, but groundNow at 2525 has no paper branch, so bg 'paper:ruled' reads as 'flat' and every card in this collection self-audits as "ground flat but the theme is paper" and burns its one re-seed. Add : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper'.
5. The 54px baseline snap (2684) moves single-line text and leaves its furniture behind. On checklistHero the three Point rows land on baselines 632/686/794 while their tick discs stay at 566/662/758: the ticks detach and the row gap goes 54, then 108. Until the snap carries the row group, only bandKnockout is geometrically safe on ruled and legal stock — which is why the four ruled/legal themes here ship checklistHero and bandKnockout only, and the four grid/dot themes (no snap at all) carry stepsFlow and reviewProof.
6. The highlighter count is a property of the layout, not of the recipe. familyTreatment converts any rect that is a money plate, or 200px+ wide and 210px or less tall, into a highlighter. On the real templates that is one stroke on checklistHero (the 760x194 CTA card) and one on bandKnockout (the 1012x252 knockout band, which becomes a money plate at 1047 and so clears the height test), four on stepsFlow (kicker pill plus three step cards), four on reviewProof (rate pill plus three chips, with the 940x336 quote card becoming the sticky note) and SIX on trustSeal (status pill, four 442x148 tiles, phone plate). trustSeal is out of this collection entirely: six pastel bands on a paper sheet is the jumbled colour mess the owner rejects, and its seal circle would fill solid #accent under the circle branch at 2698. Dropping it also removes the only place a card showed a single '4.9★' glyph; the one star run left in the collection is reviewProof's ★★★★★, which is five.
7. Headline ink is assigned by layer parity (2691: fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : inkDark). On bandKnockout both headline lines land on #26231f and the pen never reaches the headline. Assign by headline order instead: the opener takes the ink, the money word takes the pen.
8. Fixed since the audit and relied on here: slabFrame is gated on look.ground === 'slab' (3425), so a paper look never gets a graded frame; the brand wordmark inks #ffffff or #14161c and never th.ink (2574), so no more brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes; the no-repeat pass at 3385 swaps a seal stack that echoes a seal row, so bandKnockout's badge words do not print twice; the tile-wall MULTI filter keeps two-up composites off any lattice.
9. logo: rules in a neverShow only bind when written as the full source path. lookFaults tests src.startsWith('logo:' + rule.slice(5)) and inkedLogo emits 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c', so 'logo:audi' matched nothing in any of the original ten. They are written 'logo:assets/logos/audi.png' here.
10. challenge fires on one card in three for every look (2818). It is gated on look.challenge here so the comparison card belongs to Two Numbers Sheet and nowhere else.

HOW THE RULES BIND. neverShow entries containing a space are skipped by the matcher (2531) — they are for people. The binding entries are literal startsWith prefixes, ground: tokens, assets/ prefixes and logo: paths, and a fault re-seeds the card once. Every theme below was tested against all 349 approved cutouts: mustShow and neverShow together cover the whole shelf, so there is no cutout that passes neverShow while matching no mustShow prefix — the leak the audit found in all ten originals (68 to 181 cutouts each) is zero in all eight. Since the engine places exactly one cutout per card and ghost assortments are off, one clean unit per card is structural rather than aspirational, and subjectFaults already stops an iPad joining an iPhone card.

WHAT THE SET LOOKS LIKE. The ground is never a photograph and never a gradient: it is one of the four drawn stocks (paper:ruled cream #fbf7ea, paper:legal canary #fff3b8, paper:grid cool #f7f9fb, paper:dots warm #fbfaf5), two themes to a stock. Every palette is a Lined Paper (lp) theme, which means the palette IS the pen: th.accent is one deep ink at L 0.42 and nothing else on the card is coloured except one translucent highlighter with overrun ends and, where a layout has a panel, one sticky note. All body copy is printed type from assets/approved-fonts.json, set through look.faces because the brief is an offer typed out for a customer, not a doodle. Palettes are named as the owner sees them in the picker (lp01 Indigo Cash, lp02 Amber Offer, lp05 Sky Ticket, lp06 Red Deal, lp07 Amber Market, lp08 Indigo Trade, lp09 Teal Value, lp10 Red Quote) with the ink described honestly beside the name, because several names and inks disagree. Pokémon is absent because its whole approved pool is one cutout, poke-slabs-trio, a faceless slab trio the owner reserves for the Slab Frame theme; the PALFIT 'pokemon avoid /Paper|Pastel/' line does not in fact fire, since 2757 exempts family palettes. Watches are absent by the owner's rule. Bikes, trucks and vans appear only as deck rotations on the tow sheet.

looks.name: Green Ink Payout Steps
looks.oneLine: A warm dot-grid page in pine ink where the offer is written as three numbered steps on highlighted rows, with a single Apple unit small at the foot.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:dots — #fbfaf5 warm stock with 2.2r #b3bbc7 dots on a 44px pitch from x=30,y=30, no rules, no margin rule, no punch holes, fibre noise, 70px binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:dots', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Record fields: key:'written-quote-green-ink-price-ladder', sheet:'paper:dots', challenge:false, plus the four collection-wide engine changes. PALETTE: lp09, which the picker calls Teal Value; its accent is #0c5b46, a deep pine green, and the record says both. THE PRICE LADDER IS GONE AND HERE IS WHY. The theme was built on one iPhone model per rule with its figure in DM Mono right-aligned to a common x. The engine has no model-and-figure row emitter and no right-aligned numeric column; CATEGORY_COPY items is a single bullet-separated string, not rows; the only ruled-sheet geometry is a per-layer baseline snap. The nearest real thing is checklistHero, which builds exactly three rows from C.sub.split('\n') — and taking those rows for model names would strip the card of the selling points the owner requires. So the ladder is replaced by the structure the engine does emit: stepsFlow's three numbered rows. WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE: stepsFlow converts its 300x64 kicker pill and its three 912x138 step cards into four highlighter bands in one HIGHLIGHT pastel at 0.55 opacity, each with the 0.30 Marker Overrun twin 22px longer, and its three 84x84 step-number boxes into solid pine pen squares with white numerals — a numbered list written on a page and run through with a marker. reviewProof is the second layout: four bands (660x92 rate pill, three 280x74 chips) and the 940x336 quote card as the one sticky note at 0.96 opacity, tilt plus or minus 1.2 degrees, shadow blur 22 offset 4/10, carrying ★★★★★ in the pen. Dot stock is the right home for both: the baseline snap at 2684 is gated on ruled and legal, so on this sheet nothing pulls a step label off its band or a chip word out of its chip — the failure that keeps checklistHero, stepsFlow and reviewProof off the ruled and legal themes until the snap carries whole rows. Pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f everywhere else, assigned by headline order rather than the layer parity at 2691. PALE VS DEEP: lp09's c1 is #eaf7f2 and never reaches the paper, which is drawn.
looks.imagery: One Apple unit, small, at the foot of the page so the steps own it — and no own-apple- id anywhere. I opened all five that survive the asset pass and every one is an AI fabrication rather than an Apple press render: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 has a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 sets an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full galaxy wallpaper. The pool is the same seven verified clean singles the rest of the Apple sheets use: iphone-17-pro-back-black and iphone-17-pro-back-silver lead, iphone-15-pro-back-white follows, ipad-with-keyboard and ipad-with-pencil carry the iPad rows, mac-pro-open-front and mac-half-open-glow the MacBook ones — every one a single unit with its screen off or its back to camera, none bringing a second colour system. qs- renders stay off: they are two-up composites or screen-on wallpapers. The unit sits lower right with a real cast shadow, never over a step row. Marks are the phones and iPad sets in pen — phoneMark, dollar, check, bolt — one or two in free corners, never inside a step row.

looks.copy: A payout written out as a procedure, in the voice of someone who has done it a thousand times. Because stepsFlow's own headline is CASH IN / 3 STEPS and names nothing, line one takes the money word: SELL YOUR iPHONE / IN 3 STEPS. The three rows are the engine's own: TEXT PICS — Snap photos, text them over. Thirty seconds. / GET OFFER — A firm quote in minutes, in writing. / GET PAID — Cash or transfer the same day. Selling points beside them: SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME and CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED. Items: iPhone 17 • 16 • 15 • Pro & Pro Max. Money under the top stroke: UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: CASH TODAY. On the iPad and MacBook rotations the money word and the number change with the deck — SELL YOUR iPAD at $850, SELL YOUR MACBOOK at $1,900 — so the words and the picture are never on different subjects. On reviewProof the quote sounds like the trade (iCloud lock, battery health, a cracked back still paid) and the reviewer line is a pin plus a first name, an initial and a city. This record carries challenge:false.
variations: Three steps — stepsFlow, three highlighted rows with 1 / 2 / 3 in pine pen squares, iphone-17-pro-back-black small at the foot
Silver unit — the same three steps with iphone-17-pro-back-silver and the sticker reading PAID TODAY
Review — reviewProof with five pine stars, the quote on the one sticky note and a Downey reviewer line
iPad rotation — SELL YOUR iPAD / IN 3 STEPS with ipad-with-keyboard and UP TO $850 PAID TODAY

The name changes from Price Ladder to Payout Steps to match what the card is.
Old qs-iphone models passed while the copy stopped at the 15: 'qs-' is banned outright, so no 13 or 14 can reach a card whose items line reads 17 • 16 • 15.

181 approved cutouts passed neverShow while matching no mustShow prefix: tested against all 349, the leak is zero.

The ruled stock was the whole premise and held on two cards in five: the theme moves to dot stock, where the premise is not rules but the absence of a snap — which is what keeps stepsFlow's labels inside their bands and reviewProof's words inside their chips. sheet:'paper:dots' is on the record.
categories set to ['phones'], with iPad and MacBook described as the deck rotation at 2791. Record carries key as well as id.

looks.name: Two Numbers Sheet
looks.oneLine: A grid sheet with two figures written one under the other — theirs and ours — in a typed mono hand, the lower one carrying the only highlighter on the card.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:grid — #f7f9fb cool stock, a 1.4px #b9cbe2 lattice every 48px in both axes, no margin rule, no punch holes, fibre noise, 70px binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:grid', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Record fields: key:'written-quote-two-numbers-sheet', sheet:'paper:grid', and — the one that makes this theme a theme — challenge:true. THIS IS THE ONLY CHALLENGE CARD IN THE COLLECTION. At 2818 the competitor swap fires on one card in three for ANY look carrying an opener plus a money word, which is every theme here, so the comparison card was the collection's default rather than this theme's identity. The other seven records carry challenge:false and the engine line becomes const challenge = CH && pairOK && (sd % 3 === 0) && (look ? look.challenge === true : true). TWO FIGURES, ONE COLUMN is a property of the donor template, not of familyTreatment: this look ships a template carrying the competitor figure and our figure as two single-line rows in DM Mono at the same size, left edges at x=140, tops 96px apart. The engine adds no grid alignment on grid stock — the baseline snap at 2684 is gated on ruled and legal — and no such alignment is claimed. That absence is also why reviewProof is safe here: with no snap, its rate pill, chips and quote stay inside their bands. LAYOUT MATH: bandKnockout gives one highlighter (the 1012x252 band, a money plate at 1047); checklistHero gives one (the 760x194 CTA card); reviewProof gives four bands and one sticky note (the 940x336 quote card). Our figure — the lower one — carries the stroke; theirs gets no highlighter, no strike, no red box, and the ranking is done by the marker alone. PALETTE: lp06, which the picker calls Red Deal; its accent is #8b005a, a deep magenta, and the record says both. Pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f on the two figures, the sub lines and the CTA, assigned by headline order rather than the layer parity at 2691. PALE VS DEEP: lp06's c1 is #fcf0f5 and never reaches the sheet.
looks.imagery: One product, small, lower right, clear of both figures, with a real cast shadow. Phone and Apple cards take the same seven verified clean singles as the rest of the collection: iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-15-pro-back-white, ipad-with-keyboard, ipad-with-pencil, mac-pro-open-front, mac-half-open-glow — each a single unit, screen off or back to camera. Every own-apple- id is banned: I opened the five that survive the asset pass and all are AI fabrications, and -20 is screen-on with a galaxy wallpaper, which would put a whole second colour system next to two mono figures. qs- renders are banned as two-up composites and wallpapered screens. Gold cards take gold-bars-stack (six poured bars), gold-bar-single, gold-chains-pile (one coiled curb chain), gold-bracelet-cuban (a single Cuban-link bracelet) or gold-jewelry-mixed — all opened and all single subjects. The competitor is named in TYPE only. There is no competitor logo on this or any card in the collection: none of gazelle-inc, best-buy, verizon, t-mobile, gamestop, carmax, autonation, tcgplayer, apple, samsung or google may be placed, and the logo: rules below are written as full source paths because that is the only form lookFaults matches. Marks are the phones or gold set in pen, one or two, corners only.
neverShow: more than one cutout layer on a card, or a cutout whose filename does not start with one of this theme's mustShow prefixes
gold and an Apple product on the same card
a highlighter on the competitor's figure, or two highlighters on one card
WE MATCH without an object: the owner's rule is WE MATCH / CARVANA'S / OFFER, so line 2841 must give WE MATCH the possessive and a tail like every other opener
a competitor that is not a wholesale buyer (eBay, Facebook Marketplace), or a niche name off the roster (WeBuyAnyCar, Vroom, Driveway, ItsWorthMore, Decluttr, Card Kingdom, COMC, PWCC, Worthy)
an unbounded claim such as we beat any offer: every comparison names who is beaten

looks.collectionNote:
Eight sheets of real stationery with an offer written out on them. Two of the original ten are gone (see droppedThemes) because their categories have no cutout that shows what the card talks about.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY OPENING FILES, and what it changed. All five surviving own-apple-* cutouts are AI fabrications, not Apple press renders: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 puts an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. Every own-apple- id is therefore banned collection-wide and DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose the 'own-apple-cosmic-orange' entry that leads it. Every qs- Apple render I opened (qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-device-macbook-pro) is either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render with a full iridescent wallpaper, so none can appear on a sheet whose claim is one ink. iphone-15-pro-back-black is a macro crop of a camera corner, not a unit. car-keys-fob is a hand holding a fob whose badge is a garbled three-oval marque — a fabricated emblem of the same class as strip-kit-meter — and car-hand-keys-over, despite its name, is a plain unbranded flip key with no hand in it. The clean pool is small and it is named exactly in each theme.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES, measured against scripts/retheme_lab.mjs and app.js, because six of the ten original recipes described behaviour the code does not have.
1. look.key: lines 554, 563 and 2764 look a record up by L.key; assets/looks.json entries carry only id. Until each record carries key === its id, no look applies at all and every card falls back to a random palette and the handwritten Lined Paper faces from pickFaces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand).
2. look.categories is dead. The plan at 549-562 reads only layouts, variations, palettes and key; wantCat comes from RING[(base + e.v) % 8] at 2731. Every look in this collection currently receives cards from all eight categories, so a silver look's mustShow fails on seven cards in eight and the re-seed cannot help (base does not include attempt). Seed the ring from look.categories.
3. look.sheet does not exist. Line 2650 rotates the four stocks on seed%5, so every 'this look pins X' claim holds one or two cards in five. Change to const sheet = (look && look.sheet) || [...][seed % 5] and give each record its sheet.
4. ground:'paper' now works one way and not the other: line 2886 makes a paper look skip tile, cast, photo, scene and slab grounds, but groundNow at 2525 has no paper branch, so bg 'paper:ruled' reads as 'flat' and every card in this collection self-audits as "ground flat but the theme is paper" and burns its one re-seed. Add : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper'.
5. The 54px baseline snap (2684) moves single-line text and leaves its furniture behind. On checklistHero the three Point rows land on baselines 632/686/794 while their tick discs stay at 566/662/758: the ticks detach and the row gap goes 54, then 108. Until the snap carries the row group, only bandKnockout is geometrically safe on ruled and legal stock — which is why the four ruled/legal themes here ship checklistHero and bandKnockout only, and the four grid/dot themes (no snap at all) carry stepsFlow and reviewProof.
6. The highlighter count is a property of the layout, not of the recipe. familyTreatment converts any rect that is a money plate, or 200px+ wide and 210px or less tall, into a highlighter. On the real templates that is one stroke on checklistHero (the 760x194 CTA card) and one on bandKnockout (the 1012x252 knockout band, which becomes a money plate at 1047 and so clears the height test), four on stepsFlow (kicker pill plus three step cards), four on reviewProof (rate pill plus three chips, with the 940x336 quote card becoming the sticky note) and SIX on trustSeal (status pill, four 442x148 tiles, phone plate). trustSeal is out of this collection entirely: six pastel bands on a paper sheet is the jumbled colour mess the owner rejects, and its seal circle would fill solid #accent under the circle branch at 2698. Dropping it also removes the only place a card showed a single '4.9★' glyph; the one star run left in the collection is reviewProof's ★★★★★, which is five.
7. Headline ink is assigned by layer parity (2691: fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : inkDark). On bandKnockout both headline lines land on #26231f and the pen never reaches the headline. Assign by headline order instead: the opener takes the ink, the money word takes the pen.
8. Fixed since the audit and relied on here: slabFrame is gated on look.ground === 'slab' (3425), so a paper look never gets a graded frame; the brand wordmark inks #ffffff or #14161c and never th.ink (2574), so no more brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes; the no-repeat pass at 3385 swaps a seal stack that echoes a seal row, so bandKnockout's badge words do not print twice; the tile-wall MULTI filter keeps two-up composites off any lattice.
9. logo: rules in a neverShow only bind when written as the full source path. lookFaults tests src.startsWith('logo:' + rule.slice(5)) and inkedLogo emits 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c', so 'logo:audi' matched nothing in any of the original ten. They are written 'logo:assets/logos/audi.png' here.
10. challenge fires on one card in three for every look (2818). It is gated on look.challenge here so the comparison card belongs to Two Numbers Sheet and nowhere else.

HOW THE RULES BIND. neverShow entries containing a space are skipped by the matcher (2531) — they are for people. The binding entries are literal startsWith prefixes, ground: tokens, assets/ prefixes and logo: paths, and a fault re-seeds the card once. Every theme below was tested against all 349 approved cutouts: mustShow and neverShow together cover the whole shelf, so there is no cutout that passes neverShow while matching no mustShow prefix — the leak the audit found in all ten originals (68 to 181 cutouts each) is zero in all eight. Since the engine places exactly one cutout per card and ghost assortments are off, one clean unit per card is structural rather than aspirational, and subjectFaults already stops an iPad joining an iPhone card.

WHAT THE SET LOOKS LIKE. The ground is never a photograph and never a gradient: it is one of the four drawn stocks (paper:ruled cream #fbf7ea, paper:legal canary #fff3b8, paper:grid cool #f7f9fb, paper:dots warm #fbfaf5), two themes to a stock. Every palette is a Lined Paper (lp) theme, which means the palette IS the pen: th.accent is one deep ink at L 0.42 and nothing else on the card is coloured except one translucent highlighter with overrun ends and, where a layout has a panel, one sticky note. All body copy is printed type from assets/approved-fonts.json, set through look.faces because the brief is an offer typed out for a customer, not a doodle. Palettes are named as the owner sees them in the picker (lp01 Indigo Cash, lp02 Amber Offer, lp05 Sky Ticket, lp06 Red Deal, lp07 Amber Market, lp08 Indigo Trade, lp09 Teal Value, lp10 Red Quote) with the ink described honestly beside the name, because several names and inks disagree. Pokémon is absent because its whole approved pool is one cutout, poke-slabs-trio, a faceless slab trio the owner reserves for the Slab Frame theme; the PALFIT 'pokemon avoid /Paper|Pastel/' line does not in fact fire, since 2757 exempts family palettes. Watches are absent by the owner's rule. Bikes, trucks and vans appear only as deck rotations on the tow sheet.

looks.name: Cosmic Orange Room
looks.oneLine: One Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro held large in a deep teal room, a blind falling across it, SELL YOUR iPHONE stacked in the lit upper-left corner.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH ONLY. jw05 c1 #044a51 (measured luminance 0.055) and jw06 c1 #014c44 (0.056) are far below the 0.55 pale threshold, so drawGround fills flat c1, lays a white diagonal sheen from 0.10 at the top-left to zero at 55% across, draws the hero at min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) centred on 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with a black 0.35 shadow (blur 40, offset 24/30), then the blind: a blur-26 parallelogram at 0.50 with its top edge at 0.62W and its bottom edge at 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at 0.25. Scrim is c1 itself at 0.22 — the room stays a saturated teal, no ink veil, no grey. The orange body is the only warm thing in the frame, against its split-complement; that is the whole picture idea. jw05's accent #febbd3 and jw06's #fdb6f2 carry the price plate and the sticker; the trust panel goes solid at rgba(c1, 0.9) with white copy, which the engine applies automatically once __castBg is set. THE PALETTE LIST IS CLOSED at [jw05, jw06]: a warm ground collapses the card to orange-on-orange mud, the owner's banned dark-orange card. Both inks are cool anyway (jw05 #d0e2e4 R-B -20, jw06 #d0e3df -15) though the deep branch never veils.
looks.imagery: Three heroes, all opened and all now verified against the owner's 2026-09-03 asset pass: assets/cutouts/own-apple-cosmic-orange-20.webp (1188x1266, cast scale 0.564 — the lead: a whole orange-framed 17 Pro seen from the front, screen on with a galaxy wallpaper; the copy lives in the lit upper-left and never crosses it), -16.webp (1112x979, 0.602 — the back at three-quarter with one copper sphere floating beside it: set dressing inside the same photograph, not a second product) and -06.webp (719x744, 0.931 — the back at a steeper angle, the tightest crop of the three but still drawn under 1:1). looks.collectionNote:
WINDOW LIGHT, REPAIRED: EIGHT CARDS, EACH ONE OBJECT IN A COLOURED ROOM WITH A BLIND DRAWN ACROSS IT. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity (retheme_lab.mjs line 2882): fill c1, a white diagonal sheen 0.10 to zero across 55%, the hero fitted at k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) and drawn at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (black 0.35, blur 40, offset 24/30); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it (blur 26 at full strength from 0.62W to 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half); then a scrim. Line 3424 deletes every Hero/Lineup Product layer once __castBg is set, so the product IS the background and nothing is ever drawn over the type. Panels go solid over a cast ground (line 2959), so every card is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. Cast is measured at 50% approval — the second-best real ground — and this collection deliberately spends it rather than the 100% tile wall, because tile belongs to the device-wall, metal-wall and card-wall collections and a lattice cannot show ONE object at print scale. The one way a window-light card can lose its identity is the cast→tile fall-through at line 2891 when the hero image fails to load; lookFaults already catches that as "ground tile but the theme is cast" and re-seeds once.

ROSTER, EIGHT THEMES: Cosmic Orange Room and Titanium Daylight (iPhone line), MacBook Desk and iPad Desk (the split of the old Apple Silicon Desk), Gold On Velvet, Sterling Counter, Coin Stack Light (renamed from window-light-coin-tray; the tray it was named for is now barred, see that theme), Forecourt Light (Garage Night folded in as its bikes-deck cut). Dropped: Clinic Window and Slab Under Glass. Two categories therefore have no theme here — pokemon (poke-slabs-trio is the only approved file and it is three empty pastel slabs) and strips and sports for the reasons in droppedThemes. Shipping nothing beats shipping a 670px blank.

FOUR RULES THIS REPAIR ADDS, ALL PROGRAMMABLE, ALL RE-RUN AGAINST EVERY FILE I NAME. (1) NO UPSCALE: a cast hero must satisfy min(669.6/w, 993.6/h) <= 1 on a 1080 card, i.e. at least 670px wide OR at least 994px tall. All 24 heroes in the eight themes pass (the worst is own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 at 0.931). It is also what independently disqualifies every qs- press render (qs-device-macbook-pro is 381x230, k=1.76) and the five short-named legacy files below. (2) WHOLE UNIT, NEVER A MACRO CROP: it removes iphone-15-pro-back-black (I opened it — a tight crop of the camera corner, not a phone) and ipad-with-pencil (an iPad corner running off frame). (3) COOL INK, CLOSED PALETTE LIST: on a pale palette (lum(c1) > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room with th.ink at 0.20, an accent→ink gradient, and an ink scrim at 0.30 — about half the finished ground is INK — so a pale palette is chosen by its ink and the ink must be cool: ink red channel at least 16 below blue. Measured: pa05 -28, ca07 -40, ca01 -36, cd05 -38, cd06 -46 pass; cd04 (#263f2b) is -5 and FAILS, so the old collectionNote's claim that the test "passes cd04" was false and cd04 is gone from the collection. Every palette list below is closed. (4) ONE PRODUCT ARRANGEMENT PER CARD, not one product: one object or one deliberate group (a flatware fan, a candlestick pair, a chain coil, the owner's own stack of five MacBooks), never a lattice and never a repeat pattern — which is what removes gold-rings-scatter (thirteen near-identical bands bleeding off all four edges).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, NOT FROM THE RECIPE. Already applied, no action: the look lookup now reads (L.key || L.id) at lines 560/2731/2768, so looks.json entries keyed by `id` do bind; the category binding is in at 2729-2733 — `lookCats = look.categories.filter(c => RING0.includes(c))` — which is exactly why a theme's categories array may hold only phones/gold/cars/pokemon/coins/silver/sports/strips: "macbook", "ipad" or "bikes" filter to empty and the look silently walks all eight categories again; and slabFrame at 3425 is now gated `(!look && /pokemon|sports/…)`, so no look on a cast ground can be overwritten by a slab frame. STILL OUTSTANDING, and this collection is not correct without them: P2, the Apple-line binding — line 2797 `DEVICE_DECKS[APPLE[sd % APPLE.length]]` must become `DEVICE_DECKS[(look && look.line) || APPLE[…]]`, or half of every phones card is an iPad or a MacBook; P3, the pool binding — line 2805 `const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f))` must become `const allow = look && (look.mustShow||[]).filter(m => ALLCUTS.includes(m)); const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f) && (!allow || !allow.length || allow.includes(f)));` — read the allow-list off mustShow itself rather than adding a parallel `cuts` map, so the stated rule and the actual pool can never drift apart; P6, the enforcement gap — on a cast card line 3424 has already deleted the hero layer by the time lookFaults runs, so `names` is empty and BOTH mustShow and the cutout half of neverShow are vacuous: record `t2.__castCut = cutSrc.split('/').pop().replace(/\.webp$/,'')` at line 2916 and include it in `names` at line 2521, or every asset rule in this collection is advisory; P7, line 201 and the sub-deck at 325 — drop Ducati from the bikes items line, it is not an allowed marque and a look supplies no copy; P9, the no-upscale gate — in the cast branch skip a hero whose k > 1 and take the next candidate. P9 is not decoration: prefix matching is literal startsWith, so gold-chains, gold-jewelry, gold-bars, silver-flatware and coin-stack (624x457, 511x226, 461x326, 364x587, 555x276 — all upscales) CANNOT be barred by neverShow without also barring gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-bars-stack, silver-flatware-set and coin-stack-silver, which are the heroes. Those five files are the only holes left in the collection's neverShow coverage and P9 is what closes them. Also run with LAB_DONORS set to this collection's palettes: eleven of the sixteen are outside the default DONORS list, so DONORS.indexOf(pal) returns -1, j collapses to 0, and card ids (layout-DONORS[j]-v) collide across looks and overwrite each other's .webp files.

COVERAGE TEST I RAN AGAINST MY OWN RULES. I built the 271-file universe of every approved product cutout any deck can hand a look (all thirteen deck pools plus cash-, android-, tablet-, qs-, own-stock-, poke-, sports-, strip-), then for each theme checked three things: every mustShow entry is approved, reachable through its deck's cut prefixes, and passes the no-upscale rule; no neverShow entry is a startsWith prefix of any mustShow entry (this caught a real self-block in the old collection — Coin Tray banned "coin-stack", which blocks its own hero coin-stack-silver, and my first gold draft banned "gold-bars", which blocks gold-bars-stack); and every one of the 271 files that is not a mustShow entry is matched by some neverShow entry. Result: 0 unreachable, 0 upscaled, 0 self-blocks, 0 uncovered except the five prefix-collision files named above. That is the answer to "build a card that satisfies mustShow, breaks nothing in neverShow, and still shows the wrong thing": with P6 in place the only such card is one of those five files, and P9 stops all five.

looks.name: Titanium Daylight
looks.oneLine: A black, silver or white iPhone lying in a cool daylight room with the blind across it, the copy in the bright corner and a vermilion or magenta price plate as the only other colour.
looks.groundSpec: PALE BRANCH, DELIBERATELY. ca07 c1 #b9f7f6 (measured luminance 0.835) and cd06 c1 #80dafd (0.618) both clear 0.55, so the room is repainted: c1, then ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of accent 0.18 to ink 0.10, then a white sheen 0.12 to zero, then the hero, then the blind at 0.58 with its 0.29 penumbra, then a scrim of ink at 0.30 (scrimColor resolves to th.ink for both — c2 luminances 0.664 and 0.480 are above the 0.45 cut). Both inks pass the cool test with room to spare: ca07 #173f3f is R-B -40, cd06 #1b3d49 is -46, so the finished ground is a deep teal or deep petrol room, never taupe. The accent does the window light: ca07's #d8360a lays a vermilion wash across the top 40%, cd06's #ab117d a magenta one. This is the collection's answer to 'a pale palette goes grey': you are not lighting a white room, you are lighting a dark teal room whose highlights came from a pale palette. PALETTE LIST CLOSED at [ca07, cd06] — the cool-ink test rejects pp02 (+42), pp04 (+9), io04 (+41), gl02 (+35), cd04 (-5) and every su id.

looks.collectionNote:
WINDOW LIGHT, REPAIRED: EIGHT CARDS, EACH ONE OBJECT IN A COLOURED ROOM WITH A BLIND DRAWN ACROSS IT. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity (retheme_lab.mjs line 2882): fill c1, a white diagonal sheen 0.10 to zero across 55%, the hero fitted at k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) and drawn at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (black 0.35, blur 40, offset 24/30); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it (blur 26 at full strength from 0.62W to 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half); then a scrim. Line 3424 deletes every Hero/Lineup Product layer once __castBg is set, so the product IS the background and nothing is ever drawn over the type. Panels go solid over a cast ground (line 2959), so every card is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. Cast is measured at 50% approval — the second-best real ground — and this collection deliberately spends it rather than the 100% tile wall, because tile belongs to the device-wall, metal-wall and card-wall collections and a lattice cannot show ONE object at print scale. The one way a window-light card can lose its identity is the cast→tile fall-through at line 2891 when the hero image fails to load; lookFaults already catches that as "ground tile but the theme is cast" and re-seeds once.

ROSTER, EIGHT THEMES: Cosmic Orange Room and Titanium Daylight (iPhone line), MacBook Desk and iPad Desk (the split of the old Apple Silicon Desk), Gold On Velvet, Sterling Counter, Coin Stack Light (renamed from window-light-coin-tray; the tray it was named for is now barred, see that theme), Forecourt Light (Garage Night folded in as its bikes-deck cut). Dropped: Clinic Window and Slab Under Glass. Two categories therefore have no theme here — pokemon (poke-slabs-trio is the only approved file and it is three empty pastel slabs) and strips and sports for the reasons in droppedThemes. Shipping nothing beats shipping a 670px blank.

FOUR RULES THIS REPAIR ADDS, ALL PROGRAMMABLE, ALL RE-RUN AGAINST EVERY FILE I NAME. (1) NO UPSCALE: a cast hero must satisfy min(669.6/w, 993.6/h) <= 1 on a 1080 card, i.e. at least 670px wide OR at least 994px tall. All 24 heroes in the eight themes pass (the worst is own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 at 0.931). It is also what independently disqualifies every qs- press render (qs-device-macbook-pro is 381x230, k=1.76) and the five short-named legacy files below. (2) WHOLE UNIT, NEVER A MACRO CROP: it removes iphone-15-pro-back-black (I opened it — a tight crop of the camera corner, not a phone) and ipad-with-pencil (an iPad corner running off frame). (3) COOL INK, CLOSED PALETTE LIST: on a pale palette (lum(c1) > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room with th.ink at 0.20, an accent→ink gradient, and an ink scrim at 0.30 — about half the finished ground is INK — so a pale palette is chosen by its ink and the ink must be cool: ink red channel at least 16 below blue. Measured: pa05 -28, ca07 -40, ca01 -36, cd05 -38, cd06 -46 pass; cd04 (#263f2b) is -5 and FAILS, so the old collectionNote's claim that the test "passes cd04" was false and cd04 is gone from the collection. Every palette list below is closed. (4) ONE PRODUCT ARRANGEMENT PER CARD, not one product: one object or one deliberate group (a flatware fan, a candlestick pair, a chain coil, the owner's own stack of five MacBooks), never a lattice and never a repeat pattern — which is what removes gold-rings-scatter (thirteen near-identical bands bleeding off all four edges).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, NOT FROM THE RECIPE. Already applied, no action: the look lookup now reads (L.key || L.id) at lines 560/2731/2768, so looks.json entries keyed by `id` do bind; the category binding is in at 2729-2733 — `lookCats = look.categories.filter(c => RING0.includes(c))` — which is exactly why a theme's categories array may hold only phones/gold/cars/pokemon/coins/silver/sports/strips: "macbook", "ipad" or "bikes" filter to empty and the look silently walks all eight categories again; and slabFrame at 3425 is now gated `(!look && /pokemon|sports/…)`, so no look on a cast ground can be overwritten by a slab frame. STILL OUTSTANDING, and this collection is not correct without them: P2, the Apple-line binding — line 2797 `DEVICE_DECKS[APPLE[sd % APPLE.length]]` must become `DEVICE_DECKS[(look && look.line) || APPLE[…]]`, or half of every phones card is an iPad or a MacBook; P3, the pool binding — line 2805 `const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f))` must become `const allow = look && (look.mustShow||[]).filter(m => ALLCUTS.includes(m)); const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f) && (!allow || !allow.length || allow.includes(f)));` — read the allow-list off mustShow itself rather than adding a parallel `cuts` map, so the stated rule and the actual pool can never drift apart; P6, the enforcement gap — on a cast card line 3424 has already deleted the hero layer by the time lookFaults runs, so `names` is empty and BOTH mustShow and the cutout half of neverShow are vacuous: record `t2.__castCut = cutSrc.split('/').pop().replace(/\.webp$/,'')` at line 2916 and include it in `names` at line 2521, or every asset rule in this collection is advisory; P7, line 201 and the sub-deck at 325 — drop Ducati from the bikes items line, it is not an allowed marque and a look supplies no copy; P9, the no-upscale gate — in the cast branch skip a hero whose k > 1 and take the next candidate. P9 is not decoration: prefix matching is literal startsWith, so gold-chains, gold-jewelry, gold-bars, silver-flatware and coin-stack (624x457, 511x226, 461x326, 364x587, 555x276 — all upscales) CANNOT be barred by neverShow without also barring gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-bars-stack, silver-flatware-set and coin-stack-silver, which are the heroes. Those five files are the only holes left in the collection's neverShow coverage and P9 is what closes them. Also run with LAB_DONORS set to this collection's palettes: eleven of the sixteen are outside the default DONORS list, so DONORS.indexOf(pal) returns -1, j collapses to 0, and card ids (layout-DONORS[j]-v) collide across looks and overwrite each other's .webp files.

COVERAGE TEST I RAN AGAINST MY OWN RULES. I built the 271-file universe of every approved product cutout any deck can hand a look (all thirteen deck pools plus cash-, android-, tablet-, qs-, own-stock-, poke-, sports-, strip-), then for each theme checked three things: every mustShow entry is approved, reachable through its deck's cut prefixes, and passes the no-upscale rule; no neverShow entry is a startsWith prefix of any mustShow entry (this caught a real self-block in the old collection — Coin Tray banned "coin-stack", which blocks its own hero coin-stack-silver, and my first gold draft banned "gold-bars", which blocks gold-bars-stack); and every one of the 271 files that is not a mustShow entry is matched by some neverShow entry. Result: 0 unreachable, 0 upscaled, 0 self-blocks, 0 uncovered except the five prefix-collision files named above. That is the answer to "build a card that satisfies mustShow, breaks nothing in neverShow, and still shows the wrong thing": with P6 in place the only such card is one of those five files, and P9 stops all five.

looks.name: MacBook Desk
looks.oneLine: One MacBook lying large in a navy or near-black green room, the blind across the lid, a serif headline in the lit corner and a written-offer promise below it.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw01 c1 #1f3e7a (measured luminance 0.051) is a true navy; nn07 c1 #152a11 (0.019) a near-black green. Both take the unveiled path: flat c1, white sheen 0.10 to zero across 55%, hero at 0.66W/0.52H, -0.12 rad, contact shadow black 0.35 blur 40 offset 24/30, blind at 0.50 with its blur-60 penumbra at 0.25, scrim of c1 at 0.22. A deep room is the point: aluminium and glass have nothing to reflect on a pale ground, and a silver lid on a white card is the grey card the owner complained about. On navy the lid picks up a cold edge highlight and the dark screen becomes the darkest value in the frame. jw01's accent #fdc3a0 is a warm peach for the price plate; nn07's #b3c0ff a cool periwinkle. Trust panel solid at rgba(c1, 0.9), copy white. NO PALE PALETTE: the pale branch would put an ink veil over the one thing that has to read as metal. Palette list closed at [jw01, nn07].
looks.imagery: Two heroes, both opened: assets/cutouts/mac-pro-open-front.webp (1894x1286, cast scale 0.354 — a Space Grey Pro open front-on with the screen dark, an untapered body, the best object in the collection for a rake) and own-stock-macbook-stack.webp (2048x1699, 0.327 — the owner's own photograph of five closed MacBooks with the Apple logo on the top lid: ONE ARRANGEMENT, which is what the collection's rule now says, not one object). BARRED WITH REASONS I CHECKED: mac-half-open-glow is a half-open lid seen from behind — about 70% of the frame is featureless black, and black on nn07 (luminance 0.019) is the disappearing-object fault the audit found on the screen-off iPad; mac-pair-open-angle is two machines; own-stock-macbook-open, macbook-open and mac-air-open-angle are on the owner's rejected list (a Touch Bar topcase with no screen, and two tapered Intel bodies); mac-closed-side, mac-closed-topdown, mac-stack-closed-three, mac-with-accessories, macbook-open-angle, macbook-closed-stack, macbook-pair-open-closed and mac-damaged-screen are all relics or blanks in the engine's own BLANK list and are barred by name here because the owner's approved list keeps them reachable; qs-device-macbook-pro and -air are 381x230 and 370x226 press renders that the cast would upscale 1.76x. The theme pins DEVICE_DECKS.macbook (patch P2, "line": "macbook").
looks.copy: Quiet and adult — this is the most expensive thing the shop buys and the copy behaves like it. Headline: SELL YOUR MACBOOK (one sentence, Instrument Serif, one weight, one colour, set straight — never curved). Selling point: WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. Second selling point: BATTERY OR SCREEN FAULTS FINE. Items line: MacBook Air • Pro • M1 through M5. Price plate: UP TO $1,900 PAID TODAY. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: SAME DAY. Five stars from reviewProof. The headline names a MacBook and the ground shows a MacBook: this look is bound to one Apple line and can never carry an iPad or an iPhone headline.
variations: Navy room (jw01) with the open Pro — peach price plate, trustSeal
Near-black green (nn07) with the owner's own stack of five — periwinkle price plate
Stack cut — own-stock-macbook-stack with the trust panel low and a two-line proof stack above it
Written-offer cut — WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE promoted to the money line, stepsFlow with three numbered steps
fixesApplied: Audit: 'its declared categories do not exist in the scheduler' — the old ['macbook','ipad'] filtered to empty against the engine's eight-name ring at line 2732 and the look walked all eight categories. Now categories:['phones'] with the MacBook line pinned by P2, exactly as the audit's split directed.
Audit: 'split this theme in two so each can be bound to a single Apple line' — done; this is the MacBook half, window-light-ipad-desk is the other.
Audit: 'mac-pair-open-angle is two devices, remove from mustShow' — removed and barred by name.

Audit: 'add every remaining reachable file in the deck that the list is silent on' — all 13 reachable macbook-deck files are now either a hero or barred by name; verified 0 uncovered across the 271-file universe.
Audit: 'keep own-stock-macbook-stack only if the one-product sentence is rewritten' — the collectionNote now says one product ARRANGEMENT, one object or one deliberate group, never a lattice.
New: mac-half-open-glow removed from mustShow — a mostly featureless black lid on a 0.019-luminance room is the same disappearing-object fault the audit found on ipad-front-screen-off.

looks.name: iPad Desk
looks.oneLine: One iPad lying large in a deep violet room with the blind across the glass, SELL YOUR iPAD in the lit corner and the cracked-glass-still-paid line under it.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw02 c1 #3e3577 (measured luminance 0.049) is a deep violet; nn02 c1 #241f3b (0.017) a near-black violet — the two palettes freed by dropping the sports theme, and both were verified deep by the audit. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with the black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. Violet is chosen against the subject: an iPad is a silver rectangle with a dark front, so the room has to supply every bit of the colour and the amber accents have to supply the warmth — jw02's #fec674 and nn02's #feb263 on the price plate and the sticker only. Both inks are cool (#dcdceb -15, #dddceb -14) though the deep branch never veils. NO PALE PALETTE and no third palette: the list is closed at [jw02, nn02].
looks.imagery: Two heroes, both opened: assets/cutouts/ipad-angle-tilt-back.webp (1546x1062, cast scale 0.433 — the lead: an iPad Pro back at three-quarter, bright aluminium, with the Apple logo AND the iPad wordmark visible, so the picture proves the headline) and ipad-with-stylus.webp (1576x1116, 0.425 — a whole iPad Pro seen from above with a white Apple Pencil lying on the glass; the Pencil is the bright line that keeps a dark screen from going flat). BARRED WITH REASONS: ipad-front-screen-off is a near-black rectangle with a thin silver edge — on a 0.017-luminance room the object disappears (verified by opening it, and this was the audit's finding); ipad-mini-single is the same black-slab problem with thick bezels that read as a generic tablet; ipad-back-camera is a clean silver back but carries NO Apple logo and no iPad wordmark, so nothing in the picture says it is an iPad; ipad-with-pencil is a corner crop, not a whole unit; ipad-pair-sizes and ipad-stack-three are groups of two and three; ipad-with-keyboard adds a second product; ipad-front is on the owner's rejected list (a home button, below the iPad Pro M4 / Air M2 / mini 7 floor); the qs-ipad-* press renders are 512x563 and smaller and the cast would upscale them. The theme pins DEVICE_DECKS.ipad (patch P2, "line": "ipad").
looks.copy: Plain and practical — an iPad seller is clearing a drawer, not making a decision about money. Headline: SELL YOUR iPAD (one sentence, Sora, one weight, one colour). Selling point: WI-FI OR CELLULAR, ANY SIZE. Second selling point: CRACKED GLASS STILL PAID. Items line: iPad Pro • mini • Air • Regular • with Pencil. Price plate: UP TO $850 PAID TODAY. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: PAID TODAY. Five stars from reviewProof. The headline names an iPad and the ground shows an iPad with its logo and wordmark legible; this look is bound to one Apple line and can never carry a MacBook or an iPhone headline.
variations: Deep violet (jw02) with the aluminium back — amber price plate, reviewProof with five stars
Near-black violet (nn02) with the Pencil on the glass — the Pencil catching the blind
Pencil cut — headline SELL YOUR iPAD, items line leading with with Pencil, checklistHero with the four acceptance rules
Cracked-glass cut — CRACKED GLASS STILL PAID promoted to the money line, trustSeal

Audit: 'add every remaining reachable file in the deck that the list is silent on' — all 15 reachable ipad-deck files are now either a hero or barred by name or prefix; verified 0 uncovered, 0 self-blocks.

New: ipad-with-pencil dropped from the heroes — it is a corner crop, not a whole unit, the same rule that removed iphone-15-pro-back-black. ipad-with-stylus replaces it: a whole iPad Pro with the Pencil on the glass.
New: ipad-back-camera barred — a clean silver tablet back with no Apple logo and no iPad wordmark cannot carry a SELL YOUR iPAD headline.
Palettes jw02 and nn02, both verified deep by the audit, are reused here from the dropped sports theme so no two themes in the collection share a room.

looks.name: Gold On Velvet
looks.oneLine: One Cuban bracelet, a coil of chain or a stack of bars lying large in a forest-green or wine room, the blind across it, a serif headline and the tested-and-weighed promise in the light.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw07 c1 #054e2f (measured luminance 0.057) is a jeweller's forest green; jw10 c1 #6a2245 (0.046) a wine. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with the black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. Gold is the only warm thing in the frame and the room is its complement, which is how a jeweller lays gold on a green or burgundy tray. The white diagonal sheen matters more here than anywhere else in the collection: it is what makes the link edges flash where the blind has not reached them. jw07's accent #e1c2fe (lilac) and jw10's #94e994 (mint) go on the price plate and the sticker only — never on the metal, never behind it. A PALE PALETTE IS BARRED: the pale branch would wash a 0.30 ink scrim over gold and turn it to brass, and the two palettes PALFIT prefers for gold (pp02 ink R-B +42, gl02 +35) both fail the cool-ink test. Palette list closed at [jw07, jw10]. jw10's own ink is warm at +11, which is admitted only because the deep branch never veils.
looks.imagery: Six heroes, every one opened at full size: assets/cutouts/gold-bracelet-cuban.webp (1484x1184, cast scale 0.451 — the owner's stated lead, a clean Cuban link bracelet), gold-chains-pile.webp (2048x1718, 0.327 — a coil of Cuban and Figaro chain, one arrangement), gold-necklace-single.webp (1314x1591, 0.510 — a single heavy Cuban necklace), gold-bars-stack.webp (2048x1555, 0.327 — six bars whose only legible stamp is the word GOLD, the rest soft and uncontradicted), gold-jewelry-mixed.webp (2048x1734, 0.327 — a contained heap of bangles, rings and a medallion) and gold-scale-weighing.webp (1659x1785, 0.404 — an analytical balance with gold actually on the pan, for the tested-and-weighed cut only, never the lead: the appliance is bigger than the metal). BARRED WITH REASONS I CHECKED BY OPENING THE FILES: gold-rings-scatter is about thirteen near-identical wedding bands bleeding off all four edges — a repeat pattern, not an object, which is what the collection refuses; gold-bars-fan (NEW FINDING, not in the audit) is stamped SS019 WORR GOLD and 200g with mirrored nonsense along one bar — legible fabricated text at 670px, the same fault that condemned silver-bars-row's WILD BOLD / 69906. gold-chains, gold-jewelry and gold-bars cannot be barred by prefix without blocking gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed and gold-bars-stack; they are 624x457, 511x226 and 461x326, so patch P9's no-upscale gate is what stops them.
looks.copy: Discreet and precise — a gold seller is deciding whether to trust you, not whether to be excited. Headline: CASH FOR GOLD (Cormorant Garamond, one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour, always straight). Selling point: TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU. Second selling point: ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY. Items line: 10k • 14k • 18k • Scrap & Dental • Cuban Links. Price plate: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE — a number a seller can check, never 'top dollar'. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Sticker: ON THE SPOT. Five stars from reviewProof.

looks.name: Sterling Counter
looks.oneLine: A row of tarnished sterling flatware, a pair of candlesticks or a heap of silver jewellery laid large in a near-black blue room with the blind across it and the spot-shown promise in the light.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH, THE DEEPEST IN THE COLLECTION. nn09 c1 #002838 (measured luminance 0.018) and nn05 c1 #002c20 (0.019) are near-black blue and near-black teal. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H, -0.12 rad, contact shadow black 0.35, blind at 0.50 with the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. Silver has almost no colour of its own, so the room has to supply all of it: on a pale ground tarnished sterling is literally grey on grey, the failure this collection was briefed to solve. At luminance 0.018 the flatware becomes the brightest thing on the card by a wide margin and the tarnish reads as depth rather than dirt. nn09's accent #fda8bb and nn05's #d4b2fd carry the price plate; the trust panel goes solid at rgba(c1, 0.9) with white copy. Both inks are cool (#d1e1e9 -24, #d2e3dc -10). Palette list closed at [nn09, nn05]. Night Neon has no measured approval data of its own, which is stated here rather than hidden: the case for it is the luminance, not a score.
looks.imagery: Three heroes, and only three, because the rest of the silver shelf is unusable at 670px. All opened: assets/cutouts/silver-flatware-set.webp (1989x1919, cast scale 0.337 — seven pieces of genuinely tarnished sterling laid in a row, the lead), silver-candlesticks.webp (1314x1640, 0.510 — a matched pair, one arrangement) and silver-jewelry-mixed.webp (2048x1681, 0.327 — bangles and chains in one heap). THE BULLION FILES STAY BARRED AND I RE-CHECKED WHY: silver-bars-stack is silver-coloured bars stamped GOLD, silver-bars-row is stamped WILD BOLD / 69906, silver-rounds-pile carries Bitcoin symbols and reads UNITED SATES OF AMERICA. Because the honest heroes are sterling and hollowware, the headline is sterling and hollowware — the imagery decided the copy, not the other way round. silver-flatware (364x587) cannot be barred by prefix without blocking silver-flatware-set; the no-upscale gate (it would be drawn at 1.69x) is what stops it.
looks.copy: Plain and weight-led — silver sellers are usually clearing a house, so the copy is about the process, not the shine. Headline: WE BUY STERLING SILVERWARE (one sentence, Saira Condensed, one weight, one colour). Selling point: WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN. Second selling point: ANTIQUE AND ESTATE PIECES WELCOME. Items line: Sterling • .925 • Silverware • Tiffany & Co • David Yurman. Price plate: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Sticker: SAME DAY. Five stars from reviewProof. The words BARS, ROUNDS, BULLION and EAGLES never appear on this theme: no approved bullion cutout is honest, so the card must not promise one.
variations: Near-black blue (nn09) with the flatware row — blush price plate
Near-black teal (nn05) with the candlestick pair — lilac price plate
Jewellery cut — silver-jewelry-mixed as the hero, headline WE BUY SILVER JEWELRY, items Sterling • .925 • Tiffany & Co • Chrome Hearts
Estate cut — the estate line promoted above the items row, trustSeal

looks.name: Coin Stack Light
looks.oneLine: Five columns of stacked silver standing large in a petrol or cornflower room, the blind cutting across the rims, a typewriter headline and the by-weight promise in the light.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw09 c1 #054666 (measured luminance 0.054) is a petrol blue; du08 c1 #5593ef (0.290) a mid cornflower — both below 0.55, so both take the unveiled path: flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H, -0.12 rad, contact shadow black 0.35 blur 40, blind at 0.50 with the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. du08 is the one mid-value room in the collection and it earns its place here: a stack of coins is a column of small horizontal highlights, and against a mid cornflower every rim keeps an edge instead of dissolving. The blind does real work on this hero — it crosses the columns diagonally, so the rims in the light and the rims in the shadow tell you the stacks have depth. jw09's accent #fdc0b7 and du08's #3c3e65 go on the price plate only. Numerals are DM Mono, the one deliberate third face in the collection, because a coin card is a ledger and a ledger sets its figures monospaced. Palette list closed at [jw09, du08].
looks.imagery: ONE hero, and the reason is the point of this repair: assets/cutouts/coin-stack-silver.webp (1817x2048, cast scale 0.369) — five columns of stacked coins seen edge-on with no legible inscription anywhere in the frame. It is the only coin cutout that cannot contradict whatever items line the engine prints. EVERY OTHER REACHABLE COIN FILE FAILS ON WHAT IS IN THE PICTURE, and I opened them all at full size to check: coin-collection-tray is a world tray — I zoomed it and the cells hold euro 5-cent pieces beside Washington quarters and Lincoln cents, so under an items line reading Morgans • Peace Dollars • Eagles it is the owner's own complaint back again; coin-rolls-paper is six rolls of 1 EURO coins; coin-jar-full is a jar of euros; coin-album-pages mixes euro cents with US quarters; coin-silver-dollar-pair is a Morgan whose obverse reads 1998, a year with no Morgan mintage; coin-graded-fan-three reads V LODS OF EY and INO COH WO ROUT; coin-loose-pile is US-dominant but bleeds off all four edges, so at -0.12 rad it reads as a rotated photograph rather than an object; coin-slab, coin-slabs-stack and coin-single-large are slabs, and the slab frame belongs to Pokemon and sports only. coin-stack (555x276) cannot be barred by prefix without blocking coin-stack-silver; the no-upscale gate (1.21x) stops it.
looks.copy: Ledger-plain, the voice of somebody who counts for a living. Headline: WE BUY COINS (one sentence, Special Elite, one weight, one colour). Selling point: 90% JUNK SILVER PAID BY WEIGHT. Second selling point: WHOLE COLLECTIONS AND ESTATES. Items line: Morgans • Peace Dollars • Key Dates • Junk Silver • Proof Sets. Price plate: PAID ON THE SPOT, AT SPOT. CTA: REQUEST AN APPRAISAL. Sticker: ON THE SPOT. Five stars from reviewProof. No grading company is named in the headline — the hero is ungraded metal — and the slab frame is barred outright.
variations: Petrol room (jw09) — the blind crossing the columns, reviewProof with five stars
Cornflower room (du08) — every rim keeping its edge, trustSeal
By-weight cut — 90% JUNK SILVER PAID BY WEIGHT promoted to the money line, stepsFlow
Challenge cut — kicker GOT A COIN SHOP QUOTE?, money line WE TOP THE COIN SHOP, same hero
fixesApplied: Audit REJECT: 'three of seven mustShow assets are foreign coins under a US coin headline' — coin-rolls-paper, coin-jar-full and coin-album-pages moved to neverShow, and I opened them to confirm.

Audit: 'coin-silver-dollar-pair is a Morgan dated 1998 and a look has no lead/non-lead mechanism' — barred by name; cutSrc is a flat modulo over the pool, so an allowed-but-never-lead asset does not exist.
Audit: 'du07 is the second-worst measured palette at 20%' — replaced with du08 (44%), and the groundSpec is rewritten for #5593ef, the mid cornflower, with its real accent #3c3e65.

Audit: keep coin-collection-tray — OVERRIDDEN, with evidence: I zoomed the tray and it holds euro 5-cent pieces beside the US coins, which fails the same test the audit applied to the other three euro files. It is barred and the theme now runs on the one hero that carries no inscription at all.

Old self-block fixed: the previous neverShow contained 'coin-stack', which by literal startsWith blocks its own mustShow entry coin-stack-silver. Removed; coin-stack is stopped by the no-upscale gate instead.

Audit: 'if LAB_SUBCATS=1 the coins sub-deck reduces the pool to three barred slabs and prints GRADED COINS' — run this collection with LAB_SUBCATS unset or 0, or set the coins 'slabs' sub-deck at line 320 to ready:false.

looks.collectionNote:
WINDOW LIGHT, REPAIRED: EIGHT CARDS, EACH ONE OBJECT IN A COLOURED ROOM WITH A BLIND DRAWN ACROSS IT. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity (retheme_lab.mjs line 2882): fill c1, a white diagonal sheen 0.10 to zero across 55%, the hero fitted at k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) and drawn at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (black 0.35, blur 40, offset 24/30); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it (blur 26 at full strength from 0.62W to 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half); then a scrim. Line 3424 deletes every Hero/Lineup Product layer once __castBg is set, so the product IS the background and nothing is ever drawn over the type. Panels go solid over a cast ground (line 2959), so every card is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. Cast is measured at 50% approval — the second-best real ground — and this collection deliberately spends it rather than the 100% tile wall, because tile belongs to the device-wall, metal-wall and card-wall collections and a lattice cannot show ONE object at print scale. The one way a window-light card can lose its identity is the cast→tile fall-through at line 2891 when the hero image fails to load; lookFaults already catches that as "ground tile but the theme is cast" and re-seeds once.

ROSTER, EIGHT THEMES: Cosmic Orange Room and Titanium Daylight (iPhone line), MacBook Desk and iPad Desk (the split of the old Apple Silicon Desk), Gold On Velvet, Sterling Counter, Coin Stack Light (renamed from window-light-coin-tray; the tray it was named for is now barred, see that theme), Forecourt Light (Garage Night folded in as its bikes-deck cut). Dropped: Clinic Window and Slab Under Glass. Two categories therefore have no theme here — pokemon (poke-slabs-trio is the only approved file and it is three empty pastel slabs) and strips and sports for the reasons in droppedThemes. Shipping nothing beats shipping a 670px blank.

FOUR RULES THIS REPAIR ADDS, ALL PROGRAMMABLE, ALL RE-RUN AGAINST EVERY FILE I NAME. (1) NO UPSCALE: a cast hero must satisfy min(669.6/w, 993.6/h) <= 1 on a 1080 card, i.e. at least 670px wide OR at least 994px tall. All 24 heroes in the eight themes pass (the worst is own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 at 0.931). It is also what independently disqualifies every qs- press render (qs-device-macbook-pro is 381x230, k=1.76) and the five short-named legacy files below. (2) WHOLE UNIT, NEVER A MACRO CROP: it removes iphone-15-pro-back-black (I opened it — a tight crop of the camera corner, not a phone) and ipad-with-pencil (an iPad corner running off frame). (3) COOL INK, CLOSED PALETTE LIST: on a pale palette (lum(c1) > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room with th.ink at 0.20, an accent→ink gradient, and an ink scrim at 0.30 — about half the finished ground is INK — so a pale palette is chosen by its ink and the ink must be cool: ink red channel at least 16 below blue. Measured: pa05 -28, ca07 -40, ca01 -36, cd05 -38, cd06 -46 pass; cd04 (#263f2b) is -5 and FAILS, so the old collectionNote's claim that the test "passes cd04" was false and cd04 is gone from the collection. Every palette list below is closed. (4) ONE PRODUCT ARRANGEMENT PER CARD, not one product: one object or one deliberate group (a flatware fan, a candlestick pair, a chain coil, the owner's own stack of five MacBooks), never a lattice and never a repeat pattern — which is what removes gold-rings-scatter (thirteen near-identical bands bleeding off all four edges).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, NOT FROM THE RECIPE. Already applied, no action: the look lookup now reads (L.key || L.id) at lines 560/2731/2768, so looks.json entries keyed by `id` do bind; the category binding is in at 2729-2733 — `lookCats = look.categories.filter(c => RING0.includes(c))` — which is exactly why a theme's categories array may hold only phones/gold/cars/pokemon/coins/silver/sports/strips: "macbook", "ipad" or "bikes" filter to empty and the look silently walks all eight categories again; and slabFrame at 3425 is now gated `(!look && /pokemon|sports/…)`, so no look on a cast ground can be overwritten by a slab frame. STILL OUTSTANDING, and this collection is not correct without them: P2, the Apple-line binding — line 2797 `DEVICE_DECKS[APPLE[sd % APPLE.length]]` must become `DEVICE_DECKS[(look && look.line) || APPLE[…]]`, or half of every phones card is an iPad or a MacBook; P3, the pool binding — line 2805 `const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f))` must become `const allow = look && (look.mustShow||[]).filter(m => ALLCUTS.includes(m)); const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f) && (!allow || !allow.length || allow.includes(f)));` — read the allow-list off mustShow itself rather than adding a parallel `cuts` map, so the stated rule and the actual pool can never drift apart; P6, the enforcement gap — on a cast card line 3424 has already deleted the hero layer by the time lookFaults runs, so `names` is empty and BOTH mustShow and the cutout half of neverShow are vacuous: record `t2.__castCut = cutSrc.split('/').pop().replace(/\.webp$/,'')` at line 2916 and include it in `names` at line 2521, or every asset rule in this collection is advisory; P7, line 201 and the sub-deck at 325 — drop Ducati from the bikes items line, it is not an allowed marque and a look supplies no copy; P9, the no-upscale gate — in the cast branch skip a hero whose k > 1 and take the next candidate. P9 is not decoration: prefix matching is literal startsWith, so gold-chains, gold-jewelry, gold-bars, silver-flatware and coin-stack (624x457, 511x226, 461x326, 364x587, 555x276 — all upscales) CANNOT be barred by neverShow without also barring gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-bars-stack, silver-flatware-set and coin-stack-silver, which are the heroes. Those five files are the only holes left in the collection's neverShow coverage and P9 is what closes them. Also run with LAB_DONORS set to this collection's palettes: eleven of the sixteen are outside the default DONORS list, so DONORS.indexOf(pal) returns -1, j collapses to 0, and card ids (layout-DONORS[j]-v) collide across looks and overwrite each other's .webp files.

COVERAGE TEST I RAN AGAINST MY OWN RULES. I built the 271-file universe of every approved product cutout any deck can hand a look (all thirteen deck pools plus cash-, android-, tablet-, qs-, own-stock-, poke-, sports-, strip-), then for each theme checked three things: every mustShow entry is approved, reachable through its deck's cut prefixes, and passes the no-upscale rule; no neverShow entry is a startsWith prefix of any mustShow entry (this caught a real self-block in the old collection — Coin Tray banned "coin-stack", which blocks its own hero coin-stack-silver, and my first gold draft banned "gold-bars", which blocks gold-bars-stack); and every one of the 271 files that is not a mustShow entry is matched by some neverShow entry. Result: 0 unreachable, 0 upscaled, 0 self-blocks, 0 uncovered except the five prefix-collision files named above. That is the answer to "build a card that satisfies mustShow, breaks nothing in neverShow, and still shows the wrong thing": with P6 in place the only such card is one of those five files, and P9 stops all five.

looks.name: Forecourt Light
looks.oneLine: One vehicle — a silver sedan, a white pickup, a cargo van or a naked motorcycle — parked large in a daylight-teal or midnight-navy room with the blind across its flank and a stencilled headline in the light.
looks.groundSpec: ONE PALE, ONE DEEP. ca01 c1 #baf8f1 (measured luminance 0.839) clears 0.55 and takes the pale path, so the room is repainted by its ink #183f3c (R-B -36, comfortably cool) at 0.20 plus a 0.30 scrim, with its accent #d9322b laying a crimson wash across the top at 0.18 — a deep teal shed with late sun coming through. nn01 c1 #0e253c (0.017) is a midnight navy on the unveiled path: flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero, black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22 — the garage at nine at night, with accent #fcaca5 as the one neon on the price plate. Every body in the pool is white or silver, which is why the room must carry the colour: a white van on a white ground is the grey card, a white van on a teal ground is a photograph. The blind is at its most literal here, reading as light through a roller door across the flank. Big Shoulders Stencil Display is the collection's one stencil face and it belongs on this theme — stencil is the top-scoring style at 60% and it reads as fleet marking rather than decoration. Palette list closed at [ca01, nn01]. nn04 (#39181e), the old Garage Night oxblood, is dropped: its ink is warm at R-B +16 measured, and an unenforceable 'fall back if it ever reads brown on a proof' is not a rule a run can apply.
looks.imagery: Four heroes, one for each deck the cars slot rotates through (line 2793, VEHICLES = cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans), all opened: assets/cutouts/car-sedan-front.webp (2048x1366, cast scale 0.327 — a silver sedan in three-quarter front; the grille emblem is a Toyota Crown and Toyota is an allowed marque) for the cars deck, car-truck-front.webp (1869x1599, 0.358 — a white crew-cab pickup) for trucks, car-van-cargo.webp (1903x1689, 0.352 — a white high-roof Sprinter-shape body; Mercedes is allowed) for vans, and car-motorcycle-side.webp (1790x1886, 0.374 — a modern naked bike from the rear three-quarter, white tank, black engine and rear tyre; I zoomed the tank and the badge is an illegible emblem, so the card never implies a marque) for bikes. This one look therefore owns the whole cars slot instead of sharing it. BARRED WITH REASONS I VERIFIED AT ZOOM: car-sedan-rear is a C7-facelift Audi A6 and Audi is first on the owner's too-niche list; car-suv-side is a black Lincoln, a marque not on the allowed list, and a black body defeats the white-or-silver-against-a-coloured-room premise. Keys, titles, wheels, engine bays, the classic and the damaged front are all barred: the premise is the vehicle itself in the light, and a key fob at three-quarter scale is not the thing the headline names.
looks.copy: Flat and operational — a tow, a title, a number, no adjectives. Headline: WE BUY CARS, or WE BUY TRUCKS / WE BUY WORK VANS / WE BUY MOTORCYCLES, matched to the deck the card is running and to the vehicle in the ground (one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour). Selling point: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE TOW (bikes: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE LOAD IT). Second selling point: TITLE, DMV AND LIEN PAYOFF HANDLED (bikes: TITLE OR NOT, RUNNING OR NOT). Items line: Title In Hand • Running Or Not • High Miles • Salvage • Free Tow. Price plate: UP TO $15,000 CASH (trucks $25,000, vans $20,000, bikes $12,000). CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER. Sticker: SAME DAY. Five stars from reviewProof. NO MARQUE IS EVER PRINTED OR DRAWN: no wordmark (every logo: layer is barred, which is what stops the brand-led path inking a TOYOTA mark into a corner) and none of TOYOTAS, TACOMAS, TUNDRAS, HONDAS, FORDS, F-150S, TRANSITS, CHEVYS, SILVERADOS, NISSANS, JEEPS, TESLAS, BMWS, MERCEDES, SPRINTERS, HYUNDAIS, KIAS, DODGES, RAMS, HARLEYS, YAMAHAS, KAWASAKIS or DUCATIS in a headline — these live here in copy because an uppercase word in neverShow is tested against lowercase filenames and can never match. Patch P7 is required with this theme: the engine's own bikes items line at line 201 prints Ducati, which is not an allowed marque and which a look cannot overwrite. Comparative cuts are allowed on named wholesale buyers only, without an apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CARVANA, WE TOP CARMAX.
variations: Daylight teal (ca01) with the silver sedan — crimson window light, headline WE BUY CARS
Daylight teal (ca01) with the white pickup — headline WE BUY TRUCKS, price plate UP TO $25,000 CASH
Van cut — car-van-cargo as the hero, headline WE BUY WORK VANS, items Transit • Sprinter • ProMaster • Fleet Lots, kicker FLEETS OK
Midnight navy (nn01) with the naked bike — blush neon on the price plate, headline WE BUY MOTORCYCLES, neonNight (this is the old Garage Night, folded in)

All four heroes go in one list keyed by the category; the deck's own cut prefixes already separate them — verified: the cars pool intersects to car-sedan-front, trucks to car-truck-front, vans to car-van-cargo, bikes to car-motorcycle-side.

looks.name: Mint Counter Wall
looks.oneLine: The engine's device wall drowned in pastel teal, with the shop's plainest counter copy on solid ink plates and a magenta money word.
looks.groundSpec: pa05 c1 #c6faeb has luminance 0.864, so the plane keeps the mint rather than falling back to #eceef2. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7; every unit is contain-fitted to its OWN cell at min((cw-24)/w,(chh-24)/h)*0.96, so the wall is not one scale and this recipe does not claim it is. One contact shadow per cell, rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, +10/+16. Veil is the palette ink #1b4037 (luminance 0.042, so the scrim is 0.60, not 0.72). The panel pass then fills EVERY rect between 150x60 and 0.92W x 0.92H with rgba(#1b4037,0.90) — several solid plates, not one counter-card; white on that tone measures 11.4:1, so the small print holds on all of them. Signature colour is pa05's magenta #c44fbd on the money word and the CTA rule, with support #638f49 on the small caps. The pa04 run is the same build one step warmer: plane #d9f7d3, veil #2b3e27, accent violet #9265ee. ground:'tile' is itself the enforcement — lookFaults raises a fault on any other ground, and the tile pass cannot fall through to cast because the Apple pools never drop below four.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for whichever Apple line the seed deals — twelve cells on the iPhone and MacBook decks, eight on the iPad deck. Foreground: this is the collection's baseline card and it takes any honest current single unit the deck offers — a 17 Pro back, a 15 Pro blue, gold or white body, a black-glass front, a current qs- press render, or one of the two upright orange 17 Pro renders. On one card in three the engine also lays a lineup of up to five singles from the same deck pool; both hero and lineup are governed by the lists below.
