The pool is the subject's whole approved shelf minus two-up composites (the MULTI filter) minus anything under 240px wide, sliced to twelve, so it is fixed per deck: the iPhone wall is always iphone-15-pro-back-black, -blue, -gold, -white, iphone-15-pro-front-on, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-hand-back-offer, iphone-in-hand-screen-on, iphone-screen-on-glow, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02 and -06; the iPad wall is exactly eight units (ipad-angle-tilt-back, ipad-back-camera, ipad-front-screen-off, ipad-mini-single, ipad-with-keyboard, ipad-with-pencil, ipad-with-stylus, own-stock-iphone-ipad), which is the pool size that makes row three a copy of row one; the MacBook wall still carries mac-damaged-screen. No look field selects wall units, so NO theme here claims a curated wall, a pool size or a lattice rhythm — index=(n+seed)%pool.length is arithmetic the recipe cannot reach, and the two in-hand shots and one macro crop in the iPhone wall are ground texture under a 0.60 veil, not a promise the recipe can make. (b) EACH UNIT IS CONTAIN-FITTED TO ITS OWN CELL. Aspects in the iPhone pool run 0.42 to 1.11, so adjacent cells differ in apparent size by more than 2x; 'all twelve share one scale' is deleted collection-wide. (c) THE DECK ROTATES iphone, iphone, iphone, ipad, ipad, macbook on sd%6 and look.categories does not steer it, so every card's headline, items line, price, badges, marks and selling points belong to whichever Apple line the seed dealt. Every copy block here is written deck-neutral: SELL YOUR iPHONE / iPAD / MACBOOK is the engine's own sentence, one sentence in one face, and the two selling points come from the engine's pool (the deck's sub lines, then FREE WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE, then INFO.yes and INFO.no) — no theme invents a claim and every bare figure keeps its UP TO. WHAT A THEME OWNS: two palettes, its faces, its layouts, its variations, and its mustShow/neverShow, which lookFaults now enforces on the card's cutout LAYERS (hero and lineup), re-seeding the card once on a fault. Those lists are the only enforcement in the set, so every rule is a bare startsWith token — a rule containing a space is prose the matcher skips, which is why every parenthesised entry from the first draft banned nothing. Each theme also carries ONE enforceable foreground rule (greyscale bodies, backs only, single bodies, dark bodies, pale bodies) so the eight differ in what they SHOW, not only in what colour they are. WHAT THE LISTS CANNOT REACH, stated rather than pretended: the wall (a drawn ground, not layers); a cast product (the hero layer is deleted under a cast ground, which is why no theme here takes cast); the sticker (five texts by seed: CASH TODAY, PAID TODAY, SAME DAY, ON THE SPOT, FREE QUOTE); the kicker (KICKERS.apple by seed); and the icon marks — ELEMENTS.phones carries a watch glyph on iPhone cards, and there is no tablet or laptop glyph in the set at all. Three refusals hold across all eight: no slab (slabFrame already returns unless the category is pokemon or sports), no watch theme (watch is out of the Apple rotation), and no curved headline over a straight lattice, so arcCrown and gradientWave stay out of every layout list. Two data fixes are asked for and neither is applied here: assets/approved-assets.json still lists mac-damaged-screen in the approved array while filing it under damage-heavy, so it sits in the live MacBook wall; and no code path places an Apple mark (BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only), so 'logo:apple' is unreachable and every theme bans logos outright with the catch-all rule 'logo:'.

looks.name: Blueprint Navy Wall
looks.oneLine: A blueprint navy field under a stencil headline and a mono spec panel — the technical card of the set, with the relic laptops kept out of the foreground by name.
looks.groundSpec: jw01 c1 #1f3e7a has luminance 0.051, so the plane falls back to the neutral #eceef2 and the veil is the navy itself at 0.60 — a blueprint field with pale hardware in it. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit, one shadow per cell rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16. Panels take rgba(#1f3e7a,0.90), white on it 10.4:1. Numerals are the one place this theme spends a third face: JetBrains Mono on the money line and the spec panel, which is the point of the card. Accent #fdc3a0 on the money word, support #53b9e0 on the small caps. The nn01 run drops the field to near-black: veil #0e253c, accent coral #fcaca5, white on panel 15.7:1. DUOTONE STAYS OUT here and collection-wide: du07 and du08 have c1 luminance 0.29-0.31, so the panel pass would land white copy on a mid blue at about 3:1. Note for the reviewer: Night Neon has no approval data at family or palette level, so the jw01 run is the one to judge first.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for the deck the seed deals — and on the MacBook seed that wall still contains mac-damaged-screen, because assets/approved-assets.json lists it in the approved array while also filing it under damage-heavy. The recipe cannot reach the wall; it can and does keep every relic out of the FOREGROUND. Foreground: one machine or one handset, screen off or wallpapered, no hands, no stacks, no accessories. The two qs-device-macbook- files are the only current laptop singles on the shelf — I opened the rest: mac-with-accessories is a closed lid beside a home-button iPhone and an AirPods case, mac-half-open-glow is a black silhouette seen from behind, mac-closed-side is a 288x1834 edge-on sliver, mac-pro-open-front and macbook-open-angle have no notch and an unlit screen, and own-stock-macbook-stack is a pile of closed lids. All are banned below. Marks are the deck's own icons — there is no laptop glyph in the set, so the check and the bolt carry it.
looks.copy: Technical and unbothered — the language of someone who has opened a hundred of these. The headline is the deck's own sentence in the stencil face, one sentence, one weight, one colour; on the MacBook seed it reads SELL YOUR MACBOOK with the deck's own UP TO $1,900 PAID TODAY set in JetBrains Mono, and on stepsFlow line one must carry the money word (SELL YOUR MACBOOK / IN 3 STEPS, never a bare IN 3 STEPS). Two selling points from the engine's pool; BATTERY OR SCREEN FAULTS FINE and WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE are the MacBook deck's own sub lines and land first when that deck is dealt. One seal from INFO.seals. Money keeps its UP TO. Five stars where a rating appears.

Night rack (nn01: the field goes almost black, coral money word)
Challenge card (one seed in three: WE BEAT / BEST BUY'S / MACBOOK TRADE-IN VALUE on a MacBook seed)

Replaced 'marks are a laptop glyph' with the truth: no laptop glyph exists.

looks.name: Chalk Mono Wall
looks.oneLine: A near-white plane gone true charcoal, one knockout band of type, one teal accent — and the only foreground in the set held to black, white and silver bodies.
looks.groundSpec: ck03 c1 #f2f8f9 has luminance 0.929 — the palest plane in the collection, effectively a white counter. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit, one shadow per cell rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16. Veil is ink #173f43 at 0.60: because the plane is near-neutral the wall lands as true charcoal rather than a tinted colour, which is the whole idea. Panels take rgba(#173f43,0.90), white on it 11.5:1. Exactly one colour is allowed on the type: ck03's teal #026a73 on the money word and nothing else — no second accent, no support tint. bandKnockout gives the headline its full-bleed band, but the panel pass solidifies every other qualifying rect too, so the card carries more than one solid mass; the knockout is the band's job, not a claim about the whole card. The ck09 run swaps the one colour to #0c658d. Note for the reviewer: Chalk carries no approval data at family or palette level.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for the deck the seed deals; it is fixed and it contains colour, which no recipe can change. Foreground rule, enforced, and it is what makes this card monochrome: BLACK, WHITE AND SILVER BODIES ONLY. The hero and every lineup unit must be a 17 Pro in black or silver, a white 15 Pro back, a black-glass front, a grey iPad back, front or mini, or the silver MacBook — the blue and gold bodies, the orange renders, the lit cyan screen and the wallpapered qs- press sheets are banned below, so a coloured foreground re-seeds instead of shipping. The one licensed colour on the card is the teal money word; the one licensed colour in a foreground unit is the MacBook's own wallpaper, which cannot be separated from the only current laptop file on the shelf. No ornament but a hairline rule in the accent.
looks.copy: Blunt, few words, high contrast — the type is the design. The headline is the deck's own sentence knocked out of the band, one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour. Two selling points from the engine's pool; PAID BEFORE WE LEAVE and NO LOWBALL "FINAL OFFERS" are real INFO lines and suit this voice. One seal from INFO.seals. Money keeps its UP TO, set in Oswald. No glow behind the condensed face at any size. On reviewProof the rating is five stars, always five. On one card in three the challenge framing replaces the deck copy, and WE MATCH takes no apostrophe-S.
variations: Teal accent (ck03: #f2f8f9 plane, #173f43 veil, #026a73 money word)
Indigo accent (ck09: #f3f8fa plane, #1f3c4c veil, #0c658d money word)
Challenge card (one seed in three)

Replaced the unenforceable sentence 'no coloured phone may enter this wall' with a closed list that a matcher can act on.
Recorded that bandKnockout's band is full-bleed but the panel pass solidifies the other plates too, so the card is not one solid mass.
Dropped the pool-of-6 rhythm and the 'every unit appears twice' arithmetic — unreachable.
Every rule rewritten as a bare token; logo:apple exception dropped for 'logo:'.

looks.name: Night Screen Wall
looks.oneLine: The deepest veil in the set — a near-black teal field with pale hardware floating in it, monospaced digits, and a foreground of dark bodies and lit glass.
looks.groundSpec: nn06 c1 #012a2c has luminance 0.018 — the deepest ground here — so the plane falls back to the neutral #eceef2 and the veil is that near-black at 0.60, which leaves the wall reading as night with the pale devices floating in it. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit; keep the contact shadow at rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16 even on a dark field, because it is what stops the units looking pasted on. Panels take rgba(#012a2c,0.90) and white on that is 15.4:1 — the highest contrast in the collection, which is what lets this card carry small print at night. Night Neon keeps monospaced digits, so DM Mono carries the money line and the phone number on a square-cornered plate. Accent pink #fe9eea on the money word, support #d063bc on the small caps; the nn05 run goes green-black at #002c20 with a lilac #d4b2fd accent. Note for the reviewer: Night Neon carries no approval data at family or palette level, and this is the only theme in the set riding on it.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for the deck the seed deals. Foreground rule, enforced: DARK BODIES AND LIT GLASS. The hero is a black 17 Pro, a blue 15 Pro, a black-glass front, an upright orange 17 Pro render, a wallpapered qs- press sheet, a grey iPad or the MacBook with its screen lit — the pale white, gold and silver finishes are banned below so nothing on the foreground goes chalky against the night field. The one thing the recipe cannot promise is a travelling glow: the only lit iPhone cutout on the shelf is a notched 12/13-era body with a flat cyan screen, and it is banned as below the newest-hardware floor. Marks are the deck's own icons in the accent — no stars, planets or nebulae; note that ELEMENTS.phones also carries a watch glyph, which is the one mark this card would rather not have and cannot suppress.
looks.copy: After-hours, fast, no ceremony. The headline is the deck's own sentence in Teko, one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour. Two selling points from the engine's pool; NO MAIL IT IN AND WAIT WEEKS and WE COME TO YOU are real INFO lines and fit the hour. The money line and the phone number (562) 999-4994 are set in DM Mono on a square-cornered plate — the Night Neon corner language. One seal from INFO.seals. Money keeps its UP TO. On reviewProof the rating is five stars, always five. On one card in three the challenge framing replaces the deck copy; WE MATCH takes no apostrophe-S.

Green night (nn05: #002c20 veil, lilac money word)

looks.name: Ink Tag Wall
looks.oneLine: A slate plane, a stub-shaped plate with a perforated edge and one hot pink — the challenge card of the set, where we name the other guy's number.
looks.groundSpec: ik01 c1 #e5f3f6 has luminance 0.874, so the plane keeps its pale slate. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit, one shadow per cell rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16. Veil is ink #173e45 at 0.60; panels take rgba(#173e45,0.90), white on it 11.5:1. Two cautions for the reviewer, both from the measured data: ticketStub took 25%, the lowest layout in the table, so it is the third choice here and never the headline one; and Ink Pop carries no approval data at family or palette level.

fixesApplied: Abandoned the lean premise, which had one supporting asset. I opened all five named units: ip-angle-hero-tilt lies near-horizontal, ip-angle-standing-lean is a near-upright two-lens iPhone 12, ip-angle-back-topdown is a top-down crop with no lean at all, and the blue and gold 15 Pro bodies are upright.

looks.collectionNote: Eight colourways of ONE engine-built ground: the device wall drawn at scripts/retheme_lab.mjs:2925-2952 — 4 columns x 3 rows, 28px gutters, cells 235 x 322.7 at 1080, one contact shadow per cell (rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, +10/+16), veiled by the palette's own dark tone at 0.60. Three engine facts govern every theme here and none of them was true in the first draft. (a) THE WALL IS NOT AUTHORED. The pool is the subject's whole approved shelf minus two-up composites (the MULTI filter) minus anything under 240px wide, sliced to twelve, so it is fixed per deck: the iPhone wall is always iphone-15-pro-back-black, -blue, -gold, -white, iphone-15-pro-front-on, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-hand-back-offer, iphone-in-hand-screen-on, iphone-screen-on-glow, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02 and -06; the iPad wall is exactly eight units (ipad-angle-tilt-back, ipad-back-camera, ipad-front-screen-off, ipad-mini-single, ipad-with-keyboard, ipad-with-pencil, ipad-with-stylus, own-stock-iphone-ipad), which is the pool size that makes row three a copy of row one; the MacBook wall still carries mac-damaged-screen. No look field selects wall units, so NO theme here claims a curated wall, a pool size or a lattice rhythm — index=(n+seed)%pool.length is arithmetic the recipe cannot reach, and the two in-hand shots and one macro crop in the iPhone wall are ground texture under a 0.60 veil, not a promise the recipe can make. (b) EACH UNIT IS CONTAIN-FITTED TO ITS OWN CELL. Aspects in the iPhone pool run 0.42 to 1.11, so adjacent cells differ in apparent size by more than 2x; 'all twelve share one scale' is deleted collection-wide. (c) THE DECK ROTATES iphone, iphone, iphone, ipad, ipad, macbook on sd%6 and look.categories does not steer it, so every card's headline, items line, price, badges, marks and selling points belong to whichever Apple line the seed dealt. Every copy block here is written deck-neutral: SELL YOUR iPHONE / iPAD / MACBOOK is the engine's own sentence, one sentence in one face, and the two selling points come from the engine's pool (the deck's sub lines, then FREE WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE, then INFO.yes and INFO.no) — no theme invents a claim and every bare figure keeps its UP TO. WHAT A THEME OWNS: two palettes, its faces, its layouts, its variations, and its mustShow/neverShow, which lookFaults now enforces on the card's cutout LAYERS (hero and lineup), re-seeding the card once on a fault. Those lists are the only enforcement in the set, so every rule is a bare startsWith token — a rule containing a space is prose the matcher skips, which is why every parenthesised entry from the first draft banned nothing. Each theme also carries ONE enforceable foreground rule (greyscale bodies, backs only, single bodies, dark bodies, pale bodies) so the eight differ in what they SHOW, not only in what colour they are. WHAT THE LISTS CANNOT REACH, stated rather than pretended: the wall (a drawn ground, not layers); a cast product (the hero layer is deleted under a cast ground, which is why no theme here takes cast); the sticker (five texts by seed: CASH TODAY, PAID TODAY, SAME DAY, ON THE SPOT, FREE QUOTE); the kicker (KICKERS.apple by seed); and the icon marks — ELEMENTS.phones carries a watch glyph on iPhone cards, and there is no tablet or laptop glyph in the set at all. Three refusals hold across all eight: no slab (slabFrame already returns unless the category is pokemon or sports), no watch theme (watch is out of the Apple rotation), and no curved headline over a straight lattice, so arcCrown and gradientWave stay out of every layout list. Two data fixes are asked for and neither is applied here: assets/approved-assets.json still lists mac-damaged-screen in the approved array while filing it under damage-heavy, so it sits in the live MacBook wall; and no code path places an Apple mark (BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only), so 'logo:apple' is unreachable and every theme bans logos outright with the catch-all rule 'logo:'.

looks.name: Gem Label
looks.oneLine: The real graded-slab frame fills the card, WE BUY / POKEMON typed on the paper label like a grade line, a 1999 Charizard washed back to a grey ghost in the window below, and a 10 / GEM MT block at the right.
looks.groundSpec:
slabFrame() paints the whole ground and now fires deterministically: the call site reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && ...sd % 3 === 0)), so a look declaring ground 'slab' gets the frame on every card. The audit's 'two cards in three are not slab cards' is resolved in the engine; LAB_SLAB=1 is no longer required, only LAB_SLABGRADE=num (see the grade block).

GEOMETRY, RE-DERIVED AND THEN RE-MEASURED OFF THE FILE. SLAB = { iw 1572, ih 1425, label [0.075,0.055,0.925,0.265], win [0.075,0.31,0.925,0.95] }. k0 = 1080/1425 = 0.7579, dw = 1191.4, ox = -55.7 — the frame bleeds 56px off both edges, which is correct. LABEL box: x 33.7, y 59.4, w 1012.7, h 226.8. WINDOW box: x 33.7, y 334.8, w 1012.7, h 691.2 — a 1.47:1 letterbox, NOT the 1.49:1 the old spec claimed, and 1013 wide, not 1027. Then the correction nobody had made: I sampled the asset's pixels, and the physical white label runs y 0.074-0.259 and the physical white card runs y 0.354-0.916. So the painted window overhangs the real card by 48px at the top and 37px at the bottom — 12% of its height sits on the moulded bezel and the holder's lower lip, and the top edge of the wash cuts across the step between label and window. REQUIRED: SLAB.win becomes [0.075,0.354,0.924,0.916] and SLAB.label becomes [0.075,0.074,0.924,0.259]. Until that lands the window is 12% taller than the card it is printed on.

WHAT GOES IN THE WINDOW. slabFrame takes WEBBG[cat] first; WEBBG.pokemon has two files and the pick is web[seed % 2], so the engine alternates pokemon-charizard-card-1 and -2 by seed and CANNOT be pinned. Both are washed at the same rate, so the wash is set for the busier of the two (-2, detail 15.47 in assets/backdrop-lum.json). REQUIRED: raise the photo wash from rgba(c1,0.66) to rgba(c1,0.74) — enough that the slab in the photograph reads as a grey ghost rather than as a third party's grading record (see neverShow). The fit is cover, k = max((1012.7-12)/iw, (691.2-12)/ih) * 1.02.

THE HEADLINE COLOUR, STATED THE RIGHT WAY ROUND. Code: const dark = lumHex(th.ink) < 0.35 ? th.ink : '#17171a'. Both palettes clear that test — ck02 ink #4d2f2c at lum 0.038, ck05 ink #2c3850 at lum 0.039 — so the headline takes th.ink, a warm or cool near-black, and NOT #17171a. slabFrame then strips gradient, shadow and stroke and locks it, which is why this theme genuinely delivers one sentence in one face and one colour where the cast themes cannot.

LABEL FURNITURE. Label painted rgba(c1,0.06) so ck02's #fbf5f5 and ck05's #f5f7fb stay paper-white. Divider 2px rgba(20,20,24,0.55) at 68% of the label, x 722. Barcode 2-5px bars at #1a1a1e, height 0.12 of the label, running 72% to 96%, x 762 to 1006. Headline scaled into the left 66% of the label at k <= 1.8. Grade block centred at x 884.

THE HERO IS DRAWN TWICE. slabFrame does not remove the deck's cutout. Line 3428 filters Hero Product only when t2.__castBg, and slabFrame runs after it, so poke-slabs-trio is scaled into the same window box as the copy, on top of the photograph. REQUIRED: add `if (t2.__slab) t2.layers = t2.layers.filter(l => !/^Hero Product|^Lineup Product/.test(l.name || ''));` beside the cast filter. Until that lands, three blank acrylic cases sit over the Charizard.

bg.scrim stays 0.001 (the ground is already painted) and __dg = true, so the canvas keeps its own colour instead of being greyscaled.
looks.imagery:
assets/cutouts/sports-slab-graded.webp as the frame — I opened it: a blank front-on graded holder, a landscape label panel over a landscape window, no branding of any kind on it. In the window: assets/bg-web/pokemon-charizard-card-1.jpg or -2.jpg (1920x1280), alternating by seed. I opened both: a PSA-slabbed 1999 Pokemon Game Charizard Holo, GEM MT 10, standing on an easel on a white table with two more slabs behind it.

LICENCE, AND THE THING THE OLD SPEC GOT BACKWARDS. assets/bg-web/ATTRIBUTION.json: CC BY-SA 2.0, artist 'Romer Jed Medina from Newark, NJ', File:2021 New York Comic Con (Batch Edits - 031). The photographer's HAKURO PHOTOGRAPHY mark in the bottom-right IS the licence's attribution. It is never covered, cropped or blurred; the old spec's 'watermark control' spec chip was the one thing BY-SA forbids, and no such chip exists in the engine anyway. Instead print the credit line PHOTO: ROMER JED MEDINA / CC BY-SA 2.0 in th.faces.support at fontSize 18, fill th.sub, at left 40 / top 1042, originY bottom.

AND THE GATE THE AUDIT NAMED BUT DID NOT CLOSE: ShareAlike is hostile to a proprietary ad, and the photograph additionally contains a real third party's grading record and Pokemon trade dress. This theme does not ship until the owner has accepted CC BY-SA 2.0 terms on the finished card, or the photograph is replaced by a cleared one. The 0.74 wash reduces the exposure; it does not remove it. That decision is the owner's, and it is written here so it is made deliberately.

looks.copy: Flat and factual, the voice of a flip label — no adjective the label would not carry. Headline: WE BUY / POKEMON, one sentence in Special Elite on the label strip (Special Elite's LIMIT2 cap is 16 characters; POKEMON is 7, so the face holds). Selling point one: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED. Selling point two: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. Kicker GRAILS WANTED; money line UP TO $10,000 PER CARD (bounded, per the standing rule); CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL. The items line may list Charizard, Moonbreon, alt arts, illustration rares, ETBs and WOTC — a list of what is bought is nominative. The watermark cover-up is gone. imagery now carries the CC BY-SA 2.0 attribution, prints the credit line at left 40 / top 1042, and neverShow bans covering, cropping or blurring the mark. The ShareAlike exposure the audit named but did not close is now an explicit owner gate.
The PSA label and cert 25475578: the wash is raised from 0.66 to 0.74 on both photographs and a neverShow rule bans the grading record being legible.
The 'Charizard two' variation is deleted — WEBBG.pokemon is picked as web[seed % 2] and cannot be pinned; groundSpec now says so and sets the wash for the busier photograph.
The headline colour is stated the right way round: lumHex(th.ink) < 0.35 is TRUE for both palettes (0.038, 0.039), so the headline takes th.ink, not #17171a.

Window arithmetic corrected to 1013 x 691 and 1.47:1 — and then re-measured off the asset's pixels, which showed the constant overhangs the real card by 48px top and 37px bottom. New SLAB.win and SLAB.label values are given.
A second selling-point line added: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU.
The SEALED BOOSTER BOXES rule is restated as what it actually is — a change to CATEGORY_COPY.pokemon.sub, because the MINIMUM INFORMATION backfill draws from that same array.

The LAB_SLAB dependency is resolved in the engine: the slabFrame call now honours look.ground === 'slab', so a look gets the frame on every card.

NEW: every 'cut:' and 'bg:' rule is rewritten into the forms lookFaults actually matches, and the 53-prefix block leaves only poke-slabs-trio reachable out of the 344-cutout pool.
looks.collectionNote:
WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED. The audit returned REWORK. Four themes are gone: Case Light (merged into Five Star Slab as its deep variation, which is what the audit asked for), Grade Wall and Rookie Board (no card lattice can be built in this repo), Raw And Graded (its entire canvas was the faceless asset). Two new themes replace them on grounds the old set never used: Under Glass (deep) and Step Sheet (paper, on stepsFlow).

THE POOL, OPENED AND MEASURED. assets/approved-assets.json approves 349 cutouts; okCut drops 5 more by LEGACY, so the live pool is 344 (the file's own note still says 360/104 and is stale). Exactly THREE of the 344 are cards: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products and kept as slab frames, and only sports-slab-graded is loaded (CUTOUT_ELS is built from the approved list plus that one file). I opened all four:
- poke-slabs-trio (1794x1831) — three LANDSCAPE acrylic cases, blank white labels, flat peach/mint/pink rectangles where the card face would be. No Pokemon, no card, no text.
- sports-slabs-stack (1843x1328) — four portrait holders fanned. The label is a WHITE panel inside a thin RED OUTLINE, not a filled red bar; two of the four holders are completely empty and two hold blank cream cards. No card face. (The old set's "red label bars are the only warm colour and must survive the veil" was wrong about the asset: at 670px cast width that outline is about 5px, and under a veil it is not a colour note.)
- sports-slab (523x215) — the only asset in the repo showing a real card: a PSA-slabbed basketball card at a steep low angle, with a real grading label.
- sports-slab-graded (1572x1425) — the empty front-on holder used as the frame. I measured its panels off the pixels: the white LABEL runs y 0.074-0.259, x 0.063-0.939; the white CARD in the window runs y 0.354-0.916, x 0.074-0.924.
In assets/bg-web there are ZERO sports photographs and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard, CC BY-SA 2.0, Romer Jed Medina, NYCC 2021, carrying a HAKURO PHOTOGRAPHY studio mark bottom-right.

THE WALL DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE COLLECTION IS NAMED FOR IT. The tile ground pools the deck's cuts plus the subject's whole approved shelf, strips MULTI, keeps cutouts >=240px wide and gates at pool.length >= 4. Pokemon yields ZERO — poke-slabs-trio matches -trio\b in MULTI, which still stands in front of the newer ^qs-/^ip-group-/^iphone-(pair|trio|...) clauses. Sports yields TWO (sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack) against a gate of four. Relaxing the count gate does nothing for Pokemon, and even with both gates fixed the cell is 235 x 322.7 portrait while every card object here is a landscape band, leaving 116-240px of slack per cell. So there is no lattice here. The "wall" the collection is named for is the shop's slab case: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window.

FOUR GROUNDS, NOT SEVEN. slab 2, cast 2, paper 3, deep 1. Paper carries three because a drawn sheet is the only ground where this repo's card supply — one small specimen — is the right size, and the three differ by what is written on the sheet: a want list, a review, and a worked process.

THE RULE GRAMMAR, WHICH THE OLD SET GOT WRONG ON EVERY THEME. lookFaults() is the matcher. It ignores any entry containing a space unless it begins ground: or treat:. It understands exactly four forms: a bare cutout-name prefix (literal startsWith on the basename, no extension); "assets/..." matched against the background src; "ground:<slab|tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|flat>"; and "logo:<prefix of the layer src>", where a placed wordmark's src is "logo:assets/logos/<file>.png:<colour>". So every "cut:" entry in the original ten was a no-op, every "bg:assets/..." entry was a no-op, and "logo:psa" would not have matched even if a psa.png existed. Every rule below is rewritten in the forms the matcher reads. A fault re-seeds the card on attempt 0 and prints a SUBJECT warning on attempt 1, so a correct rule really does stop a mismatched card.

I TESTED THE RULES AGAINST THE POOL. For each theme I ran all 344 approved cutouts against its neverShow. The residue — what can still reach the card — is exactly poke-slabs-trio for the Pokemon themes, and sports-slab plus sports-slabs-stack for the sports themes. Nothing else survives. The 53-prefix block that does this is identical on every theme so it can be diffed; it closes the holes subjectFaults leaves, which are large: SUBJECTS.pokemon.never is /^(iphone|ip-|qs-|ipad|mac|watch|sam-|pix-|gold-|silver-|coin-|strip-|sports-|car-)/i, and 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, 'watch' does not match apple-watch-single, and nothing there stops android-trio, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, cash-fan, handshake-deal or tv-flatscreen. Eighty non-card cutouts passed the old rules.

WHAT THE RULES CANNOT DO, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. (1) mustShow is skipped entirely when a card carries no cutout layer, so it can never require that a product is present — only constrain which one is. (2) "sports-slab" is a literal prefix of "sports-slabs-stack" and "sports-slab-graded", so the 523px slab cannot be excluded by prefix without excluding the sports themes' own hero; it is excluded in code instead (it is absent from CATEGORY_COPY.sports.cuts so it is never cutSrc) and the one place it still reaches a card — the slab window's seed % 2 pick — is named as a required change on both slab themes. (3) groundNow has no 'paper' and no 'deep' value, so a look declaring either faults on every card; 16 approved looks already declare 'paper' and 5 declare 'deep', so this is a matcher gap, not a theme error, and the one-line fix is named in each groundSpec.

ONE SENTENCE, ONE FACE — WHERE IT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. Nearly every layout in app.js sets Headline 2 as a gradient (grad c1:P.a1, c2:P.a2) against a flat Headline 1 — checklistHero, trustSeal, reviewProof, stepsFlow, bandKnockout, arcCrown, voltStack, gradientWave, hudTech all do — and retheme() only re-colours that gradient, it never removes it. Two paths remove it: slabFrame(), which forces every headline to one flat near-black and locks it, and the Lined Paper family, which deletes the gradient but then fills headlines by layer-index parity (k % 2 === 0 ? pen : '#26231f'), so the sentence comes out in two colours instead. So the slab themes satisfy the rule as shipped; the paper themes satisfy it once both headline layers are forced to the pen colour (one line, named in every paper theme); the cast and deep themes need the gradient flattened, also named. No theme here claims the rule is met when it is not.

THE MARK LAW. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji whatever the palette. ELEMENTS_FAMILY covers only 'Lined Paper', which swaps them for [accent, ink, accent] and drops the emoji. So every Pokemon theme here is either on a Lined Paper palette or carries the ELEMENTS_FAMILY requirement in its own rules. ELEMENTS.sports.colors is null, so the sports themes take the palette's own colours and have no such problem — which, with sports-slabs-stack being the better object, is why the set leans sports.

TWO ENGINE TRAPS THE AUDIT DID NOT REACH. (a) On a slab card the deck's cutout is NOT removed: line 3428 filters Hero Product only when t2.__castBg, and slabFrame runs after it, so the product is painted into the window by the ground AND scaled into the same window as a live cutout on top of the copy. The fix is the same one line the cast branch already has, applied to __slab. (b) The SPEC CHIP GRID (retheme_lab.mjs ~893) is not category-gated: its CHIPS array is phone copy — ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK — and it fires on any card whose last band is >=96px tall. On a card ad that is nonsense, and it is banned in prose on every theme here.

THE PASSES. Slab themes need LAB_LOOKS=1 with LAB_SLABGRADE=stars for Five Star Slab and LAB_SLABGRADE=num for Gem Label and the Case variation — the flag is process-global, so the two grade blocks cannot share a run. Under Glass needs LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet. Everything else runs in the default looks pass. The random slab trigger is already fixed in the engine: the call now reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)), so a look owns its ground and the audit's repeated "one card in three is a slab card" finding no longer applies to any theme that belongs to a look.

COPY LAW. A list of what is bought is nominative and may name grails; a claim line must be backed by the picture. Two of the three card cutouts show no card face, so no theme whose picture is an empty holder may name a grail in a claim, and only Gem Label — whose window holds a photograph of a real graded Charizard — may say Charizard. Money lines stay bounded (UP TO $10,000 / UP TO $5,000 PER CARD). Competitors come only from CHALLENGE's own rosters and never take an apostrophe-S. Every card carries at least two selling-point lines besides the items line and the CTA. Five stars, never four, never six. And stepsFlow is barred from the sports deck everywhere in this set: its 'CASH IN' rewrite takes the first word of deck.h2, so a sports card prints SELL SPORTS.

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a graded item: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window — printed on the slab frame, drawn on a sheet, or lit in a case.

looks.name: Five Star Slab
looks.oneLine: The same graded frame turned to sports: WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS stencilled on the label, four empty red-edged holders fitted whole into the window, and five stars over TOP RATED where the grade number would be.
looks.groundSpec:
Same frame and the same corrected geometry as Gem Label — dw 1191.4, ox -55.7, label x 33.7 / w 1012.7, window x 33.7 / w 1012.7 — including the same required correction of SLAB.win to [0.075,0.354,0.924,0.916] and SLAB.label to [0.075,0.074,0.924,0.259], measured off the asset. slabFrame fires on every card because the look declares ground 'slab'.

WHAT DIFFERS IS THE WINDOW. WEBBG.sports is EMPTY — there is not one sports photograph in assets/bg-web; the eight sports files all sit in bg-web-rejected — so slabFrame falls to its cutout branch, sets __cut, and FITS rather than covers: k = min((WB.w-60)/iw, (WB.h-60)/ih), then a lighter rgba(c1,0.55) wash. sports-slabs-stack at 1843x1328 gives k = 0.475, so 875 x 631 sitting whole inside the window with air around it, crisp, no crop.

THE BUG THAT BREAKS THIS THEME ON HALF ITS CARDS. slabFrame's sports branch is `names = ['sports-slabs-stack','sports-slab']` and the pick is `[seed % 2]`. Both files are approved and both are in CUTOUT_ELS, so on odd seeds the window holds sports-slab — 523 x 215 — fitted at k = min(952.7/523, 631.2/215) = 1.822, i.e. blown up to 953 x 392. That is a 1.8x enlargement of the smallest asset in the pool, and it carries a real PSA grading label that becomes semi-legible at that size. REQUIRED, and this theme does not ship until it lands: the sports branch reads `const el = CUTOUT_ELS['assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp']` with no seed alternation. The rule cannot be written as a neverShow prefix, because 'sports-slab' is a literal prefix of 'sports-slabs-stack'.

THE GRADE BLOCK, AND WHY IT NEEDS ITS OWN PASS. starGrade = FACESYS.slabGrade ? FACESYS.slabGrade === 'stars' : seed % 2 === 1. LAB_SLABGRADE is process-global, so a run cannot carry two grade blocks: this theme runs with LAB_SLABGRADE=stars, and Gem Label plus the Case variation run in a separate pass with LAB_SLABGRADE=num. The stars are set in Satoshi at fontSize round(LB.h*0.22) with charSpacing 60, over TOP RATED at 0.10 with charSpacing 180, and take th.accent only when lumHex(accent) < 0.62: ca07 #d8360a is 0.173 and ca05 #a16f12 is 0.190, so both take the accent. That test is exactly why the Case variation is a NUMBER slab.

THE PALETTES ARE PALE. ca07 #b9f7f6 (lum 0.835) and ca05 #d4eeff (0.824), so the 0.55 wash is a pale aqua veil. Both inks clear the 0.35 test (#173f3f at 0.041, #1f3c4c at 0.040), so the label headline takes the ink and slabFrame strips its gradient, shadow and stroke — one sentence, one face, one colour, delivered rather than claimed. Big Shoulders Stencil Display is in NO_ACCENT and capped at 14 characters by LIMIT2; SPORTS CARDS is 12, so the stencil holds.

The hero-drawn-twice fix applies here too: `if (t2.__slab)` must filter Hero Product / Lineup Product, or sports-slabs-stack is drawn into the window by the ground and then scaled into the same window again as a live cutout.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/sports-slab-graded.webp as the frame. In the window: assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp, fitted whole. looks.collectionNote:
WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED. The audit returned REWORK. Four themes are gone: Case Light (merged into Five Star Slab as its deep variation, which is what the audit asked for), Grade Wall and Rookie Board (no card lattice can be built in this repo), Raw And Graded (its entire canvas was the faceless asset). Two new themes replace them on grounds the old set never used: Under Glass (deep) and Step Sheet (paper, on stepsFlow).

THE POOL, OPENED AND MEASURED. assets/approved-assets.json approves 349 cutouts; okCut drops 5 more by LEGACY, so the live pool is 344 (the file's own note still says 360/104 and is stale). Exactly THREE of the 344 are cards: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products and kept as slab frames, and only sports-slab-graded is loaded (CUTOUT_ELS is built from the approved list plus that one file). I opened all four:
- poke-slabs-trio (1794x1831) — three LANDSCAPE acrylic cases, blank white labels, flat peach/mint/pink rectangles where the card face would be. No Pokemon, no card, no text.
- sports-slabs-stack (1843x1328) — four portrait holders fanned. The label is a WHITE panel inside a thin RED OUTLINE, not a filled red bar; two of the four holders are completely empty and two hold blank cream cards. No card face. (The old set's "red label bars are the only warm colour and must survive the veil" was wrong about the asset: at 670px cast width that outline is about 5px, and under a veil it is not a colour note.)
- sports-slab (523x215) — the only asset in the repo showing a real card: a PSA-slabbed basketball card at a steep low angle, with a real grading label.
- sports-slab-graded (1572x1425) — the empty front-on holder used as the frame. I measured its panels off the pixels: the white LABEL runs y 0.074-0.259, x 0.063-0.939; the white CARD in the window runs y 0.354-0.916, x 0.074-0.924.
In assets/bg-web there are ZERO sports photographs and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard, CC BY-SA 2.0, Romer Jed Medina, NYCC 2021, carrying a HAKURO PHOTOGRAPHY studio mark bottom-right.

THE WALL DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE COLLECTION IS NAMED FOR IT. The tile ground pools the deck's cuts plus the subject's whole approved shelf, strips MULTI, keeps cutouts >=240px wide and gates at pool.length >= 4. Pokemon yields ZERO — poke-slabs-trio matches -trio\b in MULTI, which still stands in front of the newer ^qs-/^ip-group-/^iphone-(pair|trio|...) clauses. Sports yields TWO (sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack) against a gate of four. Relaxing the count gate does nothing for Pokemon, and even with both gates fixed the cell is 235 x 322.7 portrait while every card object here is a landscape band, leaving 116-240px of slack per cell. So there is no lattice here. The "wall" the collection is named for is the shop's slab case: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window.

FOUR GROUNDS, NOT SEVEN. slab 2, cast 2, paper 3, deep 1. Paper carries three because a drawn sheet is the only ground where this repo's card supply — one small specimen — is the right size, and the three differ by what is written on the sheet: a want list, a review, and a worked process.

THE RULE GRAMMAR, WHICH THE OLD SET GOT WRONG ON EVERY THEME. lookFaults() is the matcher. It ignores any entry containing a space unless it begins ground: or treat:. It understands exactly four forms: a bare cutout-name prefix (literal startsWith on the basename, no extension); "assets/..." matched against the background src; "ground:<slab|tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|flat>"; and "logo:<prefix of the layer src>", where a placed wordmark's src is "logo:assets/logos/<file>.png:<colour>". So every "cut:" entry in the original ten was a no-op, every "bg:assets/..." entry was a no-op, and "logo:psa" would not have matched even if a psa.png existed. Every rule below is rewritten in the forms the matcher reads. A fault re-seeds the card on attempt 0 and prints a SUBJECT warning on attempt 1, so a correct rule really does stop a mismatched card.

I TESTED THE RULES AGAINST THE POOL. For each theme I ran all 344 approved cutouts against its neverShow. The residue — what can still reach the card — is exactly poke-slabs-trio for the Pokemon themes, and sports-slab plus sports-slabs-stack for the sports themes. Nothing else survives. The 53-prefix block that does this is identical on every theme so it can be diffed; it closes the holes subjectFaults leaves, which are large: SUBJECTS.pokemon.never is /^(iphone|ip-|qs-|ipad|mac|watch|sam-|pix-|gold-|silver-|coin-|strip-|sports-|car-)/i, and 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, 'watch' does not match apple-watch-single, and nothing there stops android-trio, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, cash-fan, handshake-deal or tv-flatscreen. Eighty non-card cutouts passed the old rules.

WHAT THE RULES CANNOT DO, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. (1) mustShow is skipped entirely when a card carries no cutout layer, so it can never require that a product is present — only constrain which one is. (2) "sports-slab" is a literal prefix of "sports-slabs-stack" and "sports-slab-graded", so the 523px slab cannot be excluded by prefix without excluding the sports themes' own hero; it is excluded in code instead (it is absent from CATEGORY_COPY.sports.cuts so it is never cutSrc) and the one place it still reaches a card — the slab window's seed % 2 pick — is named as a required change on both slab themes. (3) groundNow has no 'paper' and no 'deep' value, so a look declaring either faults on every card; 16 approved looks already declare 'paper' and 5 declare 'deep', so this is a matcher gap, not a theme error, and the one-line fix is named in each groundSpec.

ONE SENTENCE, ONE FACE — WHERE IT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. Nearly every layout in app.js sets Headline 2 as a gradient (grad c1:P.a1, c2:P.a2) against a flat Headline 1 — checklistHero, trustSeal, reviewProof, stepsFlow, bandKnockout, arcCrown, voltStack, gradientWave, hudTech all do — and retheme() only re-colours that gradient, it never removes it. Two paths remove it: slabFrame(), which forces every headline to one flat near-black and locks it, and the Lined Paper family, which deletes the gradient but then fills headlines by layer-index parity (k % 2 === 0 ? pen : '#26231f'), so the sentence comes out in two colours instead. So the slab themes satisfy the rule as shipped; the paper themes satisfy it once both headline layers are forced to the pen colour (one line, named in every paper theme); the cast and deep themes need the gradient flattened, also named. No theme here claims the rule is met when it is not.

THE MARK LAW. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji whatever the palette. ELEMENTS_FAMILY covers only 'Lined Paper', which swaps them for [accent, ink, accent] and drops the emoji. So every Pokemon theme here is either on a Lined Paper palette or carries the ELEMENTS_FAMILY requirement in its own rules. ELEMENTS.sports.colors is null, so the sports themes take the palette's own colours and have no such problem — which, with sports-slabs-stack being the better object, is why the set leans sports.

TWO ENGINE TRAPS THE AUDIT DID NOT REACH. (a) On a slab card the deck's cutout is NOT removed: line 3428 filters Hero Product only when t2.__castBg, and slabFrame runs after it, so the product is painted into the window by the ground AND scaled into the same window as a live cutout on top of the copy. The fix is the same one line the cast branch already has, applied to __slab. (b) The SPEC CHIP GRID (retheme_lab.mjs ~893) is not category-gated: its CHIPS array is phone copy — ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK — and it fires on any card whose last band is >=96px tall. On a card ad that is nonsense, and it is banned in prose on every theme here.

THE PASSES. Slab themes need LAB_LOOKS=1 with LAB_SLABGRADE=stars for Five Star Slab and LAB_SLABGRADE=num for Gem Label and the Case variation — the flag is process-global, so the two grade blocks cannot share a run. Under Glass needs LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet. Everything else runs in the default looks pass. The random slab trigger is already fixed in the engine: the call now reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)), so a look owns its ground and the audit's repeated "one card in three is a slab card" finding no longer applies to any theme that belongs to a look.

COPY LAW. A list of what is bought is nominative and may name grails; a claim line must be backed by the picture. Two of the three card cutouts show no card face, so no theme whose picture is an empty holder may name a grail in a claim, and only Gem Label — whose window holds a photograph of a real graded Charizard — may say Charizard. Money lines stay bounded (UP TO $10,000 / UP TO $5,000 PER CARD). Competitors come only from CHALLENGE's own rosters and never take an apostrophe-S. Every card carries at least two selling-point lines besides the items line and the CTA. Five stars, never four, never six. And stepsFlow is barred from the sports deck everywhere in this set: its 'CASH IN' rewrite takes the first word of deck.h2, so a sports card prints SELL SPORTS.

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a graded item: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window — printed on the slab frame, drawn on a sheet, or lit in a case.

looks.name: Cert Cast
looks.oneLine: One slab drawn large into a near-white blueprint field, with every numeral on the card — the money line, the phone number, the rules — set in JetBrains Mono as a single cert-document typographic system; no other theme in the set sets its numbers as a system.
looks.groundSpec:
The cast ground, pale branch: ck09 #f3f8fa (lum 0.931) and pp07 #eff7fe (0.920) both clear 0.55. Sequence, read out of the code: fill c1; rgba(ink,0.20) over the whole card so a near-white ground does not read as the blank 'what is this light theme' card; a vertical gradient from rgba(accent,0.18) to rgba(ink,0.10); a white sheen from 0.12 to transparent across the top-left 55%. The product is placed at 0.66W / 0.52H, rotated -0.12rad, at k = min(669.6/iw, 993.6/ih), alpha 0.92, with an rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur-40 shadow offset 24/30 — 670x684 for poke-slabs-trio, 670x483 for sports-slabs-stack, both downscaled from a larger source and crisp. Over that the window shadow: a blur-26 rgba(8,10,16,0.58) wedge from 0.62W at the top to 0.22W at the bottom, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half strength. Final scrim: scrimC resolves to th.ink on both palettes at 0.30. Because both accents are blue (#0c658d, #0378c7) the card reads as a blueprint or a cert document, which is the point.

THE CAST GROUND REMOVES THE PRODUCT LAYER. Line 3428: `if (t2.__castBg) t2.layers = t2.layers.filter(l => !/^Hero Product|^Lineup Product/.test(l.name));` — so the cast product IS the picture and there is no cutout layer left on the card. Two consequences to be honest about: the cutout rules below cannot bite on a card that carries no cutout, and mustShow is skipped entirely in that state (lookFaults only runs the mustShow test when names.length is non-zero). What actually binds this theme is ground:, assets/ and logo:.

THE SLAB TRIGGER IS NO LONGER A PROBLEM. The audit found this theme overwritten by slabFrame one card in three. The call site now reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)) — the random arm is gated on !look, so a locked look never gets it. No code change is needed here any more; the requirement is only that this theme is rendered as a look and never with LAB_SLAB=1 set.

WHAT THIS GROUND DOES NOT DO. It does not flatten Headline 2. checklistHero, trustSeal and reviewProof all set Headline 2 as grad{c1:P.a1, c2:P.a2} against a flat Headline 1, and retheme() re-colours that gradient rather than removing it. REQUIRED for one-sentence-one-colour on this theme: delete props.grad on every headline layer and set them all to th.ink after the cast ground is built. The panel pass over __castBg already forces every plate to rgba(deep,0.9) with a single copy colour, which is what keeps the small mono type legible — do not fight that.

Audiowide is in NO_ACCENT, so the engine strips the accent and this theme prints POKEMON, not the accented form.

looks.copy: Technical and exact, the voice of a written offer. Headline: WE BUY / POKEMON or WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS in Audiowide, two words a line, never more. Selling point one: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED (Pokemon) or PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW (sports). Selling point two: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. The mono numerals carry the money line — UP TO $10,000 PER CARD or UP TO $5,000 PER CARD — and (562) 999-4994, and those are the only numbers on the card: no invented cert or population figures, because we cannot back them. The items line may list Charizard, Moonbreon and alt arts, or rookies, autos and numbered /99; a claim line may not, because the picture is an empty holder.
variations: Blueprint (ck09) — Chalk, #0c658d on #f3f8fa with the near-black support; the cleanest, and the best read of the mono system.
Document (pp07) — Paper, #0378c7 with the #c0765f terracotta kept to the rules only; warmer, and the better fit on the sports run.
Shadow long — push the window-shadow wedge origin from 0.62W to 0.70W so the light comes in flatter and the slab sits in more of it.
fixesApplied: The slabFrame-overwrite problem is resolved in the engine, not by a rule: the sd % 3 arm is now gated on !look, so a locked look keeps its cast ground. groundSpec states the one remaining requirement (render as a look, never with LAB_SLAB=1).
oneLine is rewritten to say what makes this theme different from every other cast card — the numerals set as one system — rather than describing the ground.
The recipe count is cut as the audit demanded: Grade Wall, Rookie Board and Raw And Graded are gone, so the cast recipe now carries two themes (this and Shop Callout) instead of six.
The locked-Pokemon-marks problem is carried as an explicit neverShow with the exact code requirement (ELEMENTS_FAMILY extended to Chalk and Paper with colors:'pen', or move the Pokemon run to lp01).

hudTech is removed and reviewProof (93% measured) takes its place; a gradient on either headline is banned, with the required flatten named — and groundSpec now says plainly that the cast ground does NOT flatten it, which is true of every layout in this repo.
NEW, beyond the audit: Audiowide is in NO_ACCENT, so this theme prints POKEMON. The audit caught this on Gem Label and Shop Callout but not here.
NEW: stepsFlow is removed — its CASH IN rewrite would print SELL SPORTS on the sports run.
NEW: the cast ground removes the product layer, so the cutout rules and mustShow cannot bite on this theme. Said out loud rather than implied.
NEW: a copy law added for the faceless assets — no grail in a claim line when the picture is an empty holder. This is the finding that cut Raw And Graded, applied consistently here.

looks.name: Shop Callout
looks.oneLine: A knockout band across a cast slab that names the buyer you already tried — WE MATCH / THE CARD SHOP — with no borrowed wordmark beside it, because the engine cannot place one.
looks.groundSpec:
Cast ground, and this is the theme where the pale/deep split genuinely changes the build. ik02 #e8f1fa (lum 0.870) takes the PALE branch: c1, then rgba(ink,0.20) over the whole card, then the accent-to-ink gradient at 0.18/0.10, the white sheen at 0.12, the window shadow at strength 0.58 with its half-strength penumbra, and a final scrim of rgba(ink,0.30). du08 #5593ef (lum 0.290) takes the DEEP branch: no ink overlay, no accent gradient, sheen at 0.10, window shadow at 0.50, final scrim rgba(c1,0.22) — a lighter veil on a stronger ground. I checked both against the code and both are exact.

The band is the loudest object either way: a knockout bar sized to the word, taking the accent (#bf3a00 or #3c3e65) with the competitor name reversed out of it. Never a full-bleed band, which turns into a slab.

THE PREMISE FIRES ON A THIRD OF THE CARDS, AND ON ONLY SOME LAYOUTS. challenge = CH && pairOK && (sd % 3 === 0), with no look override. pairOK additionally requires the DONOR TEMPLATE's own authored headline text to be one of SELL YOUR / CASH FOR / WE BUY plus a category word — so it is a property of the picked dl_ template, not of the card. That rules two layouts out completely: stepsFlow hard-codes 'CASH IN' and '3 STEPS' as literals and can never satisfy pairOK, and trustSeal hard-codes 'TRUSTED LOCAL' and 'BUYER' around its money word and has no opener at all. It also means a dl_sports_* donor fails, because DECKS.sports.h1 is 'SPORTS', not an opener. REQUIRED: gate challenge on the look (e.g. look.challenge === true) the way look.ground === 'slab' now gates slabFrame. Until that lands, this theme must be rendered at three times the count of the others and its donor templates restricted away from dl_sports_*, or two cards in three carry no competitor and read as a plain cast slab, i.e. Cert Cast.

The cast ground removes the Hero Product layer, so there is no cutout on the card and the cutout rules below are belt-and-braces. Panels over __castBg go solid at rgba(deep,0.9) automatically, which is what keeps the comparison copy legible on the deep variant. Headline 2 is still a gradient on both layouts and must be flattened to th.ink; the same requirement as Cert Cast.

Russo One is in NO_ACCENT, so this theme prints POKEMON. The brand wordmark, when one can finally be placed, inks pure white on a deep ground and #14161c on a pale one — never th.ink, which is what printed a brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes.

a wordmark beside GOLDIN or THE CARD SHOP — neither has a file in assets/logos and neither ever will
fanatics-inc on a POKEMON headline, or tcgplayer or gamestop on a SPORTS CARDS headline

looks.copy: Comparative and specific, never a superlative — we name who, and we say what we do differently. Kicker: LOWBALLED BY TCGPLAYER? Headline: WE MATCH / THE CARD SHOP — no apostrophe-S, ever. CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker ON THE SPOT. looks.name: Want List
looks.oneLine: The buyer's want list written on a ruled sheet in pen, the items line broken into a real checklist, and one slab taped into the margin as a specimen.
looks.groundSpec:
A drawn sheet, not a photograph, and I read the drawing code. paper:ruled is #fbf7ea stock with 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px starting at y=150, a 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes at 18%, 50% and 82% height (a rgba(0,0,0,0.10) ring at (52, y+3) r15 under a #eef0f2 hole at (50, y) r15), 9000 fibre specks of 2x2px at up to 3.5% black, and a binding shadow from rgba(0,0,0,0.10) to transparent across the top 70px. keepColour is true for paper:, so the sheet is never greyscaled or tinted.

THE SHEET CANNOT BE PINNED. familyTreatment picks it as ['paper:ruled','paper:legal','paper:grid','paper:dots','paper:ruled'][seed % 5] — ruled on 2 cards in 5, and legal, grid and dots on 1 in 5 each. There is no env flag and no look field that selects it. So the theme is designed against all four, and the pen weight and the tick weight are set against paper:legal (#fff3b8, a yellow legal pad with rules at 54px from y=130 and no holes), which is the loudest of the four and the binding case. paper:grid is #f7f9fb with 1.4px #b9cbe2 at 48px; paper:dots is #fbfaf5 with 2.2px #b3bbc7 dots at 44px.

THE PALETTE PAINTS THE PEN, NOT THE GROUND. Both palettes are Lined Paper family, which is the whole reason for this theme: ELEMENTS_FAMILY['Lined Paper'] replaces the locked Pokemon #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 marks with [accent, ink, accent] and sets noEmoji, so a Pokemon card here gets hand-drawn marks in #084f88 or #920c03 and no emoji at all. It is the only documented way to run a Pokemon card without brand-colour confetti, and it makes this the one theme in the set equally safe on both categories.

WHAT ELSE THE FAMILY DOES, BUDGETED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED. Every rect under 130x130 takes the pen colour at rx 8, angle 0, locked. Every band or pill 200-210px tall and >=200px wide becomes a HIGHLIGHTER from HIGHLIGHT ['#fff59d','#ffd6e7','#c9f5c4','#cfe8ff','#ffe0b3','#e8d7ff'] at opacity 0.55, rx h*0.18, angle up to 0.8deg, plus a second Marker Overrun stroke at 0.3 offset by up to 22px so the ends run over like a real marker. Every larger panel becomes a STICKY from ['#fff3a0','#ffd9e6','#d3f7d0','#d6ebff','#ffe4bf'] at opacity 0.96 with a 22px shadow and a 1.2deg tilt. Every circle takes the pen. Every sheen, vignette and grain goes to opacity 0. Headlines get a tilt of up to 1.2deg. On a ruled or legal sheet, single-line copy is baseline-snapped to the 54px grid and row type is capped at 40px so it sits between the rules. BUDGET: one highlighter on the money line, one sticky under the list, nothing else.

THE ONE-SENTENCE BREAK, AND ITS FIX. familyTreatment sets headline fill by layer-index parity: l.props.fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : '#26231f'. WE BUY and POKEMON therefore come out in two different colours on roughly half the cards. REQUIRED: force both headline layers to the pen colour before paint. Note the family does delete the gradient, so this is the only break left.

TWO MATCHER GAPS TO KNOW ABOUT. groundNow has no 'paper' value — a paper sheet sets t2.bg.src to 'paper:ruled' and falls through to 'flat' — so this look faults on every card with 'ground flat but the theme is paper'. Sixteen approved looks in this repo already declare 'paper', so it is a matcher gap; the one-line fix is to map a bg src starting 'paper:' to 'paper' in groundNow. And the slab-overwrite the audit flagged is gone: the sd % 3 arm is now gated on !look.

This is the theme where the blankness of those two files stops mattering, and that is not an excuse — it is the design. I opened them: three empty acrylic cases with pastel inserts, and four empty holders with red-edged labels. At 260px pinned in a margin, an empty holder reads as a SPECIMEN of the thing being bought — this is the case your cards come back in — rather than as an unbranded product filling the frame. It is the only ground in the set where the object supply this repo actually has is the right size for the picture.
mustShow: ground:paper — a drawn sheet, one of paper:ruled, paper:legal, paper:grid or paper:dots; the engine cycles all four by seed % 5 and cannot be pinned, so the list must read on every one of them
a Lined Paper palette (lp01 or lp07), so the decorative marks take the pen and the emoji are dropped
the items line broken into a real checklist, one entry per rule, with a pen tick
neverShow: poke-slabs-trio and sports-slabs-stack on the same card

a deep palette — it has no meaning on a drawn sheet
headline lines in two colours — the family sets headline fill by layer-index parity (pen on even, #26231f on odd); both headline layers must be forced to the pen colour before paint
more than one highlighter band and one sticky note on a card — the family will make one out of every panel it is given
the specimen slab larger than 320px, or cast into the ground — at hero size an empty holder stops reading as a specimen
spec chips from the engine's CHIPS grid (ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK) — that array is phone copy and is not category-gated
layout:stepsFlow — its CASH IN rewrite takes the first word of deck.h2 and prints SELL SPORTS on the sports run
layout:bandKnockout, layout:arcCrown, layout:neonNight, layout:gradientWave, layout:ticketStub, layout:glassCard, layout:hudTech, layout:slabPoster, layout:voltStack
a handwriting face on body copy
a grading company's name or mark

looks.copy: Written, not proclaimed — the voice of someone who keeps a list. Headline: WE BUY / POKEMON or WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS in Zilla Slab, sitting on a rule as if it were written on the line. Selling point one: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED (Pokemon) or PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW (sports). Selling point two: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. Money line UP TO $10,000 PER CARD or UP TO $5,000 PER CARD, CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker FREE QUOTE.
variations: Blue pen (lp01) — #084f88 ink with the #9d8518 gold on the ticks; the default, and the calmest on the yellow legal sheet.
