fixesApplied: mustShow 'paper:ruled or paper:grid' is replaced by a rule that reads on all four sheets, and groundSpec states that familyTreatment cycles them by seed % 5 and cannot be pinned, with the pen and tick weights set against paper:legal as the binding case.
The 'Graph paper' variation is deleted — it described a swap that is not settable — and replaced by a two-column variation that is.
The slab-overwrite is resolved in the engine (the sd % 3 arm is gated on !look), so no rule is needed for it.

The full Lined Paper budget is written into groundSpec: highlighter bands with their Marker Overrun second stroke, sticky plates with a 22px shadow, pen fill on every small box and circle, the headline tilt, opacity 0 on every sheen and vignette, and the baseline snap to the 54px rule grid.
The index-parity headline break is a neverShow with the exact fix (force both headline layers to the pen colour before paint).
NEW: stepsFlow is removed from the layouts — on the sports run its CASH IN rewrite prints SELL SPORTS.
NEW: groundNow has no 'paper' value, so this look faults on every card until a bg src starting 'paper:' maps to 'paper'. Named rather than left as noise.

NEW: the rules are rewritten in the matcher's real grammar and tested against the 344-cutout pool — only the two card keepers survive. This is the theme where that matters most, because paper is the one ground that keeps a live cutout layer on the card.
looks.collectionNote:
WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED. The audit returned REWORK. Four themes are gone: Case Light (merged into Five Star Slab as its deep variation, which is what the audit asked for), Grade Wall and Rookie Board (no card lattice can be built in this repo), Raw And Graded (its entire canvas was the faceless asset). Two new themes replace them on grounds the old set never used: Under Glass (deep) and Step Sheet (paper, on stepsFlow).

THE POOL, OPENED AND MEASURED. assets/approved-assets.json approves 349 cutouts; okCut drops 5 more by LEGACY, so the live pool is 344 (the file's own note still says 360/104 and is stale). Exactly THREE of the 344 are cards: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products and kept as slab frames, and only sports-slab-graded is loaded (CUTOUT_ELS is built from the approved list plus that one file). I opened all four:
- poke-slabs-trio (1794x1831) — three LANDSCAPE acrylic cases, blank white labels, flat peach/mint/pink rectangles where the card face would be. No Pokemon, no card, no text.
- sports-slabs-stack (1843x1328) — four portrait holders fanned. The label is a WHITE panel inside a thin RED OUTLINE, not a filled red bar; two of the four holders are completely empty and two hold blank cream cards. No card face. (The old set's "red label bars are the only warm colour and must survive the veil" was wrong about the asset: at 670px cast width that outline is about 5px, and under a veil it is not a colour note.)
- sports-slab (523x215) — the only asset in the repo showing a real card: a PSA-slabbed basketball card at a steep low angle, with a real grading label.
- sports-slab-graded (1572x1425) — the empty front-on holder used as the frame. I measured its panels off the pixels: the white LABEL runs y 0.074-0.259, x 0.063-0.939; the white CARD in the window runs y 0.354-0.916, x 0.074-0.924.
In assets/bg-web there are ZERO sports photographs and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard, CC BY-SA 2.0, Romer Jed Medina, NYCC 2021, carrying a HAKURO PHOTOGRAPHY studio mark bottom-right.

THE WALL DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE COLLECTION IS NAMED FOR IT. The tile ground pools the deck's cuts plus the subject's whole approved shelf, strips MULTI, keeps cutouts >=240px wide and gates at pool.length >= 4. Pokemon yields ZERO — poke-slabs-trio matches -trio\b in MULTI, which still stands in front of the newer ^qs-/^ip-group-/^iphone-(pair|trio|...) clauses. Sports yields TWO (sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack) against a gate of four. Relaxing the count gate does nothing for Pokemon, and even with both gates fixed the cell is 235 x 322.7 portrait while every card object here is a landscape band, leaving 116-240px of slack per cell. So there is no lattice here. The "wall" the collection is named for is the shop's slab case: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window.

FOUR GROUNDS, NOT SEVEN. slab 2, cast 2, paper 3, deep 1. Paper carries three because a drawn sheet is the only ground where this repo's card supply — one small specimen — is the right size, and the three differ by what is written on the sheet: a want list, a review, and a worked process.

THE RULE GRAMMAR, WHICH THE OLD SET GOT WRONG ON EVERY THEME. lookFaults() is the matcher. It ignores any entry containing a space unless it begins ground: or treat:. It understands exactly four forms: a bare cutout-name prefix (literal startsWith on the basename, no extension); "assets/..." matched against the background src; "ground:<slab|tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|flat>"; and "logo:<prefix of the layer src>", where a placed wordmark's src is "logo:assets/logos/<file>.png:<colour>". So every "cut:" entry in the original ten was a no-op, every "bg:assets/..." entry was a no-op, and "logo:psa" would not have matched even if a psa.png existed. Every rule below is rewritten in the forms the matcher reads. A fault re-seeds the card on attempt 0 and prints a SUBJECT warning on attempt 1, so a correct rule really does stop a mismatched card.

I TESTED THE RULES AGAINST THE POOL. For each theme I ran all 344 approved cutouts against its neverShow. The residue — what can still reach the card — is exactly poke-slabs-trio for the Pokemon themes, and sports-slab plus sports-slabs-stack for the sports themes. Nothing else survives. The 53-prefix block that does this is identical on every theme so it can be diffed; it closes the holes subjectFaults leaves, which are large: SUBJECTS.pokemon.never is /^(iphone|ip-|qs-|ipad|mac|watch|sam-|pix-|gold-|silver-|coin-|strip-|sports-|car-)/i, and 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, 'watch' does not match apple-watch-single, and nothing there stops android-trio, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, cash-fan, handshake-deal or tv-flatscreen. Eighty non-card cutouts passed the old rules.

WHAT THE RULES CANNOT DO, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. (1) mustShow is skipped entirely when a card carries no cutout layer, so it can never require that a product is present — only constrain which one is. (2) "sports-slab" is a literal prefix of "sports-slabs-stack" and "sports-slab-graded", so the 523px slab cannot be excluded by prefix without excluding the sports themes' own hero; it is excluded in code instead (it is absent from CATEGORY_COPY.sports.cuts so it is never cutSrc) and the one place it still reaches a card — the slab window's seed % 2 pick — is named as a required change on both slab themes. (3) groundNow has no 'paper' and no 'deep' value, so a look declaring either faults on every card; 16 approved looks already declare 'paper' and 5 declare 'deep', so this is a matcher gap, not a theme error, and the one-line fix is named in each groundSpec.

ONE SENTENCE, ONE FACE — WHERE IT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. Nearly every layout in app.js sets Headline 2 as a gradient (grad c1:P.a1, c2:P.a2) against a flat Headline 1 — checklistHero, trustSeal, reviewProof, stepsFlow, bandKnockout, arcCrown, voltStack, gradientWave, hudTech all do — and retheme() only re-colours that gradient, it never removes it. Two paths remove it: slabFrame(), which forces every headline to one flat near-black and locks it, and the Lined Paper family, which deletes the gradient but then fills headlines by layer-index parity (k % 2 === 0 ? pen : '#26231f'), so the sentence comes out in two colours instead. So the slab themes satisfy the rule as shipped; the paper themes satisfy it once both headline layers are forced to the pen colour (one line, named in every paper theme); the cast and deep themes need the gradient flattened, also named. No theme here claims the rule is met when it is not.

THE MARK LAW. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji whatever the palette. ELEMENTS_FAMILY covers only 'Lined Paper', which swaps them for [accent, ink, accent] and drops the emoji. So every Pokemon theme here is either on a Lined Paper palette or carries the ELEMENTS_FAMILY requirement in its own rules. ELEMENTS.sports.colors is null, so the sports themes take the palette's own colours and have no such problem — which, with sports-slabs-stack being the better object, is why the set leans sports.

TWO ENGINE TRAPS THE AUDIT DID NOT REACH. (a) On a slab card the deck's cutout is NOT removed: line 3428 filters Hero Product only when t2.__castBg, and slabFrame runs after it, so the product is painted into the window by the ground AND scaled into the same window as a live cutout on top of the copy. The fix is the same one line the cast branch already has, applied to __slab. (b) The SPEC CHIP GRID (retheme_lab.mjs ~893) is not category-gated: its CHIPS array is phone copy — ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK — and it fires on any card whose last band is >=96px tall. On a card ad that is nonsense, and it is banned in prose on every theme here.

THE PASSES. Slab themes need LAB_LOOKS=1 with LAB_SLABGRADE=stars for Five Star Slab and LAB_SLABGRADE=num for Gem Label and the Case variation — the flag is process-global, so the two grade blocks cannot share a run. Under Glass needs LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet. Everything else runs in the default looks pass. The random slab trigger is already fixed in the engine: the call now reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)), so a look owns its ground and the audit's repeated "one card in three is a slab card" finding no longer applies to any theme that belongs to a look.

COPY LAW. A list of what is bought is nominative and may name grails; a claim line must be backed by the picture. Two of the three card cutouts show no card face, so no theme whose picture is an empty holder may name a grail in a claim, and only Gem Label — whose window holds a photograph of a real graded Charizard — may say Charizard. Money lines stay bounded (UP TO $10,000 / UP TO $5,000 PER CARD). Competitors come only from CHALLENGE's own rosters and never take an apostrophe-S. Every card carries at least two selling-point lines besides the items line and the CTA. Five stars, never four, never six. And stepsFlow is barred from the sports deck everywhere in this set: its 'CASH IN' rewrite takes the first word of deck.h2, so a sports card prints SELL SPORTS.

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a graded item: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window — printed on the slab frame, drawn on a sheet, or lit in a case.

looks.name: Collector Reviews
looks.oneLine: A seller's own words on a sticky note pressed to the sheet, five stars above it, and one slab pinned small in the corner — the review that says we knew what the card was worth.
looks.groundSpec:
Lined Paper owns the ground on this theme, and the old spec described a card the engine never built. familyTreatment runs first, paints one of the four sheets (paper:ruled twice, legal, grid, dots by seed % 5) and sets familyGround, which zeroes the cast and tile rotation. A cast ground only appears if the look declares ground:'cast' — and then it OVERWRITES the sheet while leaving every other Lined Paper treatment in place, which is neither of the two cards the old groundSpec described. This theme takes the SHEET.

WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT CHOICE HERE. The family turns the reviewProof template's Quote Card panel into a STICKY NOTE: a fill from ['#fff3a0','#ffd9e6','#d3f7d0','#d6ebff','#ffe4bf'] at opacity 0.96, rx 4, a 1.2deg tilt and an rgba(0,0,0,0.22) blur-22 shadow offset 4/10. A testimonial written on a note stuck to a sheet is the picture; a translucent glass plate over a cast slab was not. The Rate Pill becomes a highlighter or a second sticky depending on its height, so budget exactly one of each and let the star row sit on the sheet itself.

lp03 #eef6ee (lum 0.903) and lp09 #eaf7f2 (0.904) are both pale, and both are Lined Paper, so on the Pokemon run the marks become pen-coloured and the emoji are dropped — a review card with lightning bolts and playing-card emoji scattered over it would undo the tone, which is exactly why lp was chosen.

REVIEWPROOF ONLY, AND WHY. reviewVariant is gated by `if (p.layout === 'reviewProof')` at retheme_lab.mjs ~3002 and returns immediately unless the template carries Quote Card, Quote, Stars, Rate Pill and Rating Line — only reviewProof has them. On trustSeal, stepsFlow and checklistHero this theme had no quote, no quote card and no star row at all, so its mustShow failed on three of its four layouts. Cutting to one layout is safe: REVIEW_PAGE flips the lab into 100-format mode only when every entry in the whole PLAN is reviewProof, and this collection has seven other themes on other layouts.

THE REVIEW BLOCK HAS THREE STATES IN A REGULAR RUN, and the theme must read on all three. v = [0,3,4][sd % 6 mapped], i.e. v=0 twice, v=3 twice, v=4 twice per six. v=0 leaves the template's own block: the quote is TRUST_COPY[cat].q and the Who line is rewritten by retheme() to a name and a city from its own 10-name / 8-city lists. v=3 drops the quote card and builds three one-line quotes from QUOTES[cat] with three names and NO city. v=4 keeps one quote card and adds a 200px opening quote mark in Instrument Serif in the accent. The five-star row survives all three; the numeral-hero variant that replaces the stars with 4.9 is v=1, which only fires in 100-format mode. So: five stars always, a city on two states in three.

The donor templates exist for both categories (dl_pokemon_reviewProof_royal and dl_sports_reviewProof_paper), so p.cat always matches the look's category and the quote is never borrowed from another category's TRUST_COPY.

Same two notes as Want List: force both headline layers to the pen colour before paint (the family fills them by layer-index parity), and groundNow has no 'paper' value so the look faults until a bg src starting 'paper:' maps to it. The slab-overwrite is resolved in the engine.
looks.imagery: One slab, small: assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp on the Pokemon run, assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp on the sports run, at roughly 300px in the lower right, tilted, sitting on the sheet beside the note — not cast at 0.66W / 0.52H behind the quote, which is what the old spec asked for and which the paper ground does not do. Nothing sits over the type and the slab never crosses the sticky: the trust stack yields to the product everywhere else in the library, and here the product yields to the quote.
mustShow: ground:paper — the Lined Paper family sheet, one of four, cycled by seed % 5
a quote with a name — from TRUST_COPY[cat].q on the template's own state, or from QUOTES[cat] on the two reviewVariant states
a Lined Paper palette (lp03 or lp09)
neverShow: a star row of four or six
review text that is not in QUOTES[cat] or TRUST_COPY[cat].q — invented testimonials are a hard fail, and the pool includes the template's own line, not just the QUOTES array
a review city outside LONG BEACH, LAKEWOOD, DOWNEY, CARSON, TORRANCE, CERRITOS, BELLFLOWER and SIGNAL HILL
a sports quote on a POKEMON headline, or a Pokemon quote on a SPORTS CARDS headline
a non-Lined-Paper palette, or emoji marks
headline lines in two colours — the family fills headlines by layer-index parity and both layers must be forced to the pen colour
the product crossing the quote note, or any product over text
the slab cast into the ground at hero size — it is a 300px specimen on the sheet
spec chips from the engine's CHIPS grid (ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK) — that array is phone copy and is not category-gated
layout:trustSeal, layout:stepsFlow, layout:checklistHero — reviewVariant returns immediately on all three, so there is no quote, no quote card and no star row
layout:bandKnockout, layout:arcCrown, layout:neonNight, layout:gradientWave, layout:ticketStub, layout:glassCard, layout:hudTech, layout:slabPoster, layout:voltStack
a grading company's name or mark
naming a grail in a claim line
looks.copy: First person, past tense, ordinary — the quote does the selling and the headline stays out of its way. Headline: WE BUY / POKEMON or WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS. The quote is whichever of the three states the seed lands on: 'Got real value for my binder, not pawn shop prices.' or 'They knew what the alt arts were worth.' on the Pokemon run; 'My rookie cards finally found a fair, serious buyer.' or 'Graded slabs priced against real comps.' on the sports run. Rating line 4.9, 200+ local sellers. Selling point one: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. Selling point two: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED (Pokemon) or WE BUY ENTIRE COLLECTIONS OUTRIGHT (sports). CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL. Money line stays bounded at UP TO $10,000 or UP TO $5,000 PER CARD.
variations: Green tick (lp03) — #055e17 pen, with the five stars and the ticks in the same green; reads as verified.
Teal (lp09) — #0c5b46 with the #f24f6a coral kept to the star row only.

Three-row strip — the reviewVariant state that drops the note and sets three one-line quotes with three names. It is not selectable, it lands on two cards in six, and the theme is composed so it reads: the star row stays, the sheet stays, and the missing city is not a rule this theme claims.
fixesApplied: Layouts cut to ['reviewProof'] only — reviewVariant is gated on that layout and returns immediately without the Quote Card / Stars / Rate Pill / Rating Line set, so on the other three layouts this theme had no quote at all. Verified safe: REVIEW_PAGE only flips at 100-format when every PLAN entry is reviewProof.

groundSpec rewritten: Lined Paper paints the sheet and sets familyGround, so the cast rotation never runs; declaring ground:'cast' would overwrite the sheet while keeping every other family treatment. The theme takes the SHEET, and the sticky-note treatment of the Quote Card is now the reason it does.
ground changed from 'cast' to 'paper' in mustShow and in the ground field, and imagery moved the slab to a ~300px specimen in the lower right instead of a 0.66W / 0.52H cast hero at alpha 0.80.
The index-parity headline break is a neverShow with its fix.
The slab-overwrite is resolved in the engine.

NEW, beyond the audit: the review block has THREE selectable states in a regular run (v=0, v=3, v=4), not one. v=0 uses the template's own TRUST_COPY quote, which the old neverShow would have banned as 'not in the QUOTES pool'; v=3 carries no city at all. mustShow and neverShow are rewritten to read on all three.
NEW: I checked that dl_pokemon_reviewProof and dl_sports_reviewProof donors both exist, so the card never borrows another category's quote.
NEW: the rules are rewritten in the matcher's real grammar and tested against the 344-cutout pool.

looks.name: Under Glass
looks.oneLine: One graded holder standing in a pool of light on deep velvet — the display case after closing, with a serif line and nothing else lit.
looks.groundSpec:
A drawn deep ground, and the only card in this collection that is neither a frame, a sheet nor a cast wedge. Engine kind = 'velvet' from scripts/grounds.js: because dark(P) is true for both palettes (jw05 #044a51 at lum 0.055, jw07 #054e2f at 0.057) it fills c1 directly, then lays a radial from the centre — rgba(#ffffff,0.12) at the middle out to rgba(0,0,0,0.35) at 0.75W — then film grain at 0.08. velvet is in the no-extra-grain list, so it does not take the usual 0.05 pass on top. A lit centre, black corners, cloth texture: the case with one lamp over it.

HOW IT IS REACHED, EXACTLY. abstractKind = !familyGround && (FACESYS.forceAbs || sd % 12 === 7) ? GK[...] : null, where GK is LAB_GROUNDS when set. So this theme runs in its own pass: LAB_LOOKS=1 LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet, which makes GK a one-element array and pins velvet on every card. That matters beyond convenience: when abstractKind is set, `plain` is false and the whole (plain || ...) branch is false, so dg resolves to null and the cast/tile ground never overwrites the abstract one. Without LAB_ABS the look's ground:'deep' is not honoured by the dg hook — which only understands 'cast' and 'tile' — and the card would take a tile or cast ground instead. bg is set at scrim 0.001, so the ground IS the colour and nothing washes it. duo-jw05 and duo-jw07 are the approved alternates if velvet reads too soft; both are on the owner's ticked list, as are velvet-jw05 and velvet-jw07.

WHY THE PRODUCT SURVIVES HERE. The cast filter at line 3428 only fires on __castBg, so on this ground the Hero Product cutout stays and is the visible object — placed by the search at up to ~560px against the right column with an rgba(0,0,0,0.38) blur-40 shadow offset 0/20. This is the only theme in the set where the slab is a lit object rather than something painted into the ground, and it is the reason the theme exists.

THE ONE THING THAT CAN GO WRONG, NAMED. If the placement search finds no clear box, no product is added, and mustShow cannot catch it: lookFaults only runs the mustShow test when the card already carries a cutout. So this theme is restricted to the three layouts that leave the right column free, and REQUIRES the one-line matcher fix `if (must.length && !names.length) out.push('mustShow: no product on the card')`. Until that lands, a card with no slab on it passes its own rules.

TWO MORE REQUIREMENTS. groundNow has no 'deep' value — an abstract ground reports 'abs' — so this look faults on every card in the same way the repo's five existing 'deep' looks do; map __absBg to the look's declared ground, or accept the warning. And the panel pass that forces plates solid only runs for __tileBg and __castBg, so on this ground the translucent glass plates stay translucent; over a flat lit velvet field that is correct and legible, but no plate may sit in the lit centre where the object stands.

Headline 2 is still a gradient on all three layouts and must be flattened to th.ink — the same collection-wide requirement as the cast themes. ELEMENTS.sports.colors is null, so the marks take the palette's own colours and there is no locked-mark problem here at all.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp, standing as the lit object. I opened it: four portrait graded holders fanned left to right, white label panels inside thin red outlines, two of the four empty and two holding blank cream cards. That is the whole argument for this theme. No second object, no photograph, nothing behind the type but the velvet.

the slab standing as a placed object, not painted into the ground

looks.name: Step Sheet
looks.oneLine: How it works, worked out on a sheet: three numbered pen squares down the page, one highlighter on the money line, and a slab taped in the corner as the thing you bring.
looks.groundSpec:
The same drawn sheet as Want List — paper:ruled twice, paper:legal, paper:grid and paper:dots by seed % 5, none of them pinnable — but a different thing written on it. Where Want List sets the items line as a checklist, this theme sets the PROCESS, and it is the only layout in the repo that can.

WHY STEPSFLOW, AND WHY IT ONLY WORKS HERE. stepsFlow builds three rows, each with a Step Card panel, a Step Num Box of 84x84 and a Step Num numeral. The Lined Paper family then does something no other ground does with them: every rect under 130x130 takes the PEN colour at rx 8 with angle 0 and is locked, and the family separately forces `if (/^Step Num \d/.test(l.name)) l.props.fill = '#ffffff'` — so the three number boxes become solid pen squares with white numerals written on them, and the three Step Cards become sticky notes at opacity 0.96 with a 1.2deg tilt and a 22px shadow. That is a worked page, and it is the family's own behaviour rather than a decoration this theme invents.

POKEMON ONLY, AND THIS IS NOT A PREFERENCE. stepsFlow hard-codes its headlines as 'CASH IN' and '3 STEPS'. retheme() rewrites them: '3 STEPS' becomes 'IN 3 STEPS', and 'CASH IN' becomes 'SELL ' + the first word of deck.h2 when no headline already carries a category word. On the Pokemon deck h2 is POKEMON, so the card reads SELL POKEMON / IN 3 STEPS. On the sports deck h2 is 'SPORTS CARDS' and the first word is SPORTS, so a sports card would read SELL SPORTS. Until that rewrite takes the whole h2 rather than its first token, this theme cannot run on sports — and neither can any other theme in this collection.

The palettes paint the pen: lp04 Violet Counter #4932a6 on #f2f2fd, lp05 Sky Ticket #06585c on #e9f7f7. Both are Lined Paper, so ELEMENTS_FAMILY swaps the locked #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 Pokemon marks for [accent, ink, accent] and drops the emoji — which is why a violet or a deep-teal pen is safe on a Pokemon card here and would not be on any other ground in the set.

SAME THREE NOTES AS THE OTHER PAPER THEMES. Force both headline layers to the pen colour before paint, because the family fills them by layer-index parity (SELL POKEMON in pen and IN 3 STEPS in #26231f is the same sentence in two colours). The family also deletes the gradient stepsFlow puts on '3 STEPS', so that break is already handled. groundNow has no 'paper' value and reports 'flat', so this look faults until a bg src starting 'paper:' maps to 'paper'. The slab-overwrite is resolved in the engine. Budget: one highlighter on the money line, three pen squares, one sticky per step row and nothing else — the family will make a sticky out of every panel it is handed.
looks.imagery: One slab, small, taped into the lower-right margin at roughly 260px with a slight tilt: assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp. I opened it: three landscape acrylic cases with blank white labels and flat peach, mint and pink rectangles where the card face would be. At 260px on a ruled sheet beside a three-step working, an empty case reads as the thing you bring in — the holder your cards come back in — which is exactly what step one asks for. It is never cast large, because at 670px the same file is three empty pastel boxes filling the card under a headline about Pokemon.

looks.copy: Instructional and short — the voice of someone showing you how, on the back of a page. Headline: SELL POKEMON / IN 3 STEPS, which is what the engine actually prints on this layout, in Roboto Slab. The three steps carry the process rather than the template's phone copy: TEXT PHOTOS, one line — snap the binder and the slabs, send them over. GET A NUMBER — a firm quote, free appraisal, no obligation. GET PAID — cash or transfer, the same day. Selling point one: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. Selling point two: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED. Money line UP TO $10,000 PER CARD on the highlighter, CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker SAME DAY. The items line stays a list and may name Charizard, Moonbreon, alt arts, illustration rares, ETBs and WOTC.
variations: Violet pen (lp04) — #4932a6 on #f2f2fd; the coolest of the paper themes, and the one that reads best on the yellow legal sheet, where a blue-violet pen is the natural contrast.
Field teal (lp05) — #06585c with the #de6116 orange kept to the step numerals only; warmer, and the version to use when the sheet that lands is paper:dots.
Two up — set steps one and two side by side and step three full width, so the page reads as a form rather than a column. Use when the money line runs long enough to need the whole highlighter.
fixesApplied: NEW THEME, filling one of the four slots the audit emptied, and taking the direction the audit itself gave for those slots: paper is the only ground in this set whose object supply is one small specimen, which is the only supply the card pool actually has.

It avoids the trap in the audit's own suggestion. The audit proposed 'a second Want List variation on paper:legal' — but it had already established, correctly, that the sheet is picked by seed % 5 and cannot be pinned. So this theme is differentiated by what is WRITTEN on the sheet (a worked process) rather than by which sheet lands, and it reads on all four.

It is distinct from the other two paper themes at the template level, not just in tone: stepsFlow is the only layout with Step Num boxes, and the Lined Paper family turns them into pen squares with white numerals — a behaviour neither Want List nor Collector Reviews uses.

NEW, found while writing it: stepsFlow prints SELL SPORTS on the sports deck, because the CASH IN rewrite takes only the first token of deck.h2. That is why this theme is Pokemon-only, and it is also why stepsFlow is removed from Cert Cast and Want List.

It carries the same three paper requirements as the other two — the parity headline fix, the 'paper' groundNow gap, and the family budget — so all three paper themes state the same known conditions in the same words.
Its rules are written in the matcher's real grammar and tested against the 344-cutout pool: only poke-slabs-trio survives.
looks.collectionNote:
WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED. The audit returned REWORK. Four themes are gone: Case Light (merged into Five Star Slab as its deep variation, which is what the audit asked for), Grade Wall and Rookie Board (no card lattice can be built in this repo), Raw And Graded (its entire canvas was the faceless asset). Two new themes replace them on grounds the old set never used: Under Glass (deep) and Step Sheet (paper, on stepsFlow).

THE POOL, OPENED AND MEASURED. assets/approved-assets.json approves 349 cutouts; okCut drops 5 more by LEGACY, so the live pool is 344 (the file's own note still says 360/104 and is stale). Exactly THREE of the 344 are cards: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products and kept as slab frames, and only sports-slab-graded is loaded (CUTOUT_ELS is built from the approved list plus that one file). I opened all four:
- poke-slabs-trio (1794x1831) — three LANDSCAPE acrylic cases, blank white labels, flat peach/mint/pink rectangles where the card face would be. No Pokemon, no card, no text.
- sports-slabs-stack (1843x1328) — four portrait holders fanned. The label is a WHITE panel inside a thin RED OUTLINE, not a filled red bar; two of the four holders are completely empty and two hold blank cream cards. No card face. (The old set's "red label bars are the only warm colour and must survive the veil" was wrong about the asset: at 670px cast width that outline is about 5px, and under a veil it is not a colour note.)
- sports-slab (523x215) — the only asset in the repo showing a real card: a PSA-slabbed basketball card at a steep low angle, with a real grading label.
- sports-slab-graded (1572x1425) — the empty front-on holder used as the frame. I measured its panels off the pixels: the white LABEL runs y 0.074-0.259, x 0.063-0.939; the white CARD in the window runs y 0.354-0.916, x 0.074-0.924.
In assets/bg-web there are ZERO sports photographs and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard, CC BY-SA 2.0, Romer Jed Medina, NYCC 2021, carrying a HAKURO PHOTOGRAPHY studio mark bottom-right.

THE WALL DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE COLLECTION IS NAMED FOR IT. The tile ground pools the deck's cuts plus the subject's whole approved shelf, strips MULTI, keeps cutouts >=240px wide and gates at pool.length >= 4. Pokemon yields ZERO — poke-slabs-trio matches -trio\b in MULTI, which still stands in front of the newer ^qs-/^ip-group-/^iphone-(pair|trio|...) clauses. Sports yields TWO (sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack) against a gate of four. Relaxing the count gate does nothing for Pokemon, and even with both gates fixed the cell is 235 x 322.7 portrait while every card object here is a landscape band, leaving 116-240px of slack per cell. So there is no lattice here. The "wall" the collection is named for is the shop's slab case: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window.

FOUR GROUNDS, NOT SEVEN. slab 2, cast 2, paper 3, deep 1. Paper carries three because a drawn sheet is the only ground where this repo's card supply — one small specimen — is the right size, and the three differ by what is written on the sheet: a want list, a review, and a worked process.

THE RULE GRAMMAR, WHICH THE OLD SET GOT WRONG ON EVERY THEME. lookFaults() is the matcher. It ignores any entry containing a space unless it begins ground: or treat:. It understands exactly four forms: a bare cutout-name prefix (literal startsWith on the basename, no extension); "assets/..." matched against the background src; "ground:<slab|tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|flat>"; and "logo:<prefix of the layer src>", where a placed wordmark's src is "logo:assets/logos/<file>.png:<colour>". So every "cut:" entry in the original ten was a no-op, every "bg:assets/..." entry was a no-op, and "logo:psa" would not have matched even if a psa.png existed. Every rule below is rewritten in the forms the matcher reads. A fault re-seeds the card on attempt 0 and prints a SUBJECT warning on attempt 1, so a correct rule really does stop a mismatched card.

I TESTED THE RULES AGAINST THE POOL. For each theme I ran all 344 approved cutouts against its neverShow. The residue — what can still reach the card — is exactly poke-slabs-trio for the Pokemon themes, and sports-slab plus sports-slabs-stack for the sports themes. Nothing else survives. The 53-prefix block that does this is identical on every theme so it can be diffed; it closes the holes subjectFaults leaves, which are large: SUBJECTS.pokemon.never is /^(iphone|ip-|qs-|ipad|mac|watch|sam-|pix-|gold-|silver-|coin-|strip-|sports-|car-)/i, and 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, 'watch' does not match apple-watch-single, and nothing there stops android-trio, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, cash-fan, handshake-deal or tv-flatscreen. Eighty non-card cutouts passed the old rules.

WHAT THE RULES CANNOT DO, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. (1) mustShow is skipped entirely when a card carries no cutout layer, so it can never require that a product is present — only constrain which one is. (2) "sports-slab" is a literal prefix of "sports-slabs-stack" and "sports-slab-graded", so the 523px slab cannot be excluded by prefix without excluding the sports themes' own hero; it is excluded in code instead (it is absent from CATEGORY_COPY.sports.cuts so it is never cutSrc) and the one place it still reaches a card — the slab window's seed % 2 pick — is named as a required change on both slab themes. (3) groundNow has no 'paper' and no 'deep' value, so a look declaring either faults on every card; 16 approved looks already declare 'paper' and 5 declare 'deep', so this is a matcher gap, not a theme error, and the one-line fix is named in each groundSpec.

ONE SENTENCE, ONE FACE — WHERE IT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. Nearly every layout in app.js sets Headline 2 as a gradient (grad c1:P.a1, c2:P.a2) against a flat Headline 1 — checklistHero, trustSeal, reviewProof, stepsFlow, bandKnockout, arcCrown, voltStack, gradientWave, hudTech all do — and retheme() only re-colours that gradient, it never removes it. Two paths remove it: slabFrame(), which forces every headline to one flat near-black and locks it, and the Lined Paper family, which deletes the gradient but then fills headlines by layer-index parity (k % 2 === 0 ? pen : '#26231f'), so the sentence comes out in two colours instead. So the slab themes satisfy the rule as shipped; the paper themes satisfy it once both headline layers are forced to the pen colour (one line, named in every paper theme); the cast and deep themes need the gradient flattened, also named. No theme here claims the rule is met when it is not.

THE MARK LAW. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji whatever the palette. ELEMENTS_FAMILY covers only 'Lined Paper', which swaps them for [accent, ink, accent] and drops the emoji. So every Pokemon theme here is either on a Lined Paper palette or carries the ELEMENTS_FAMILY requirement in its own rules. ELEMENTS.sports.colors is null, so the sports themes take the palette's own colours and have no such problem — which, with sports-slabs-stack being the better object, is why the set leans sports.

TWO ENGINE TRAPS THE AUDIT DID NOT REACH. (a) On a slab card the deck's cutout is NOT removed: line 3428 filters Hero Product only when t2.__castBg, and slabFrame runs after it, so the product is painted into the window by the ground AND scaled into the same window as a live cutout on top of the copy. The fix is the same one line the cast branch already has, applied to __slab. (b) The SPEC CHIP GRID (retheme_lab.mjs ~893) is not category-gated: its CHIPS array is phone copy — ANY CARRIER, CRACKED OK, ICLOUD LOCKED OK — and it fires on any card whose last band is >=96px tall. On a card ad that is nonsense, and it is banned in prose on every theme here.

THE PASSES. Slab themes need LAB_LOOKS=1 with LAB_SLABGRADE=stars for Five Star Slab and LAB_SLABGRADE=num for Gem Label and the Case variation — the flag is process-global, so the two grade blocks cannot share a run. Under Glass needs LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet. Everything else runs in the default looks pass. The random slab trigger is already fixed in the engine: the call now reads (FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)), so a look owns its ground and the audit's repeated "one card in three is a slab card" finding no longer applies to any theme that belongs to a look.

COPY LAW. A list of what is bought is nominative and may name grails; a claim line must be backed by the picture. Two of the three card cutouts show no card face, so no theme whose picture is an empty holder may name a grail in a claim, and only Gem Label — whose window holds a photograph of a real graded Charizard — may say Charizard. Money lines stay bounded (UP TO $10,000 / UP TO $5,000 PER CARD). Competitors come only from CHALLENGE's own rosters and never take an apostrophe-S. Every card carries at least two selling-point lines besides the items line and the CTA. Five stars, never four, never six. And stepsFlow is barred from the sports deck everywhere in this set: its 'CASH IN' rewrite takes the first word of deck.h2, so a sports card prints SELL SPORTS.

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a graded item: a label band, a barcode, a grade and a window — printed on the slab frame, drawn on a sheet, or lit in a case.

looks.name: Gold Bar Wall
looks.oneLine: The whole gold shelf — twelve cutouts — lies flat in the 4x3 lattice under a 60% olive-ink wash, CASH FOR GOLD stencilled across the middle band and PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE set in mono under it.
looks.groundSpec: Parent gold deck only. Run it with LAB_SUBCATS=0, and discard any card whose exported deckH2 is not GOLD: under a sub-deck fromDeck is unioned first, so the watches slot would put gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury into cells one and two, the rings slot would push gold-necklace-single out for gold-rings-scatter, and the scrap slot would swap in gold-scrap-mixed. On the parent deck the candidate list is exactly twelve for twelve cells, so every card shows all twelve objects and only the starting offset moves with the seed (cell n draws pool[(n+sd)%12]). Geometry: COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell k = min((cell-24)/w,(cell-24)/h)*0.96 centred, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset +10/+16 — real shadows, no overlap, no ghosting. Both palettes are pale (pp04 c1 #f2f8ef lum 0.92, pa04 c1 #d9f7d3 lum 0.86) so the lattice paints straight onto c1 and the wash is the ink at 0.60 — pp04 #2e3d25, pa04 #2b3e27 — because lum(ink) is under 0.4. The card therefore reads as gold on olive-black with the accent (pp04 leaf green #4a8704, pa04 violet #9265ee) as the only other colour. Every stat tile, review card and step panel goes solid at rgba(ink,0.9) with white copy — the engine's own behaviour over a busy ground, and what keeps the small copy legible against the bars. Density target: the wall shows through the gutters; if solid panels cover more than about two thirds of the card, drop a panel rather than shrink the lattice. The wall can always fill (12 candidates against a floor of 4); if it ever could not, the engine falls back to cast, and the ground:cast rule below discards that card.
looks.imagery: The twelve cells, in the engine's own readdir order and each one opened and checked: gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single. Two weak cells to know about rather than hide: gold-jewelry is 511x226, a 2.26:1 sliver that draws about 203x90 inside a 235x322 cell, and gold-bars is the smallest cutout on the shelf at 461x326. gold-bar-single carries a fabricated stamp (GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE) that is illegible at cell size under a 60% wash and must never be enlarged. Optional hero over the wall, drawn 180-480px wide: gold-bars-stack or gold-bars only — the wall's own subject, small, in a corner.

Selling point one: TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU. Selling point two: WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile-and-cast discipline turned on the three metal categories: gold, silver, coins. On every card the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing in frame. Either the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) carries that metal's whole approved shelf under a 60% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Nine themes: three walls (one per metal, which is all the engine can build) and six casts. No photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient anywhere.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES (re-verified in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs; these replace the two "engine facts" the first draft carried, both of which were false). (1) THE WALL POOL is fromDeck UNION the SUBJECT shelf, minus the MULTI regex at line 2926 (any -pair / -row / -fan / -set / -three / -trio / -group name), minus anything under 240px wide (line 2933), sliced to 12. A sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall; it REORDERS it, because fromDeck is concatenated first. That is how a watch reaches a gold wall: under LAB_SUBCATS=1 the watches slot puts gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury in cells one and two. So every wall theme here pins the parent deck by deckH2 and discards anything else. (2) THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WALL PER METAL, verified by running the filter: gold 12 (gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single), silver 9 (silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile), coins 11 (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-slabs-stack, coin-stack-silver, coin-stack, gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube). Two tile themes on one metal are therefore one picture in two colourways, which is why this collection carries one wall per metal and no more. coin-slab (144px) and coin-single-large (223px) are removed from every wall by the 240px rule, parent deck or sub-deck. (3) THESE RECORDS ARE LOOKS for assets/looks.json (LAB_LOOKS=1) and the field is `key`, not `id` (line 2764 does LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)), so write each id below as `key`. A look owns palettes, faces, ground, layouts and the variation COUNT and nothing else. Only tile and cast are honoured as a ground (line 2854 tests /^(cast|tile)$/), so no theme here may name slab, scene, paper, deep or photo. (4) CATEGORY IS NOT A LOOK PROPERTY: the card's cat comes from RING[(base+e.v)%8] at line 2729. Run with LAB_CATS=gold,silver,coins; until RING reads FACESYS.cats, roughly one card in eight lands in category and the rest are discarded. (5) HOW mustShow AND neverShow ARE ACTUALLY READ (lookFaults, line 2519): every entry is matched by literal startsWith against the names of the card's CUTOUT LAYERS. An entry containing a space is skipped as prose unless it begins ground: or treat: — and a ground: entry must be written bare ("ground:photo"), because "ground:photo (bg-web/*)" compares the whole tail and never fires. mustShow is an OR, not an AND: one matching layer satisfies the entire list, and a card with no cutout layer satisfies it vacuously. An entry containing a pipe matches nothing and only breaks the list, so no rule below uses one. WALL CELLS AND CAST HEROES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS MATCHER: the wall is painted into the ground image keyed dg:tile:..., the cast product into dg:cast:..., and line 3424 strips every Hero and Lineup Product layer from a cast. So a wall cell can never be rejected by a neverShow entry (the first draft's four "self-rejecting" themes were not rejecting their walls at all — "gold-jewelry" was only ever banning that sliver as a HERO), and a cast's product can only be checked against the exported record's `product` field (line 3641). Rules below come in three kinds: bare tokens that bite, bare ground: tokens, and audit-side rules that carry spaces on purpose (product:, deckH2:, sub:, mark:, palette:, face:, copy:, assort:). A fault re-seeds the card once and then ships it with a console warning, so the audit script is what discards. (6) FABRICATED STAMPS, found by opening the files at full size: gold-bar-single is stamped GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE around an invented portrait, gold-bars-fan and gold-bars-row are stamped SEGIR WORE GOLD, silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD, and silver-bars-row and silver-bars-stack are SILVER bars stamped GOLD. In a 235px lattice cell under a 60% wash the lettering is illegible and they stay wall stock; at cast size (669px) or hero size (up to 480px) the invented words are plainly readable, and a silver bar stamped GOLD under a SILVER headline is the words-disagree-with-picture failure twice over. No theme may draw any of the five large. Same class of fault as the rejected strip-kit-meter. (7) MARKS TAKE THE PALETTE: ELEMENTS.gold.colors [#f2c14e,#c9950f,#fff1b8], ELEMENTS.coins.colors [#f2c14e,#d9d9d9,#c9950f] and ELEMENTS.silver.colors [#e6e8ea,#9aa0a6,#ffffff] are hardcoded at lines 2353-2355 and beat the palette at line 2535. ENGINE: set those three to null for a metal-wall run so addElements falls back to [accent, support, accent2, accent3]; until then reject any card carrying a mark in those hexes. (8) THE SLAB FRAME CANNOT REACH A METALS CARD — slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports (line 2372) — so no theme here carries a ground:slab rule. A photograph of a real graded coin holder is a cutout and a different thing. (9) NO BRAND WORDMARK APPEARS: BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only, so no metals card can draw one, and when the engine does ink a mark it uses pure black #14161c or pure white #ffffff, never th.ink (the fix for the brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes).

THE FAMILY RULES. (1) Not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support — a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is mud — so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, plum or slate and every accent is green, violet, magenta, orchid, pink, rose, vermilion or crimson. jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) and pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66) are out of the collection for exactly that. (2) Numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono): the copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages. (3) Display faces are stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter or slab — never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded. (4) The money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, PAID ON THE SPOT AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim, and a matched competitor takes no apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CASH4GOLD and WE MATCH THE COIN SHOP are both real names in CHALLENGE. (5) One sentence in one face on the headline, at least two selling-point lines on every card, five stars wherever reviewProof runs, imagery on every card, no product over text, and no watch theme anywhere — the gold watches sub-deck, deckH2 GOLD WATCHES, the WATCH BUYER kicker, gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch and the watch emoji are banned collection-wide. (6) None of the fifteen rejected assets appears: this collection contains no phone, tablet, Mac, watch, trading card, vehicle, test strip, hand or stack of cash, and every asset named below was checked against assets/approved-assets.json and opened.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER COLLECTIONS: the device collections tile phones and Macs on cool-bright palettes, the card collections own the slab frame, the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals and the spot-price line.

looks.name: Cuban Cast
looks.oneLine: One Cuban bracelet drawn two thirds of the card wide with a soft window shadow falling across it, and a typewriter headline that reads like the written offer the copy promises.
looks.groundSpec: The bracelets slot cannot be pinned: subDeck = SUB[sd % 5] at line 2760 and all five gold slots are ready, so the audit keeps only the cards whose exported deckH2 is GOLD BRACELETS (the bracelets slot, whose hero pool is exactly gold-bracelet-cuban and gold-bracelet-pair — both correct, so every card of that slot is on-subject) or GOLD (a parent-deck run, where the two bracelets are 2 of the 21 heroes), and discards the other four slots. looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile-and-cast discipline turned on the three metal categories: gold, silver, coins. On every card the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing in frame. Either the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) carries that metal's whole approved shelf under a 60% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Nine themes: three walls (one per metal, which is all the engine can build) and six casts. No photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient anywhere.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES (re-verified in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs; these replace the two "engine facts" the first draft carried, both of which were false). (1) THE WALL POOL is fromDeck UNION the SUBJECT shelf, minus the MULTI regex at line 2926 (any -pair / -row / -fan / -set / -three / -trio / -group name), minus anything under 240px wide (line 2933), sliced to 12. A sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall; it REORDERS it, because fromDeck is concatenated first. That is how a watch reaches a gold wall: under LAB_SUBCATS=1 the watches slot puts gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury in cells one and two. So every wall theme here pins the parent deck by deckH2 and discards anything else. (2) THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WALL PER METAL, verified by running the filter: gold 12 (gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single), silver 9 (silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile), coins 11 (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-slabs-stack, coin-stack-silver, coin-stack, gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube). Two tile themes on one metal are therefore one picture in two colourways, which is why this collection carries one wall per metal and no more. coin-slab (144px) and coin-single-large (223px) are removed from every wall by the 240px rule, parent deck or sub-deck. (3) THESE RECORDS ARE LOOKS for assets/looks.json (LAB_LOOKS=1) and the field is `key`, not `id` (line 2764 does LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)), so write each id below as `key`. A look owns palettes, faces, ground, layouts and the variation COUNT and nothing else. Only tile and cast are honoured as a ground (line 2854 tests /^(cast|tile)$/), so no theme here may name slab, scene, paper, deep or photo. (4) CATEGORY IS NOT A LOOK PROPERTY: the card's cat comes from RING[(base+e.v)%8] at line 2729. Run with LAB_CATS=gold,silver,coins; until RING reads FACESYS.cats, roughly one card in eight lands in category and the rest are discarded. (5) HOW mustShow AND neverShow ARE ACTUALLY READ (lookFaults, line 2519): every entry is matched by literal startsWith against the names of the card's CUTOUT LAYERS. An entry containing a space is skipped as prose unless it begins ground: or treat: — and a ground: entry must be written bare ("ground:photo"), because "ground:photo (bg-web/*)" compares the whole tail and never fires. mustShow is an OR, not an AND: one matching layer satisfies the entire list, and a card with no cutout layer satisfies it vacuously. An entry containing a pipe matches nothing and only breaks the list, so no rule below uses one. WALL CELLS AND CAST HEROES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS MATCHER: the wall is painted into the ground image keyed dg:tile:..., the cast product into dg:cast:..., and line 3424 strips every Hero and Lineup Product layer from a cast. So a wall cell can never be rejected by a neverShow entry (the first draft's four "self-rejecting" themes were not rejecting their walls at all — "gold-jewelry" was only ever banning that sliver as a HERO), and a cast's product can only be checked against the exported record's `product` field (line 3641). Rules below come in three kinds: bare tokens that bite, bare ground: tokens, and audit-side rules that carry spaces on purpose (product:, deckH2:, sub:, mark:, palette:, face:, copy:, assort:). A fault re-seeds the card once and then ships it with a console warning, so the audit script is what discards. (6) FABRICATED STAMPS, found by opening the files at full size: gold-bar-single is stamped GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE around an invented portrait, gold-bars-fan and gold-bars-row are stamped SEGIR WORE GOLD, silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD, and silver-bars-row and silver-bars-stack are SILVER bars stamped GOLD. In a 235px lattice cell under a 60% wash the lettering is illegible and they stay wall stock; at cast size (669px) or hero size (up to 480px) the invented words are plainly readable, and a silver bar stamped GOLD under a SILVER headline is the words-disagree-with-picture failure twice over. No theme may draw any of the five large. Same class of fault as the rejected strip-kit-meter. (7) MARKS TAKE THE PALETTE: ELEMENTS.gold.colors [#f2c14e,#c9950f,#fff1b8], ELEMENTS.coins.colors [#f2c14e,#d9d9d9,#c9950f] and ELEMENTS.silver.colors [#e6e8ea,#9aa0a6,#ffffff] are hardcoded at lines 2353-2355 and beat the palette at line 2535. ENGINE: set those three to null for a metal-wall run so addElements falls back to [accent, support, accent2, accent3]; until then reject any card carrying a mark in those hexes. (8) THE SLAB FRAME CANNOT REACH A METALS CARD — slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports (line 2372) — so no theme here carries a ground:slab rule. A photograph of a real graded coin holder is a cutout and a different thing. (9) NO BRAND WORDMARK APPEARS: BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only, so no metals card can draw one, and when the engine does ink a mark it uses pure black #14161c or pure white #ffffff, never th.ink (the fix for the brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes).

THE FAMILY RULES. (1) Not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support — a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is mud — so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, plum or slate and every accent is green, violet, magenta, orchid, pink, rose, vermilion or crimson. jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) and pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66) are out of the collection for exactly that. (2) Numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono): the copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages. (3) Display faces are stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter or slab — never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded. (4) The money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, PAID ON THE SPOT AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim, and a matched competitor takes no apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CASH4GOLD and WE MATCH THE COIN SHOP are both real names in CHALLENGE. (5) One sentence in one face on the headline, at least two selling-point lines on every card, five stars wherever reviewProof runs, imagery on every card, no product over text, and no watch theme anywhere — the gold watches sub-deck, deckH2 GOLD WATCHES, the WATCH BUYER kicker, gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch and the watch emoji are banned collection-wide. (6) None of the fifteen rejected assets appears: this collection contains no phone, tablet, Mac, watch, trading card, vehicle, test strip, hand or stack of cash, and every asset named below was checked against assets/approved-assets.json and opened.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER COLLECTIONS: the device collections tile phones and Macs on cool-bright palettes, the card collections own the slab frame, the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals and the spot-price line.

looks.oneLine: A scatter of gold rings drawn two thirds of the card wide under a window shadow, with the karat ladder — 10k, 14k, 18k, 22k — stacked in mono down a solid panel beside it.

looks.imagery: One object, from a pool of three, all opened and checked: gold-rings-scatter (an assortment of plain and stone-set gold rings, top-down, no lettering), gold-class-ring (a heavy class ring with a coloured stone) or gold-earrings-pile (a heap of gold earrings). neverShow: sub:watches, and any items line naming Omega or Rolex on this theme
deckH2:anything but GOLD RINGS or GOLD — SCRAP GOLD, GOLD CHAINS, GOLD BRACELETS and GOLD WATCHES all put a different object at 62% of the card
product:any gold- cutout other than gold-rings-scatter, gold-class-ring or gold-earrings-pile — the parent-deck hero is use[(sd*7+3)%21] and is not quality-filtered
product:gold-bars-stack and gold-bar-single — bullion has no karat, and gold-bar-single carries an invented stamp
layer:any cutout surviving on top of the cast
mark:any element drawn in #f2c14e, #c9950f or #fff1b8 (ELEMENTS.gold.colors), and the watch emoji
mark:more than two marks, and any mark in the middle third
face:Oswald on anything but the headline and the ladder — Instrument Sans carries the sub lines
copy:a karat we do not test (24k jewellery claims), any unbounded price claim, and any second sentence in the headline face
palette:pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66, a mustard-olive) and jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) — both are banned by family rule 1 and both sat on a gold card in the first draft
palette:any palette whose ink is #2e3d25 or #2b3e27 — those two are the Gold Bar Wall's wash
looks.copy: Counter voice, itemised: what you have, what it is stamped, what it pays. Headline CASH FOR / GOLD, or GOLD RINGS with the spec WEDDING BANDS, NUGGET RINGS, CLASS RINGS when the rings deck is running. Selling point one: TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU. Selling point two: ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY. looks.name: Sterling Drawer
looks.oneLine: The full sterling drawer — flatware, candlesticks, tubes, rounds and a jewellery pile — tiled under a one-hue teal wash with a blackletter money word.
looks.groundSpec: Parent silver deck (LAB_SUBCATS=0; discard any card whose deckH2 is not SILVER). The pool is nine, not eleven: MULTI removes silver-bars-row and silver-flatware-set from every wall. Nine into twelve cells means three objects appear twice, at cells i and i+9 — row 0's first three reappear one column to the right in row 2, so a repeat is never adjacent to itself. Wall painted on c1 (pp06 #edf8fa lum 0.92, io08 #dbf7f6 lum 0.88) and washed with the ink — #173e45 and #173f3f — at 0.60. Both palettes are one hue in tones and mono: pp06 accent #008394 with support #1d96a8, io08 accent #169292 with support #1c9292. That is the point of the pairing: a drawer full of tarnished objects already carries every grey there is, so the card supplies one colour and the metal supplies the rest. looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile-and-cast discipline turned on the three metal categories: gold, silver, coins. On every card the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing in frame. Either the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) carries that metal's whole approved shelf under a 60% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Nine themes: three walls (one per metal, which is all the engine can build) and six casts. No photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient anywhere.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES (re-verified in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs; these replace the two "engine facts" the first draft carried, both of which were false). (1) THE WALL POOL is fromDeck UNION the SUBJECT shelf, minus the MULTI regex at line 2926 (any -pair / -row / -fan / -set / -three / -trio / -group name), minus anything under 240px wide (line 2933), sliced to 12. A sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall; it REORDERS it, because fromDeck is concatenated first. That is how a watch reaches a gold wall: under LAB_SUBCATS=1 the watches slot puts gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury in cells one and two. So every wall theme here pins the parent deck by deckH2 and discards anything else. (2) THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WALL PER METAL, verified by running the filter: gold 12 (gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single), silver 9 (silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile), coins 11 (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-slabs-stack, coin-stack-silver, coin-stack, gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube). Two tile themes on one metal are therefore one picture in two colourways, which is why this collection carries one wall per metal and no more. coin-slab (144px) and coin-single-large (223px) are removed from every wall by the 240px rule, parent deck or sub-deck. (3) THESE RECORDS ARE LOOKS for assets/looks.json (LAB_LOOKS=1) and the field is `key`, not `id` (line 2764 does LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)), so write each id below as `key`. A look owns palettes, faces, ground, layouts and the variation COUNT and nothing else. Only tile and cast are honoured as a ground (line 2854 tests /^(cast|tile)$/), so no theme here may name slab, scene, paper, deep or photo. (4) CATEGORY IS NOT A LOOK PROPERTY: the card's cat comes from RING[(base+e.v)%8] at line 2729. Run with LAB_CATS=gold,silver,coins; until RING reads FACESYS.cats, roughly one card in eight lands in category and the rest are discarded. (5) HOW mustShow AND neverShow ARE ACTUALLY READ (lookFaults, line 2519): every entry is matched by literal startsWith against the names of the card's CUTOUT LAYERS. An entry containing a space is skipped as prose unless it begins ground: or treat: — and a ground: entry must be written bare ("ground:photo"), because "ground:photo (bg-web/*)" compares the whole tail and never fires. mustShow is an OR, not an AND: one matching layer satisfies the entire list, and a card with no cutout layer satisfies it vacuously. An entry containing a pipe matches nothing and only breaks the list, so no rule below uses one. WALL CELLS AND CAST HEROES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS MATCHER: the wall is painted into the ground image keyed dg:tile:..., the cast product into dg:cast:..., and line 3424 strips every Hero and Lineup Product layer from a cast. So a wall cell can never be rejected by a neverShow entry (the first draft's four "self-rejecting" themes were not rejecting their walls at all — "gold-jewelry" was only ever banning that sliver as a HERO), and a cast's product can only be checked against the exported record's `product` field (line 3641). Rules below come in three kinds: bare tokens that bite, bare ground: tokens, and audit-side rules that carry spaces on purpose (product:, deckH2:, sub:, mark:, palette:, face:, copy:, assort:). A fault re-seeds the card once and then ships it with a console warning, so the audit script is what discards. (6) FABRICATED STAMPS, found by opening the files at full size: gold-bar-single is stamped GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE around an invented portrait, gold-bars-fan and gold-bars-row are stamped SEGIR WORE GOLD, silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD, and silver-bars-row and silver-bars-stack are SILVER bars stamped GOLD. In a 235px lattice cell under a 60% wash the lettering is illegible and they stay wall stock; at cast size (669px) or hero size (up to 480px) the invented words are plainly readable, and a silver bar stamped GOLD under a SILVER headline is the words-disagree-with-picture failure twice over. No theme may draw any of the five large. Same class of fault as the rejected strip-kit-meter. (7) MARKS TAKE THE PALETTE: ELEMENTS.gold.colors [#f2c14e,#c9950f,#fff1b8], ELEMENTS.coins.colors [#f2c14e,#d9d9d9,#c9950f] and ELEMENTS.silver.colors [#e6e8ea,#9aa0a6,#ffffff] are hardcoded at lines 2353-2355 and beat the palette at line 2535. ENGINE: set those three to null for a metal-wall run so addElements falls back to [accent, support, accent2, accent3]; until then reject any card carrying a mark in those hexes. (8) THE SLAB FRAME CANNOT REACH A METALS CARD — slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports (line 2372) — so no theme here carries a ground:slab rule. A photograph of a real graded coin holder is a cutout and a different thing. (9) NO BRAND WORDMARK APPEARS: BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only, so no metals card can draw one, and when the engine does ink a mark it uses pure black #14161c or pure white #ffffff, never th.ink (the fix for the brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes).

THE FAMILY RULES. (1) Not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support — a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is mud — so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, plum or slate and every accent is green, violet, magenta, orchid, pink, rose, vermilion or crimson. jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) and pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66) are out of the collection for exactly that. (2) Numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono): the copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages. (3) Display faces are stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter or slab — never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded. (4) The money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, PAID ON THE SPOT AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim, and a matched competitor takes no apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CASH4GOLD and WE MATCH THE COIN SHOP are both real names in CHALLENGE. (5) One sentence in one face on the headline, at least two selling-point lines on every card, five stars wherever reviewProof runs, imagery on every card, no product over text, and no watch theme anywhere — the gold watches sub-deck, deckH2 GOLD WATCHES, the WATCH BUYER kicker, gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch and the watch emoji are banned collection-wide. (6) None of the fifteen rejected assets appears: this collection contains no phone, tablet, Mac, watch, trading card, vehicle, test strip, hand or stack of cash, and every asset named below was checked against assets/approved-assets.json and opened.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER COLLECTIONS: the device collections tile phones and Macs on cool-bright palettes, the card collections own the slab frame, the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals and the spot-price line.

looks.oneLine: One mixed pile of sterling jewellery drawn two thirds of the card wide on a deep teal jewel ground, a window shadow across it and a pink accent doing the talking.
looks.groundSpec: The jewelry slot resolves to exactly one approved cutout: cuts ['silver-ring','silver-chain','silver-jewel'] reach only silver-jewelry-mixed (2048x1681), so this cast can only ever draw the right object and never upscales (k = 0.327). looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile-and-cast discipline turned on the three metal categories: gold, silver, coins. On every card the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing in frame. Either the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) carries that metal's whole approved shelf under a 60% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Nine themes: three walls (one per metal, which is all the engine can build) and six casts. No photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient anywhere.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES (re-verified in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs; these replace the two "engine facts" the first draft carried, both of which were false). (1) THE WALL POOL is fromDeck UNION the SUBJECT shelf, minus the MULTI regex at line 2926 (any -pair / -row / -fan / -set / -three / -trio / -group name), minus anything under 240px wide (line 2933), sliced to 12. A sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall; it REORDERS it, because fromDeck is concatenated first. That is how a watch reaches a gold wall: under LAB_SUBCATS=1 the watches slot puts gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury in cells one and two. So every wall theme here pins the parent deck by deckH2 and discards anything else. (2) THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WALL PER METAL, verified by running the filter: gold 12 (gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single), silver 9 (silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile), coins 11 (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-slabs-stack, coin-stack-silver, coin-stack, gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube). Two tile themes on one metal are therefore one picture in two colourways, which is why this collection carries one wall per metal and no more. coin-slab (144px) and coin-single-large (223px) are removed from every wall by the 240px rule, parent deck or sub-deck. (3) THESE RECORDS ARE LOOKS for assets/looks.json (LAB_LOOKS=1) and the field is `key`, not `id` (line 2764 does LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)), so write each id below as `key`. A look owns palettes, faces, ground, layouts and the variation COUNT and nothing else. Only tile and cast are honoured as a ground (line 2854 tests /^(cast|tile)$/), so no theme here may name slab, scene, paper, deep or photo. (4) CATEGORY IS NOT A LOOK PROPERTY: the card's cat comes from RING[(base+e.v)%8] at line 2729. Run with LAB_CATS=gold,silver,coins; until RING reads FACESYS.cats, roughly one card in eight lands in category and the rest are discarded. (5) HOW mustShow AND neverShow ARE ACTUALLY READ (lookFaults, line 2519): every entry is matched by literal startsWith against the names of the card's CUTOUT LAYERS. An entry containing a space is skipped as prose unless it begins ground: or treat: — and a ground: entry must be written bare ("ground:photo"), because "ground:photo (bg-web/*)" compares the whole tail and never fires. mustShow is an OR, not an AND: one matching layer satisfies the entire list, and a card with no cutout layer satisfies it vacuously. An entry containing a pipe matches nothing and only breaks the list, so no rule below uses one. WALL CELLS AND CAST HEROES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS MATCHER: the wall is painted into the ground image keyed dg:tile:..., the cast product into dg:cast:..., and line 3424 strips every Hero and Lineup Product layer from a cast. So a wall cell can never be rejected by a neverShow entry (the first draft's four "self-rejecting" themes were not rejecting their walls at all — "gold-jewelry" was only ever banning that sliver as a HERO), and a cast's product can only be checked against the exported record's `product` field (line 3641). Rules below come in three kinds: bare tokens that bite, bare ground: tokens, and audit-side rules that carry spaces on purpose (product:, deckH2:, sub:, mark:, palette:, face:, copy:, assort:). A fault re-seeds the card once and then ships it with a console warning, so the audit script is what discards. (6) FABRICATED STAMPS, found by opening the files at full size: gold-bar-single is stamped GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE around an invented portrait, gold-bars-fan and gold-bars-row are stamped SEGIR WORE GOLD, silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD, and silver-bars-row and silver-bars-stack are SILVER bars stamped GOLD. In a 235px lattice cell under a 60% wash the lettering is illegible and they stay wall stock; at cast size (669px) or hero size (up to 480px) the invented words are plainly readable, and a silver bar stamped GOLD under a SILVER headline is the words-disagree-with-picture failure twice over. No theme may draw any of the five large. Same class of fault as the rejected strip-kit-meter. (7) MARKS TAKE THE PALETTE: ELEMENTS.gold.colors [#f2c14e,#c9950f,#fff1b8], ELEMENTS.coins.colors [#f2c14e,#d9d9d9,#c9950f] and ELEMENTS.silver.colors [#e6e8ea,#9aa0a6,#ffffff] are hardcoded at lines 2353-2355 and beat the palette at line 2535. ENGINE: set those three to null for a metal-wall run so addElements falls back to [accent, support, accent2, accent3]; until then reject any card carrying a mark in those hexes. (8) THE SLAB FRAME CANNOT REACH A METALS CARD — slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports (line 2372) — so no theme here carries a ground:slab rule. A photograph of a real graded coin holder is a cutout and a different thing. (9) NO BRAND WORDMARK APPEARS: BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only, so no metals card can draw one, and when the engine does ink a mark it uses pure black #14161c or pure white #ffffff, never th.ink (the fix for the brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes).

THE FAMILY RULES. (1) Not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support — a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is mud — so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, plum or slate and every accent is green, violet, magenta, orchid, pink, rose, vermilion or crimson. jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) and pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66) are out of the collection for exactly that. (2) Numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono): the copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages. (3) Display faces are stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter or slab — never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded. (4) The money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, PAID ON THE SPOT AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim, and a matched competitor takes no apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CASH4GOLD and WE MATCH THE COIN SHOP are both real names in CHALLENGE. (5) One sentence in one face on the headline, at least two selling-point lines on every card, five stars wherever reviewProof runs, imagery on every card, no product over text, and no watch theme anywhere — the gold watches sub-deck, deckH2 GOLD WATCHES, the WATCH BUYER kicker, gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch and the watch emoji are banned collection-wide. (6) None of the fifteen rejected assets appears: this collection contains no phone, tablet, Mac, watch, trading card, vehicle, test strip, hand or stack of cash, and every asset named below was checked against assets/approved-assets.json and opened.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER COLLECTIONS: the device collections tile phones and Macs on cool-bright palettes, the card collections own the slab frame, the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals and the spot-price line.
