looks.name: Graded Case
looks.oneLine: A fan of graded coin holders drawn two thirds of the card wide under a window shadow, with a tall condensed headline and the grade line set in mono like a certificate.
looks.groundSpec: The slabs slot cannot be pinned — SUB for coins is [dollars, collections, slabs] after goldcoins drops out (ready:false, no matching cutouts) and subDeck = SUB[sd % 3] — so two cards in three carry the dollars or collections deck and are discarded by the product rule; the yield is one in three. One caution the operator has to know: the slot's cuts are ['coin-slab','coin-graded'] and that prefix catches the 144x144 coin-slab.webp as well as coin-slabs-stack, so one hero in three is a 4.65x upscale of a thumbnail that is not even a slab — it is a close-up of a single raw coin. Until retheme_lab.mjs:320 reads cuts ['coin-slabs','coin-graded'] — one letter — the audit rejects any card whose exported product is exactly coin-slab. jw09 leads because it is deep (c1 #054666, lum 0.054): no ink overlay, sheen 0.10, shadow 0.50 with its blur-60 penumbra at 0.25, scrim c1 at 0.22, so the holders keep their own light. cd06 is the pale variation (c1 #80dafd, lum 0.62): ink #1b3d49 at 0.20 plus a magenta #ab117d to ink gradient at 0.18, sheen 0.12, shadow 0.58 with its penumbra at 0.29, scrim ink at 0.30 (c2 #45c4ff is lum 0.48, above the 0.45 test, so the scrim is the ink). On jw09 keep the salmon accent #fdc0b7 on the grade line, the rules and the plate: a large salmon word beside a silver coin is the one place in this collection where an accent could be mistaken for metal. Cast strips Hero and Lineup Product at line 3424.
looks.imagery: One object, both opened and checked: coin-graded-fan-three (1950x1865, three rigid holders fanned with the coins visible, blank white labels) or coin-slabs-stack (1849x1314, three holders stacked at slight angles, blank white labels). k = 0.343 and 0.362, so neither upscales. The blank labels are why these two are approved where the empty coin-slab-graded holder was rejected: a holder with a coin in it is a product. Never letter those labels with a grade or a grading company's name — the grade line is typography on the card, beside the holder, never on it.
neverShow: product:coin-slab exactly — NOT as a bare prefix, which would also ban coin-slabs-stack, one of this theme's two heroes; reject any card whose exported product is exactly coin-slab (144x144, a 4.65x upscale of a raw coin, not a slab)
product:anything but coin-graded-fan-three or coin-slabs-stack — the dollars and collections decks also fire and their heroes are a different card
deckH2:SILVER DOLLARS and COIN COLLECTIONS — this theme's cards carry GRADED COINS or the parent COINS

looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile-and-cast discipline turned on the three metal categories: gold, silver, coins. On every card the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing in frame. Either the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) carries that metal's whole approved shelf under a 60% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Nine themes: three walls (one per metal, which is all the engine can build) and six casts. No photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient anywhere.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES (re-verified in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs; these replace the two "engine facts" the first draft carried, both of which were false). (1) THE WALL POOL is fromDeck UNION the SUBJECT shelf, minus the MULTI regex at line 2926 (any -pair / -row / -fan / -set / -three / -trio / -group name), minus anything under 240px wide (line 2933), sliced to 12. A sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall; it REORDERS it, because fromDeck is concatenated first. That is how a watch reaches a gold wall: under LAB_SUBCATS=1 the watches slot puts gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury in cells one and two. So every wall theme here pins the parent deck by deckH2 and discards anything else. (2) THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WALL PER METAL, verified by running the filter: gold 12 (gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single), silver 9 (silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile), coins 11 (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-slabs-stack, coin-stack-silver, coin-stack, gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube). Two tile themes on one metal are therefore one picture in two colourways, which is why this collection carries one wall per metal and no more. coin-slab (144px) and coin-single-large (223px) are removed from every wall by the 240px rule, parent deck or sub-deck. (3) THESE RECORDS ARE LOOKS for assets/looks.json (LAB_LOOKS=1) and the field is `key`, not `id` (line 2764 does LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)), so write each id below as `key`. A look owns palettes, faces, ground, layouts and the variation COUNT and nothing else. Only tile and cast are honoured as a ground (line 2854 tests /^(cast|tile)$/), so no theme here may name slab, scene, paper, deep or photo. (4) CATEGORY IS NOT A LOOK PROPERTY: the card's cat comes from RING[(base+e.v)%8] at line 2729. Run with LAB_CATS=gold,silver,coins; until RING reads FACESYS.cats, roughly one card in eight lands in category and the rest are discarded. (5) HOW mustShow AND neverShow ARE ACTUALLY READ (lookFaults, line 2519): every entry is matched by literal startsWith against the names of the card's CUTOUT LAYERS. An entry containing a space is skipped as prose unless it begins ground: or treat: — and a ground: entry must be written bare ("ground:photo"), because "ground:photo (bg-web/*)" compares the whole tail and never fires. mustShow is an OR, not an AND: one matching layer satisfies the entire list, and a card with no cutout layer satisfies it vacuously. An entry containing a pipe matches nothing and only breaks the list, so no rule below uses one. WALL CELLS AND CAST HEROES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS MATCHER: the wall is painted into the ground image keyed dg:tile:..., the cast product into dg:cast:..., and line 3424 strips every Hero and Lineup Product layer from a cast. So a wall cell can never be rejected by a neverShow entry (the first draft's four "self-rejecting" themes were not rejecting their walls at all — "gold-jewelry" was only ever banning that sliver as a HERO), and a cast's product can only be checked against the exported record's `product` field (line 3641). Rules below come in three kinds: bare tokens that bite, bare ground: tokens, and audit-side rules that carry spaces on purpose (product:, deckH2:, sub:, mark:, palette:, face:, copy:, assort:). A fault re-seeds the card once and then ships it with a console warning, so the audit script is what discards. (6) FABRICATED STAMPS, found by opening the files at full size: gold-bar-single is stamped GUEM BOT GARN / GOLD GOODDE around an invented portrait, gold-bars-fan and gold-bars-row are stamped SEGIR WORE GOLD, silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD, and silver-bars-row and silver-bars-stack are SILVER bars stamped GOLD. In a 235px lattice cell under a 60% wash the lettering is illegible and they stay wall stock; at cast size (669px) or hero size (up to 480px) the invented words are plainly readable, and a silver bar stamped GOLD under a SILVER headline is the words-disagree-with-picture failure twice over. No theme may draw any of the five large. Same class of fault as the rejected strip-kit-meter. (7) MARKS TAKE THE PALETTE: ELEMENTS.gold.colors [#f2c14e,#c9950f,#fff1b8], ELEMENTS.coins.colors [#f2c14e,#d9d9d9,#c9950f] and ELEMENTS.silver.colors [#e6e8ea,#9aa0a6,#ffffff] are hardcoded at lines 2353-2355 and beat the palette at line 2535. ENGINE: set those three to null for a metal-wall run so addElements falls back to [accent, support, accent2, accent3]; until then reject any card carrying a mark in those hexes. (8) THE SLAB FRAME CANNOT REACH A METALS CARD — slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports (line 2372) — so no theme here carries a ground:slab rule. A photograph of a real graded coin holder is a cutout and a different thing. (9) NO BRAND WORDMARK APPEARS: BRAND_LOGO maps vehicle words only, so no metals card can draw one, and when the engine does ink a mark it uses pure black #14161c or pure white #ffffff, never th.ink (the fix for the brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes).

THE FAMILY RULES. (1) Not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support — a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is mud — so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, plum or slate and every accent is green, violet, magenta, orchid, pink, rose, vermilion or crimson. jw07 (support #9eb666, hue 78) and pp09 (support #858d42, hue 66) are out of the collection for exactly that. (2) Numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono): the copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages. (3) Display faces are stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter or slab — never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded. (4) The money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, PAID ON THE SPOT AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim, and a matched competitor takes no apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CASH4GOLD and WE MATCH THE COIN SHOP are both real names in CHALLENGE. (5) One sentence in one face on the headline, at least two selling-point lines on every card, five stars wherever reviewProof runs, imagery on every card, no product over text, and no watch theme anywhere — the gold watches sub-deck, deckH2 GOLD WATCHES, the WATCH BUYER kicker, gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch and the watch emoji are banned collection-wide. (6) None of the fifteen rejected assets appears: this collection contains no phone, tablet, Mac, watch, trading card, vehicle, test strip, hand or stack of cash, and every asset named below was checked against assets/approved-assets.json and opened.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER COLLECTIONS: the device collections tile phones and Macs on cool-bright palettes, the card collections own the slab frame, the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals and the spot-price line.

looks.oneLine: A flat lattice of whole single iPhones, each with its own real drop shadow, washed to 60% in the palette's dark ink, with the five-star proof block floating clear on top of it.
looks.groundSpec: The iphones.LA device wall, tile branch at retheme_lab.mjs:2946-2982. Base fill: th.c1 when its luminance clears 0.55, else th.c2 when that clears it, else the neutral #eceef2. All three palettes here are pale — ca07 c1 #b9f7f6 measures 0.835, pa05 #c6faeb 0.864, cd06 #80dafd 0.618 — so the field is ALWAYS c1 itself and the #eceef2 neutral never fires on this theme. The last draft claimed a deep-palette branch; there is no deep palette here, and the sentence is gone. Lattice: 4 columns x 3 rows, gap 28, each cell scaled to 0.96 of its box, shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offsetX 10, offsetY 16 — no overlap, no rotation. Wash: the palette's dark tone (c1 if lum < 0.3, else c2 if lum < 0.35, else ink) at 0.6, raised to 0.72 when that tone is itself over 0.4. On all three palettes the test resolves to the ink — ca07 #173f3f, pa05 #1b4037, cd06 #1b3d49 — at 0.6, so the wall reads as bright hardware under a deep teal wash, which is the target. HOW THE POOL IS SET: the tile branch filters its own candidates through this theme's neverShow, then narrows to the mustShow prefixes when four or more survive (2960-2966). Naming the prefixes IS the pool; no engine change is needed, and the tilePool hook the audit asked for already exists in this form. Panels go solid at rgba(deep, 0.9) over the wall (2986-2996) — no translucent stat tiles on this theme.
looks.imagery: Six whole single units, every one opened and checked: iphone-15-pro-back-blue (678x1580), iphone-15-pro-back-gold (542x1297), iphone-15-pro-back-white (1430x1634), iphone-15-pro-front-on (809x1615, a dark front face — not a lit screen), iphone-17-pro-back-black (1008x1837), iphone-17-pro-back-silver (799x1668). iphone-hand-back-offer banned, which the audit had kept in the pool — I opened it: the hand was cut away in background removal and left brown finger fragments down the left edge.
iphone-in-hand-screen-on and iphone-screen-on-glow banned — blank white and flat cyan screens that become the brightest objects under the 0.6 wash.

Dead rules replaced with live ones: 'qs-iphone-' became 'qs-' (which reaches every qs- file), 'sam-' gained 'samsung-' beside it because startsWith is literal, and 'ground:bg-web'/'ground:scenes' became the real tokens 'ground:photo'/'ground:scene' plus enforceable 'assets/bg-web/' and 'assets/scenes/' background bans.
Every treatment: entry deleted — lookFaults has no treat: branch, so all of them matched nothing.
Variation 2 rewritten as reviewVariant v3 (three rows, not two); v2 twin-quotes is unreachable because 3055 picks only from [0,3,4,0,3,4].
The seed-offset claim on the strip variation deleted and replaced with the exact engine change at 2102.
Variation 4 deleted: best-buy.png exists in assets/logos but BRAND_LOGO at 2472 maps 22 vehicle make words only, so there is no code path that places it.
mustShow ambiguity resolved: lookFaults reads it as OR (2546), so the list is written so that every prefix in it resolves only to a verified whole-unit iPhone.
looks.collectionNote: PROOF WALL is nine cards that all say the same thing in the same order: five stars, a signed testimonial in the seller's own trade vocabulary, a first name and initial with a Long Beach-area city, and — standing behind all of it — a real photograph or a real lattice of the exact goods the quote is talking about. The family signature is a three-part proof block that is always the loudest object on the card: RATING (five stars plus "4.9 · 200+ local sellers", never four, never three), QUOTE (one sentence in quotation marks from the QUOTES pool at scripts/retheme_lab.mjs:2031, in the theme's grotesque support face, never the display face), SIGNATURE (pin + "Marcus T. · Long Beach, CA" from NAMES2/CITIES2, centred, 26px floor, charSpacing 20). Every card is built on reviewProof (93%) with at least one non-reviewProof sibling layout so no run trips REVIEW_PAGE/r100. Only reviewVariant v3 (three review rows) and v4 (the 200px Instrument Serif quote mark) are reachable in a regular set — line 3055 picks from [0,3,4,0,3,4][sd%6] — so no theme names a reviewFormat option (head:top, rating:free, rating:badge, quote:centered, cta:bar) or a competitor logo: BRAND_LOGO at 2472 maps 22 vehicle make words and nothing else, so best-buy.png, tcgplayer.png, fanatics-inc.png, freestyle-libre.png and pok-mon.png have no code path even though the files exist. HOW THE RULES ARE WRITTEN, which is the change from the last draft: lookFaults (2528-2551) is the only matcher, and it reads neverShow as (a) `ground:<x>` where x is one of slab|tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|flat, (b) `logo:<full src>` — the src is `logo:assets/logos/<id>.png:<colour>`, so a bare `logo:` bans every wordmark and `logo:pok-mon` bans nothing, (c) `assets/…` tested against the background src, so a photograph is banned as `assets/bg-web/<name>` or `assets/scenes/<name>` and never as a bare `scene-…`, and (d) anything else as a literal startsWith on cutout basenames. Entries containing a space are skipped, and `treatment:…` tokens match nothing at all — so every treatment ban in the last draft was decoration. They have been deleted and their intent moved into the prose. mustShow is OR, not AND (2546): a card faults only when NO listed prefix matches ANY cutout, so every prefix in a mustShow list has to be individually safe, and a theme whose ground carries all the product deliberately lists only its ground token, which matches no cutout name and therefore faults the moment any cutout appears. A faulting card is re-seeded once and then ships with a console warning (3671-3675), so rules bite twice, not forever. The negative spine shared by all nine: no ip-gen* renders; no two-up composites in a lattice (the MULTI regex at 2953 drops them); the fifteen verified-bad ids in assets/approved-assets.json never appear anywhere; no cross-category product; no watches as a premise; no competitor scenes; no spotlight/marble/memphis/linen grounds; exactly five stars; and one sentence in one face per headline. Sports has been dropped from the collection (see droppedThemes) and returns when a real sports card cutout or photograph is approved.

looks.name: Studio Lineup Proof
looks.oneLine: An Apple press lineup photograph under a measured tint, with the proof block in the clear half of the frame and the headline naming exactly the line that is in the picture.
looks.groundSpec: A single photograph from assets/scenes, drawn by the scenes path at 3083-3101. These are Apple press images and studio lineups, not shop photography, so the copy never says shelf, counter or storefront. The reachable set is the deck's own scenes and nothing else: for the iphone deck, DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.scenes at 131-132 lists five — scene-flat-iphones (lum 0.526, detail 7.5), scene-studio-blue-trio (0.197, 4.9), scene-studio-green-trio (0.260, 5.7), scene-studio-rose-pair (0.264, 4.3), scene-studio-slate-quad (0.172, 5.6); for the ipad deck, two — scene-flat-ipads (0.343, 8.6) and scene-studio-amber-ipad (0.192, 7.3). webExtra at 3100 adds nothing here because DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts[0] is 'own-apple-cosmic-orange', which does not match its /^iphone/ test. Tint by measurement, not taste: scene-flat-iphones is the one LIGHT photograph and takes the palette's DARK tone at scrim 0.5; the six dark scenes take th.c1 at 0.22-0.30 so the hardware still reads. Every detail figure is under 13, so none takes the 0.62 busy scrim. PALETTES: pp04 (#f2f8ef, 0.922) and pa05 (#c6faeb, 0.864) are pale and pair with the dark scenes; jw05 (#044a51, 0.055) replaces ca07 so the deep branch is reachable at all and scene-flat-iphones has a palette that can carry it — with three pale palettes the theme's own contrast rule fired on every card and its lead photograph could never be picked. scene-studio-slate-quad is the frame the proof block was written for: I opened it, and the hardware sits in the top third with two thirds of clean grey gradient beneath. Copy with no plate behind it takes the over-scrim tone plus a soft carry shadow (2943).
looks.imagery: The photograph is the imagery and it must show the line the headline names. iPHONE headline: scene-flat-iphones, scene-studio-blue-trio, scene-studio-green-trio, scene-studio-rose-pair, scene-studio-slate-quad. iPAD headline: scene-flat-ipads, scene-studio-amber-ipad — the ipad deck rotates inside p.cat 'phones' via APPLE at 2800, so an iPad card is a phones card wearing the iPad deck, not a separate category. THE MACBOOK CARD IS CUT: its three scenes are banned by background rule, its cutouts (macbook-open-angle, macbook-closed-stack, macbook-pair-open-closed, every mac-*) are all in the engine's BLANK regex at 45, own-stock-macbook-open is verified-bad (an Intel-era topcase with a Touch Bar), and QUOTES has no macbook key so a WE BUY MACBOOKS card would draw 'Sold my 15 Pro Max the day the 17 came out.' A foreground cutout is optional; when one is placed it comes from the six verified whole-unit iPhones or the approved ipad- singles, and it never sits over the quote card.
looks.copy: Calm and same-day; the seller measures the shop in hours, not promises. Headline: iPHONE · iPAD. Selling point: WRITTEN OFFER IN MINUTES. Second selling point: CASH THE SAME DAY. Quote: "Texted photos at noon, had cash by 3pm." Signature: Priya R. · Torrance, CA. The iPad card keeps a device-agnostic quote from the phones pool — 'Texted photos at noon, had cash by 3pm.', 'Met me at work. Five minutes, done.' or 'No "final offer" games. Number stood.' — and never the four iPhone-specific ones, because QUOTES at 2031 has no ipad key and the lookup at 2069 falls to QUOTES.phones.
variations: Quote-mark card — reviewVariant v4: the 200px Instrument Serif mark in th.accent at card.left+18, quote indented to card.left+130 at 38px, over scene-studio-slate-quad on jw05.
Three-row strip — reviewVariant v3: three rows at 942x86, rx 43, over scene-studio-blue-trio.
iPad card — scene-studio-amber-ipad (lum 0.192) at th.c1 0.24, headline WE BUY iPADS, items line PRO, AIR, MINI, quote "Texted photos at noon, had cash by 3pm."

Flat-lay card — scene-flat-iphones (lum 0.526, the one light scene) on jw05, taking the palette's dark tone at scrim 0.5 per the light-photograph rule, headline WE BUY iPHONES, quote "Cracked back, still paid what they quoted."
fixesApplied: Mac and iPad quote mismatch resolved by cutting the MacBook card and pinning the iPad card to the three device-agnostic sentences in QUOTES.phones, rather than shipping a theme that depends on an engine change. ENGINE CHANGE STILL WANTED — 2031, add ipad and macbook keys to QUOTES and key the lookups at 2069 and 2159 on the deck rather than p.cat; until then the phones pool is the only honest source.

Palette set fixed structurally: ca07 (0.835) replaced by jw05 (0.055) so the theme is no longer three pale palettes, which made its own 'on a pale palette pick a scene under 0.30' rule fire every card and put scene-flat-iphones permanently out of reach.
Variation 3's scene-flat-ipads (0.343) replaced by scene-studio-amber-ipad (0.192), which clears the pale ceiling; scene-flat-ipads stays in the allowed set for the deeper palette only.

looks.name: Scale Counter Proof
looks.oneLine: A gold piece cast large into the ground under a soft diagonal window shadow, with the proof block on the lit side and a quote about being weighed in front of you.
looks.groundSpec: The cast branch at 2929-2942, every number verified against the source. The gold cutout is drawn into the ground at min(W*0.62/iw, H*0.92/ih), translated to (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12 rad, globalAlpha 0.92, shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offsetX 24 offsetY 30. Over it one blurred diagonal window shadow (blur 26) and a wider penumbra (blur 60) fall from upper right to lower left, at strength 0.58 on a pale palette and 0.5 otherwise. PALE BRANCH (lumHex(c1) > 0.55) applies on pp02 (#fdf4ee, 0.918) and gl02 (#ffd2ca, 0.716): fill c1, then the palette's own ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient from accent 0.18 to ink 0.10, then a white corner sheen at 0.12 — without that body the card is the 'too bland, what is this light theme' failure. Type scrim on the pale branch is c2 when its luminance is under 0.45, otherwise the ink, at 0.30: pp02 c2 #e5ddd5 measures 0.732 so the scrim is the brown ink #4a3220, and gl02 c2 #ebbbac is 0.62 so its scrim is #4d2f2a. DEEP BRANCH on jw07 (#054e2f, 0.057, jeweller's green): no ink body, the 0.10 white sheen only, scrim c1 at 0.22, so the metal keeps its warmth against the green. Panels go solid at rgba(deep, 0.9). The cast object IS the ground, so the Hero Product layer is not drawn a second time and nothing can sit over the quote.
looks.imagery: Lead: gold-chains-pile (2048x1718) — I opened it, a coiled pile of heavy curb and cuban chain, real gold jewellery on transparency, and the object a gold buyer's ad should open with. Behind it, the rest of the approved gold shelf, all of which the hero picker at 2833 may draw: gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-scrap-mixed, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-bracelet-pair, gold-rings-scatter, gold-necklace-single, gold-class-ring, gold-earrings-pile, gold-chains, gold-jewelry, gold-bars-stack, gold-bar-single, gold-bars, gold-bars-row, gold-bars-fan, gold-coins-pile, gold-scale-weighing. gold-scale-weighing is NO LONGER the lead: I opened it and it is a laboratory precision balance in a glass case with a small cluster of gold on the pan — cast at 62% width it fills the card with a white instrument and reads as a lab, not as gold. It is one of seventeen in the pool, so it lands on roughly one card in seventeen, and when it does the quote is the one it illustrates.
looks.copy: Estate-shop voice: weight, spot, testing, respect. Nothing about melt value in dollars, nothing unbounded. Headline: SELL YOUR GOLD. Selling point: WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, PAID AT SPOT. Second selling point: FREE WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. Quote: "Weighed it in front of me, no games." Signature: Rosa V. · Downey, CA. Seal is DISCREET or TRUSTED — never INSURED, which is the car buyer's seal. Instrument Serif is in the engine's DECOR list at 1093, so it carries the money word and never body copy.
variations: Chains card — gold-chains-pile cast, quote "Cuban link paid by weight at a real spot rate.", items line CHAINS · RINGS · BRACELETS.
Scale card — gold-scale-weighing cast, used only where the quote is "Weighed it in front of me, no games." so the instrument is illustrating its own sentence.
Estate card — gold-jewelry-mixed cast on the jw07 green deep branch, quote "Handled my mom's estate with respect."

Quote-mark card — reviewVariant v4: the 200px Instrument Serif mark in th.accent at card.left+18, quote indented to card.left+130 at 38px, the quote card narrowed to the left of the cast piece. Replaces the deleted badge-rating variation.
fixesApplied: Lead changed from gold-scale-weighing to gold-chains-pile, and the scale demoted to the single card whose quote it illustrates — I opened the file and confirmed it reads as a glass-cased laboratory balance.
Variation 4 deleted: rating:'badge' is a reviewFormat option (2166-2171) and reviewFormat runs only under REVIEW100. Replaced with reviewVariant v4.

Dead neverShow entry 'gold-rolex-watch' removed — it is assets/bg-web/gold-rolex-watch.jpg, not a cutout — and replaced by a blanket 'assets/bg-web/' background ban plus live cutout bans on gold-pocket-watch and gold-watch-luxury, both of which ARE approved and would otherwise put a watch on the card.

The audit's LAB_SLAB warning dropped as incorrect: slabFrame returns immediately unless the category is pokemon or sports (2378), so no run flag can convert a gold card to a slab. The stray 'treatment:slab-frame-override' entry would have matched nothing in any case.

Palette count raised from two to three so no single palette runs half the theme, which was the audit's actual concern. I did NOT take its suggested pa05: pa05 is a cool pastel teal with a magenta accent and the owner's palette-fit rule puts gold on warm palettes. pp02 (warm cream), jw07 (jeweller's green) and gl02 (warm peach, ink #4d2f2a) all carry approval records and all fit the category.
groundSpec corrected: the pale-branch scrim resolves to the brown ink on both pale palettes, because neither c2 clears the engine's 0.45 test — the last draft named c2.

looks.name: Coin Tray Proof
looks.oneLine: A flat lattice of coin groups — rolls, albums, jars, trays, stacks — on a bright field under a deep wash, with a quote about key dates being priced properly.
looks.groundSpec: Same lattice engine as the device wall: 4 x 3, gap 28, cells at 0.96, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16, no overlap, no rotation, 240px width floor, and the pool set by this theme's own mustShow/neverShow at 2960-2966. On jw05 (c1 #044a51, lum 0.055) and du08 (#5593ef, 0.290) neither c1 nor c2 clears 0.55, so the base field is the neutral #eceef2 and the wash is c1 at 0.6 — a dealer's tray under a deep teal or indigo light, which is the target. On cd04 (#91e2a2, 0.630) the field is the mint c1 itself; c1 is not under 0.3 and c2 #5cd094 (0.495) is not under 0.35, so the wash resolves to the ink #263f2b at 0.6. Mix flat wide objects (coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-rolls-paper) with round ones so the lattice has rhythm rather than twelve discs. Panels solid at rgba(deep, 0.9).
looks.imagery: Seven coin cells, all approved, all over the width floor: coin-album-pages (1987x1925), coin-collection-tray (2048x1435 — I opened it: a real dealer's felt tray of graded-looking loose coins in cells), coin-jar-full (1251x1810), coin-loose-pile (1935x1383), coin-rolls-paper (1802x1569), coin-stack (555x276), coin-stack-silver (1817x2048). One coin GROUP per cell: rolls, jars, trays and piles are single subjects. The engine's MULTI regex at 2953 already removes coin-graded-fan-three, coin-silver-dollar-pair and coin-single-large from any lattice, so the theme does not repeat those exclusions as wall rules. coin-slab is out: I checked it and it is a single Morgan-type dollar at 144x144 — the lowest-resolution file in the pool and not a slab at all. The 'coin-slab' ban also removes coin-slabs-stack and coin-slab-graded, which is correct, because the slab frame is Pokemon and sports only (2378). SUBJECTS.coins at 2504 defines the subject as /^(coin-|silver-coins|gold-coins)/, so no gold pocket watch, dental gold or ring scatter can reach this lattice through the engine — the last draft opened that door in prose only, and the prose is gone.
looks.copy: Numismatic and specific — key dates, junk silver by face value, Morgans checked date by date. Never a dollar promise. Headline: WE BUY COINS. Items line: KEY DATES · JUNK SILVER · SLABS. Selling point: SLABBED OR RAW, PRICED BY DATE. Second selling point: CASH THE SAME DAY. Quote: "Key dates priced right, not junk rate." Signature: Kevin L. · Lakewood, CA. Seal is DISCREET or TRUSTED, never INSURED.
variations: Three-row strip — reviewVariant v3: three rows at 942x86 carrying "Knew more about my collection than I did.", "Morgans checked date by date. Found two I missed." and "Junk silver by the face value, paid on the spot." ENGINE CHANGE REQUIRED — 2102, qs[r % qs.length] with r fixed at 0,1,2 means every strip card opens with the same sentence; change it to qs[(seed + r) % qs.length] as reviewFormat already does at 2236.
Album card — the lattice leans on coin-album-pages and coin-collection-tray, quote "Dad's albums went to someone who cared."

Junk-silver card — the lattice leans on coin-rolls-paper, coin-jar-full and coin-stack-silver, quote "Junk silver by the face value, paid on the spot." Replaces the deleted bullion-adjacent card, which needed gold-coins-pile.

Typewriter money word — Special Elite held to the short money word only; the items line and quote stay in Libre Franklin. Special Elite carries a 16px minimum bump at 1101 and sits in the DECOR list at 1093, so it never takes body copy.
fixesApplied: The gold hole closed with one live rule: 'gold-' bans the whole family including gold-coins-pile, so there is no exception clause to leak through. The audit's fix contradicted itself here — it added 'gold-' and then tried to keep gold-coins-pile, which literal startsWith cannot do. Variation 3 was rewritten so nothing depends on the exception.
coin-slab dropped from the pool and banned, with the prefix also covering coin-slabs-stack and coin-slab-graded — a 144x144 single dollar is both mislabelled and under the lattice's resolution floor.

The one-object-per-cell inconsistency resolved: the redundant coin-graded-fan-three and coin-silver-dollar-pair bans are gone because MULTI at 2953 already removes them, and the rule is restated as one coin GROUP per cell so rolls, jars and trays are consistent with piles.
The unachievable seed-offset claim deleted from variation 1 and replaced with the exact engine change at 2102.

pp02 replaced by cd04 so all three palettes are cool, which is the owner's palette fit for coins, and the groundSpec rewritten for cd04's actual branch — c1 clears 0.55 so the field is the mint itself and the wash falls to the ink, not to a cream-and-brown reading.

'Typewriter money word' KEPT, and the audit's correction reversed: STYLE at 414 carries a dedicated typewriter bucket holding Special Elite, added by the owner ('sickest font keep this!!!!! use it'), and FACE_STYLES.coins at 429 lists typewriter. Special Elite is in vintage as well, but typewriter is its own live style, not a name the theme invented.
Dead 'treatment:' entries removed and the background bans rewritten as enforceable 'assets/bg-web/' and 'assets/scenes/' rules.

looks.oneLine: A single sterling piece cast large into the ground under a diagonal window shadow, with a quote about sterling being sorted honestly from plate.
looks.groundSpec: The cast branch at 2929-2942. The silver piece is drawn into the ground at min(W*0.62/iw, H*0.92/ih), centred at (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset 24/30, then the diagonal window shadow (blur 26) and penumbra (blur 60) at strength 0.5. Both palettes are DEEP — du08 c1 #5593ef measures 0.290 and jw05 #044a51 measures 0.055, so lumHex(c1) > 0.55 is false on both and the pale branch never fires: no ink body, no accent gradient, just the 0.10 white corner sheen and the type scrim at c1 0.22, which keeps the metal cool and bright on du08 and lamp-lit on jw05. jw05's accent #febbd3 stays on the quote mark and the rating and never takes a large field. Panels go solid at rgba(deep, 0.9). looks.imagery: One sterling object, cast. Lead: silver-flatware-set (1989x1919) — I opened it: seven pieces of antique sterling flatware, forks, spoons and a knife, laid out in a row, real hallmarked metal. Pool: silver-flatware-set, silver-candlesticks, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-bars-row, silver-bar-single, silver-flatware. silver-coins-tube and silver-coins-spill are OUT and banned — coins are their own category and their own theme in this collection. silver-serving-tray and silver-tea-set are rejected assets and never in the pool. Note silver-flatware is only 364x587 and casts at about 1.8x on a 1080 card; it is the one soft source in the pool and is the reason for the clamp named in fixesApplied.
looks.copy: Hallmark literate and unhurried — maker's marks, weight, what is plated. Headline: WE BUY STERLING. Items line: FLATWARE · BARS · ROUNDS · JEWELRY. Selling point: STERLING SORTED FROM PLATED, FREE. Second selling point: BARS AND ROUNDS PAID AT SPOT. Quote: "Honest about what was plated." Signature: Grace N. · Carson, CA. Seal is DISCREET or TRUSTED, never INSURED.
variations: Flatware card — silver-flatware-set cast on jw05, quote "Silverware set paid by weight, fair."
Bullion card — silver-bars-stack cast on du08, quote "Bars and rounds at spot, no haggling."

Estate card — silver-candlesticks cast, quote "Grandmother's tea set, treated like it mattered." The tea-set cutout itself is a rejected asset; the sentence stands on the candlesticks, which are real weighted sterling.
Quote-mark card — reviewVariant v4: the 200px Instrument Serif mark in th.accent at card.left+18, quote indented to card.left+130 at 38px. Replaces the deleted centred-quote variation.
fixesApplied: REJECT answered by moving the theme off a ground it could not select. abstract fires only on FACESYS.forceAbs or sd % 12 === 7 (2886), so the old recipe got its ground one card in twelve or by setting LAB_ABS=1, which would have forced an abstract ground onto every other theme in the run. Ground is now 'cast', which lookGround pins directly at 2911.

The whole allowed-kinds paragraph deleted: GK is a run-wide list from assets/approved-grounds.json indexed by seed (2885), never a theme property, so naming velvet-du08 and duo-jw05 described a LAB_GROUNDS setting rather than this theme.
The imageless-card risk removed: on a cast ground the product is drawn INTO the background, so this theme can no longer render as a bare gradient when the hero fails to clear the text.
Category bleed fixed: silver-coins-tube and silver-coins-spill removed from the pool and banned with a live 'silver-coins' prefix, so they stay in Coin Tray Proof.

mustShow changed from ['ground:abs','silver-'] to ['ground:cast','silver-'], and tested for the OR reading: every approved silver- id that survives the bans is genuine sterling or bullion, so no cutout can satisfy the rule and still show the wrong thing.
Variation 4 deleted: quote:'centered' is a reviewFormat option (2205-2208) reachable only under REVIEW100. Replaced with reviewVariant v4.
Named 'Sterling Cast Proof' now that the velvet case is gone; the id is unchanged so the audit trail still matches.

looks.name: Box And Meter Proof
looks.oneLine: A real photograph of branded retail test strips under a measured tint, with a discreet, box-counted proof block over it and no cutout anywhere on the card.
looks.groundSpec: One of only two photographic themes in the collection, permitted because the photograph shows recognisable retail packaging rather than a macro of an unlabelled object. The bg-web path is at 3070-3082. Tint by measurement: strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-2 (lum 0.616, detail 13.22) is LIGHT and takes the palette's dark tone at scrim 0.5. strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-3 (0.551, 15.64) is light AND busy — over the 14 detail line — so it takes th.c1 at 0.62 on these pale palettes. strips-glucose-meter-test-strip-2 (0.191, 9.87) is dark and calm and takes th.c1 at 0.42-0.50. The two Contour Next photographs carry no measured row; I opened both and they are calm, low-detail and bright — a white vial on a pale grey surface — so they follow the light rule and take the palette's dark tone at 0.5, not the busy 0.62 the last draft assumed. All three palettes are pale — pp04 #f2f8ef 0.922, cd04 #91e2a2 0.630, ca07 #b9f7f6 0.835 — which is the owner's 'strips clean' fit. Copy with no plate behind it takes the over-scrim tone plus a soft carry shadow.
looks.imagery: Five photographs, every one opened: strips-contour-next-test-strips-1 (a Contour Next vial with one loose strip beside it, branded label full-face), strips-contour-next-test-strips-2 (the same vial straight on, label sharp), strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-2 (a OneTouch Select Plus vial with branded OneTouch strips fanned across white), strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-3 (the same vial and strips, angled), strips-glucose-meter-test-strip-2 (a Bayer Contour 50-sensor vial with a pile of strips on black — despite the filename there is NO meter in this photograph, so it is never captioned as a meter card). NO CUTOUT APPEARS ON THIS THEME AT ALL. strip-kit-meter is verified-bad — the meter bezel carries a fabricated wordmark — and strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan and strip-boxes-pile-large are blank kraft cartons and blank white cards, the owner's blank-unbranded rejection reason verbatim, and all three are named in the engine's BLANK regex at 45. The photograph is the whole imagery.
looks.copy: Private, practical, counted by the box. Never a health claim, never a dollar promise, never a displayed reading. Headline: WE BUY TEST STRIPS. Items line: CONTOUR NEXT · ONE TOUCH · FREESTYLE, and the first brand named must be the brand visible in the photograph. Selling point: QUOTED BY THE BOX, PAID THE SAME DAY. Second selling point: NO MAIL IT IN AND WAIT WEEKS. Quote: "Short-dated boxes still got a fair number." Signature: Erin W. · Bellflower, CA. Seal is DISCREET or PRIVATE — never INSURED. No wordmark: freestyle-libre.png and dexcom.png exist in assets/logos but BRAND_LOGO carries no medical brands, so there is no code path to place either.
variations: Contour card — ground strips-contour-next-test-strips-1.jpg, items line opening CONTOUR NEXT, quote "Quoted by the box, paid by the box.", no wordmark.

OneTouch card — ground strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-2.jpg (lum 0.616, the light one) taking the palette's dark tone at scrim 0.5, items line opening ONE TOUCH, quote "Simple and discreet. Boxes gone, paid fairly."

Dark-vial card — ground strips-glucose-meter-test-strip-2.jpg (lum 0.191) at th.c1 0.44, quote "Text a photo of the boxes, got a number back in minutes." Called a vial card, not a meter card, because there is no meter in the frame.
Discreet card — reviewVariant v4 quote mark, the seal row reading DISCREET · PRIVATE · SAME DAY and the sticker ON THE SPOT.
fixesApplied: The cutout pool is now empty rather than cut to strip-kit-meter as the audit proposed: strip-kit-meter is verified-bad (a fabricated wordmark on the meter bezel) since the audit ran. The three blank-packaging cutouts are banned by a single live 'strip-' prefix.

mustShow deliberately carries only its ground token. It matches no cutout basename, so under the OR reading at 2546 the moment ANY cutout reaches this card lookFaults raises 'mustShow satisfied by nothing' and the card is re-seeded — which is exactly what a theme with no honest cutout wants.

Ground pool cut to the five photographs that show branded retail packaging and no person, and the five rejects are banned as enforceable 'assets/bg-web/…' background rules: CGM sensors, a bare arm, two hands holding meters that display a reading of 53, and an unlabelled white vial.
Variation 1 deleted — freestyle-libre.png has no code path — and the Libre grounds it needed are banned outright.
Variation 3 rebuilt without strip-kit-meter, and renamed away from 'meter' because I opened strips-glucose-meter-test-strip-2 and there is no meter in it.

Display face changed so it is visibly not the support face, which was the audit's real point. I did NOT take its Special Elite: this is a medical-supply ad and the owner's fit for strips is 'clean'. Saira Condensed is a condensed face, first in FACE_STYLES.strips at 431, and reads clearly against the Satoshi grotesque.

ENGINE CHANGE REQUIRED (BLOCKING) — 2818, `if (!use) continue` currently kills this category outright. CUTS.strips resolves to strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan and strip-boxes-pile-large, all three are in BLANK, so ok, catPool and wide are all empty and NO strips card is built at all today. Make the hero optional when the theme's ground supplies the product: `const noHero = !use && look && /^(slab|photo|scene|deep)$/.test(look.ground); if (!use && !noHero) continue;` and guard every later use of cutSrc.

Without it five of the ten strips photographs are still first-choice candidates and roughly a quarter of cards ship with a warning after their one re-seed.
ENGINE CHANGE WANTED — 220, add bgcat:'strips' to CATEGORY_COPY.strips so the photo path fires on every card instead of only when sd % 2 === 1 (3070).

looks.name: Graded Window Proof
looks.oneLine: The whole card is a graded slab: the headline sits on the label like a grade line, a real PSA 10 Charizard photograph fills the window under a palette wash, and the proof block is scaled in beneath it.
looks.groundSpec: slabFrame at 2377, scoped by the engine to pokemon and sports only (2378) — graded coin slabs are real but the owner has not approved that extension, so coins never reach this treatment. Geometry from SLAB at 2376: frame sports-slab-graded.webp at 1572x1425 drawn full height on a 1080x1080 ground, centred, shadow blur 50 offsetY 18. Label box [0.075, 0.055, 0.925, 0.265] — the top 5.5% to 26.5% — filled with a 0.06 whisper of th.c1 so it stays paper-white with dark ink, a 2px divider at 68% of the label width and a procedural barcode from 72% to 96%. Window box [0.075, 0.31, 0.925, 0.95] painted th.c1 at 0.97, then the photograph clipped and drawn to cover at scale max((w-12)/iw, (h-12)/ih) * 1.02, then washed with th.c1 at 0.66 (0.55 for a fitted cutout), then a corner gradient from c2 or accent 0.35 to c1 0. Ground scrim 0.001 — the slab is the whole picture. Headlines are forced to the palette's dark ink with no gradient, shadow or stroke, and everything that is not a headline is scaled into the window with a clear pad. On cd06 (#80dafd) and cd04 (#91e2a2) the wash reads as coloured glass; on io03 (#ecefff, 0.868) drop it to 0.55 or the card in the window disappears.
looks.imagery: In the window: pokemon-charizard-card-1.jpg (lum 0.353, detail 9.21) or pokemon-charizard-card-2.jpg (0.410, 15.47). I opened both — each is a genuine photograph of a PSA GEM MT 10 graded 1999 Base Set Charizard standing on a display table, with a second slab behind it. slabFrame fills the window from WEBBG['pokemon'] first (2388-2390), and that pool is exactly these two files, so the window always holds a real card. poke-slabs-trio is REMOVED from this theme: it is three blank pastel slabs with empty windows, it is in the engine's BLANK regex at 45, and it shows no Pokemon card. If neither photograph loads the card is re-seeded rather than falling back to it. NO PRODUCT CUTOUT APPEARS ON THIS THEME: the frame and the card are both drawn into the ground, not placed as cutout layers. WATERMARK — both photographs carry a small photographer's mark in the lower right. I worked the geometry: the window is about 1012x691 at aspect 1.465 and the source is 1920x1280 at 1.500, so the cover fit crops only about 20px a side and the mark lands INSIDE the window under the 0.66 wash. This has to be fixed before the theme ships.
looks.copy: Collector-fluent: alt arts, comps, PSA 10s, ETBs. No bulk-only dismissal, no invented grade. Headline on the label: WE BUY POKEMON CARDS — printed POKEMON without the accent, because the display face carries no É glyph. Selling point: PRICED OFF REAL COMPS, NOT A LOWBALL. Second selling point: SLABS AND RAW, SORTED FAIRLY. Quote: "They knew what the alt arts were worth." Signature: Jordan K. · Cerritos, CA. TCGPLAYER and GAMESTOP may be named in words — both are in CHALLENGE.pokemon.names at 279 and both are on the owner's recognition list — but never as a wordmark.
variations: Grade block — the right third of the label carries a 10 / GEM MT block and the procedural barcode; the left two thirds carry the money word.
Moonbreon card — quote "Moonbreon priced off real comps, not a lowball." over pokemon-charizard-card-2.jpg.
Binder card — quote "Childhood binder, Charizard included. Fair." over pokemon-charizard-card-1.jpg at the engine's fixed 0.66 window wash. Replaces the deleted variation that asked for a 0.72 wash.
Comps card — kicker GOT A TCGPLAYER QUOTE?, headline WE BUY POKEMON CARDS, quote "Got real value for my binder, not pawn prices.", no wordmark. Replaces the deleted WE MATCH TCGPLAYER variation.
fixesApplied: The demand-and-ban contradiction removed: 'sports-slab' is gone from neverShow and 'sports-slab-graded' is gone from mustShow. The frame is drawn into the ground by slabFrame and never appears as a cutout layer, so it could never have satisfied mustShow in the first place — mustShow now carries only the ground token, which faults the moment any cutout reaches the card, and that is the correct behaviour for a theme whose imagery is entirely in the ground.

The audit's LAB_SLAB requirement is OBSOLETE and removed. Line 3476 now reads `FACESYS.slab || (look && look.ground === 'slab') || (!look && /pokemon|sports/.test(p.cat) && sd % 3 === 0)`, so a theme that declares ground:'slab' gets the frame on every card, and the seed-driven one-in-three path applies only when no look is attached.
Variation 3's 0.72 wash claim deleted — the wash is hard-coded at 2411 as rgba(th.c1, cut ? 0.55 : 0.66) with no per-card control.
Variation 4 deleted: tcgplayer.png exists but BRAND_LOGO maps 22 vehicle make words only. TCGPLAYER survives as a printed word, which CHALLENGE.pokemon.names already sanctions.

The Pokémon wordmark is banned, but with a rule that works: the audit's 'logo:pok-mon' would have matched nothing, because inkedLogo builds the src as `logo:assets/logos/pok-mon.png:<colour>`. A bare 'logo:' bans every wordmark on the theme and is checked at 2542.
poke-slabs-trio removed from the imagery entirely — three empty slabs — and the fallback documented as a re-seed instead.

NEW, NOT IN THE AUDIT: ENGINE CHANGE REQUIRED (BLOCKING) — 2818. `if (!use) continue` kills this whole category before any ground runs. CUTS.pokemon resolves to poke-slabs-trio alone, which is in BLANK, so ok, catPool and wide are all empty and NO Pokemon card is built at all today. Same one-line fix as Box And Meter: make the hero optional when the theme's ground supplies the product.

NEW, NOT IN THE AUDIT: ENGINE CHANGE REQUIRED — 2409, bias the window's cover crop up and left so the photographer's watermark in the lower right of both Charizard files falls outside the clip: draw at `WB.x + (WB.w - w)/2 - w*0.05, WB.y + (WB.h - h)/2 - h*0.05`. The window and the source are within 2% of the same aspect ratio, so the current centred cover leaves the mark visible under the wash. The alternative is to re-export both photographs cropped above the mark.

looks.collectionNote:
CLINIC is the pale, cool, quiet collection — cards you would believe were printed by a counter, not a feed. Every one sits on a near-white or pale-cool ground, carries exactly ONE cool accent in tones (medical blue, teal or clinic green — never magenta, violet, mustard or brown), sets its numbers in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono / DM Mono), and speaks in a plain counter voice with no urgency words. No graffiti, script, handwriting, blackletter, comic, horror or novelty face appears anywhere in it.

WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED, AND WHY — five things I checked in the files, all of which override the original recipes:

1. THE STRIPS DECK RENDERS NOTHING TODAY. This is the fact that ended seven of the ten themes, and the audit did not have it. assets/approved-assets.json (owner pass, 2026-09-03) now leaves exactly three approved strip cutouts — strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large — and BLANK (retheme_lab.mjs:45) names all three. So at 2819 `ok` is empty, catPool and wide are empty too, `use` is null, and 2821 does `continue`: the frame is skipped before a ground, a photo or a headline is ever chosen. strip-kit-meter (the fabricated 'Sinatore' meter), strip-kit, strip-meter-hand, strip-box-single, strip-boxes-stack, strip-boxes-row-five, strip-box-open-vials, strip-boxes-cash and strip-vials-pile are all in the rejected list. any competitor the phones deck does not define: only ECOATM, GAZELLE, BACK MARKET, APPLE TRADE IN, BEST BUY, VERIZON, T-MOBILE and the generics A RESELLER, THE KIOSK, THE MALL KIOSK may be named (CHALLENGE.phones, line 267), and the category line is BUYBACK OFFERS

looks.name: Supply Stencil
looks.oneLine: A supply-room card: the shelf laid out as a flat device wall and the headline cut in stencil, with bracket ticks instead of plates so nothing softens it.
looks.groundSpec: Tile ground, 2974-2988. pp05 c1 #eef9f5 (lum 0.93) is the light fill; 4 by 3 lattice, gap 28, cells scaled 0.96 with the 24px inset, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16. looks.collectionNote:
CLINIC is the pale, cool, quiet collection — cards you would believe were printed by a counter, not a feed. Every one sits on a near-white or pale-cool ground, carries exactly ONE cool accent in tones (medical blue, teal or clinic green — never magenta, violet, mustard or brown), sets its numbers in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono / DM Mono), and speaks in a plain counter voice with no urgency words. No graffiti, script, handwriting, blackletter, comic, horror or novelty face appears anywhere in it.

WHAT THE REPAIR CHANGED, AND WHY — five things I checked in the files, all of which override the original recipes:

1. THE STRIPS DECK RENDERS NOTHING TODAY. This is the fact that ended seven of the ten themes, and the audit did not have it. assets/approved-assets.json (owner pass, 2026-09-03) now leaves exactly three approved strip cutouts — strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large — and BLANK (retheme_lab.mjs:45) names all three. So at 2819 `ok` is empty, catPool and wide are empty too, `use` is null, and 2821 does `continue`: the frame is skipped before a ground, a photo or a headline is ever chosen. strip-kit-meter (the fabricated 'Sinatore' meter), strip-kit, strip-meter-hand, strip-box-single, strip-boxes-stack, strip-boxes-row-five, strip-box-open-vials, strip-boxes-cash and strip-vials-pile are all in the rejected list. A strips theme is not a weak theme now — it is a theme that produces zero cards. Every strips theme is therefore dropped, not patched.

2. THE PHOTOGRAPH CANNOT BE THE IDENTITY. bg-web scored 28% and round-one law #7 forbids it as a theme's primary identity; on top of that no strips photo has a row in assets/backdrop-lum.json, so the bright/busy branches the four photo themes were written around are unreachable (lum defaults to 0.3 at the photo branch) — the audit proved this for Contour Blue and OneTouch Green and it is true of all ten strips photographs. No theme in the repaired collection uses assets/bg-web or assets/scenes at all, and none depends on a data row or a code change that has not been made.

3. THE COLLECTION MOVED TO THE DECKS THAT HAVE HONEST PICTURES. The clinic look is a look, not a category, so it now runs on the three cool decks with verified shelves: phones (23 approved iPhone cutouts, and the deck rotates iPhone/iPhone/iPhone/iPad/iPad/MacBook at 2799), coins (12) and silver (11). Four themes keep their identity and their id and are re-based (Counter White, Mail-In Beat, Supply Stencil keep their palettes, faces and ground build; every audit fix that still applies is applied); the rest are new.

4. ONLY TILE AND CAST ARE DECLARED. They are the two grounds the engine actually sets and the auditor can actually confirm (__tileBg / __castBg at 2548), they are the two that measured highest (tile 100%, cast 50%), and both ARE imagery: the ground itself is drawn from approved cutouts, so a card carries a picture even on a layout with no cutout layer. paper and deep are gone from this collection on purpose — the Lined Paper family picks its sheet by seed (2660) and its highlighter and sticky colours by seed (2683/2685) out of fixed pastel arrays that contain pink, orange and violet (2642/2643), so this collection's one-cool-accent rule is unenforceable there; and a 'deep' ground draws no imagery of its own.

5. EVERY NAMED ASSET WAS OPENED. Findings that changed the rules: coin-silver-dollar-pair is a pair of Morgan-design dollars dated 1988, a year the Mint never struck a Morgan — banned. coin-rolls-paper is rolls of ONE EURO coins and coin-jar-full is a jar of mixed change with euros in it — banned on a Long Beach card. silver-bar-single is stamped WILD GOLD and silver-bars-stack is stamped 999 GOLD — bars that say GOLD under a SILVER headline, banned; silver-bars carries no hallmark or weight at all. silver-coins-spill has a physical bitcoin token in the spill — banned. coin-slabs-stack and coin-graded-fan-three are holders with blank white labels — kept out of every positive list. iphone-17-pro-back-black/-silver are Pro backs with the three-lens corner square (15/16 Pro geometry) filed under a 17 name — honest as wall stock under the generic iPHONE headline, never named as a model. own-stock-macbook-stack has tapered shells lower in the stack, so the MacBook rotation is pinned to qs-device-macbook-air / -pro, both current M-series.

TO BRING STRIPS BACK, one asset is needed, not a theme: a recognisable retail product cut from photography — the Contour Next bottle in assets/bg-web/strips-contour-next-test-strips-2.jpg is the obvious source — registered as a cutout, ticked into approved-assets.json and kept out of BLANK. Until that exists, DIABETIC SUPPLIES cannot be advertised with a picture, and this collection does not pretend otherwise.

looks.name: Hot Wall
looks.oneLine: Twelve single Apple units laid flat in a 4x3 lattice, washed to near-black, with the deck's money word knocked out across the middle and the phone plate hot in the palette accent at the foot.
looks.groundSpec: Engine tile ground, 4 cols x 3 rows, 28px gaps, each cell scaled to 0.96 of its box with a real drop shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offset +10/+16) - no overlap, no ghosting. On ca07 the lattice paints on c1 #b9f7f6 (lum 0.835, above the 0.55 gate, so it keeps the pale cyan) and the wall then takes the dark tone, ink #173f3f at 0.6; the devices survive as bright silhouettes. Panels over the wall go SOLID: retheme_lab.mjs:2998 fills every plate between 150x60 and full-bleed with the deep tone at 0.9 and re-inks its small copy to #ffffff, so a stat tile over a device wall is never grey on grey. THE BAND CLAIM IS GONE: no layout here ships an edge-to-edge band. The number rides ctaCard's 760x194 rx-28 card at y838, and the money plate - when the money word sits over one - takes accent #d8360a flat and is re-cut to hug the word at fs*1.3 tall with a seed-chosen corner (soft/pill/round/slant/square). PALE VS DEEP: pale-ground only. On pa05 nothing changes structurally - lattice #c6faeb, wash ink #1b4037 at 0.6, accent #c44fbd. A deep palette would drop the lattice to neutral #eceef2 and the wash to c1 and lose the cyan-under-accent contrast that is the whole point, so deep palettes are out. If a wall cannot reach four cells the engine draws a cast instead; because this theme declares tile, such a card is re-seeded rather than shipped.
looks.imagery: THE WALL IS WHATEVER APPLE LINE THE CARD IS ON, and the theme owns the stock for all three. iPhone cards (three in six): iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-15-pro-back-blue, iphone-15-pro-back-gold, iphone-15-pro-back-white and own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 - six whole single backs, each one opened and checked; twelve cells over six files means each appears exactly twice and, at (4r+c+sd) mod 6, no repeat is ever adjacent in a row or a column. own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 is the only own-apple file that is a bare unit (its bottom edge is slightly warped in the render); it carries the orange the owner calls the money maker. iPad cards (two in six): ipad-angle-tilt-back, ipad-back-camera, ipad-front-screen-off, ipad-mini-single - four modern, home-button-free single tablets, one per column, each repeating down its three rows. MacBook cards (one in six): the qs-sheet-mba-/qs-sheet-mbp- press family, twelve in name order, nine Air bodies and three Pro, M1 through M5, every one a single machine lid-open front-on at the same eye level on the same blue wave wallpaper - the wall is a spec sheet and the repetition is the point. looks.collectionNote: STREET POSTER is the fly-posted end of the library: eight bills, not eight ideas. The seven house rules are rewritten here against the code, because four of the ten original rules described a poster the engine cannot build. (1) ONE money word. Its real range is 128-226px, not 240-420: reviewProof 128, stepsFlow 142, trustSeal 158, bandKnockout 188, hudTech 196, checklistHero 212, voltStack 226. It is left-ranged only on checklistHero (left 76) and stepsFlow (left 84); trustSeal, voltStack, hudTech and reviewProof centre it, and no look can move that, so the "hard 72px left margin" claim is gone. retheme_lab.mjs:1013 gives it a FLAT fill (th.accent, or th.onAccent over its plate) and deletes the gradient, so "never gradient-filled" is true and enforced. checklistHero and voltStack keep the layout's black keyline (8-9px) around that flat fill — the collection's one permitted outline; neonNight, whose two headlines are fill:'rgba(0,0,0,0)' plus a coloured stroke and a 38-42 blur glow, is now banned from all eight for exactly that reason. (2) Exactly TWO type families per card, from the styles that measured 49-60% (stencil 60, grotesque 56, typewriter 50, tech 50, condensed 49) plus one slab at 44%; street 24, script 22 and rounded 20 stay banned. A look sets th.faces directly, so this one is real. Note the length limits at retheme_lab.mjs:1099: Special Elite drops to Oswald/Big Shoulders/Barlow Condensed above 16 characters, Big Shoulders Stencil Display above 14 — the LONG money lines ("iPHONE · iPAD · MACBOOK", "CARS, TRUCKS & VANS") trip both, and no look can suppress them. (3) Flat colour. The glow is stripped automatically from Oswald, Big Shoulders, Barlow Condensed, Teko, Saira Condensed and Russo One (line 1107) — which covers seven of the eight themes; Special Elite is not on that list, so Cosmic Cast is the one theme whose money word keeps the layout's soft halo, and it says so. "Square corners on every plate" is deleted: retheme_lab.mjs:1032 gives every single-line plate a seed-chosen shape from soft 16 / pill / round 44 / slant -12 / square 0, and a look cannot pin it. (4) THE FULL-BLEED BAND DOES NOT EXIST. ctaCard is a 760x194 rx-28 card at y838 carrying (562) 999-4994; phoneBar is a 660x118 rx-24 plate; bandKnockout's Knockout Band is inset 34px, rounded, and then shrunk by retheme_lab.mjs:1058 to hug the money word. No card in this collection carries an edge-to-edge band, and every claim of one has been struck. bandKnockout is dropped from the permitted set as well, because it renders neither an items line nor a sub block and so cannot meet rule (6). (5) The ground is always real product photography drawn by the engine: a tiled wall of single units (tile, 100% approval), a cast hero under the diagonal window shadow (cast, 50%), or the graded-slab window (slab). No theme takes a Commons photograph as its GROUND — look.ground is only honoured for cast and tile (line 2916), and every photo, scene, abstract and cash branch is gated behind !t2.__dg, so declaring cast or tile shuts them all out. The collection's single Commons photograph is the PSA Charizard inside Grail Slab's slab window. (6) At least two selling-point lines, from the deck's own sub and items copy: checklistHero's three ticks, stepsFlow's three step cards, trustSeal's items line, reviewProof's quote and rating, hudTech's items plus data line, voltStack's three-line sub block. (7) THE ROTATED STICKER IS FICTION — there is no CASH TODAY / PAID TODAY / SAME DAY / ON THE SPOT mechanism anywhere in app.js or retheme_lab.mjs, and every theme's variations named one. Deleted. The only tilted things a card can have are voltStack's kicker ribbon (angle -3) and the one or two decorative marks addElements drops into free corners at ±15deg. PERMITTED LAYOUTS, now six: reviewProof 93, stepsFlow 58, trustSeal 55, checklistHero 53, hudTech 36, voltStack 30. gradientWave, arcCrown, glassCard, scriptRetro, bubblePop, ticketStub and slabPoster stay banned as before; neonNight, bandKnockout and lowerThird join them (hollow stroked headlines; no small-print slot; a 44px-rounded shadowed band with a two-colour 94px headline pair). WHAT THE ENGINE DECIDES AND NO THEME CAN: retheme_lab.mjs:2800 rotates the phones templates across APPLE = iphone, iphone, iphone, ipad, ipad, macbook, and line 2802 rotates the cars templates across cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans. There is no look.line and no look.vehicle, so every phones theme here declares its iPad and MacBook stock and every vehicle theme declares its truck, van and bike stock, and says which money word each deck brings. Line 2739 filters look.categories against RING = phones, gold, cars, pokemon, coins, silver, sports, strips and FALLS BACK TO ALL EIGHT if the filter empties — which is why "macbook" and "trucks/vans/bikes" as categories were not merely wrong but catastrophic. WHAT A LOOK REALLY CONTROLS: mustShow and neverShow are read three times — at 2828 for the hero pool, at 2960 for the tile-wall pool, and at 2528 (lookFaults) where a violation re-seeds the card. Matching is literal startsWith on the cutout basename, so 'sports-slab' also matches 'sports-slabs-stack' and 'qs-cat-mac' also matches 'qs-cat-macbook'; entries containing a space are prose for people and match nothing; 'ground:tile' style tokens test the rendered ground; and a logo rule must be written 'logo:assets/logos/ford.png', because the layer's src is the inked key 'logo:assets/logos/ford.png:#ffffff' and the old 'logo:ford' form matched nothing. A must list only narrows the wall when four or more of its files survive, and a wall that cannot reach four cells falls to a cast, never to a stock photo. NONE OF THE SIX PERMITTED LAYOUTS CARRIES A PRODUCT CUTOUT LAYER: every product on every card in this collection is in the ground. TWO ENGINE WARTS THIS COLLECTION CANNOT FIX FROM A RECIPE, both flagged for the session that edits the repo: CATEGORY_COPY.bikes.items still ships "Ducati" (line 206), which the owner listed as too niche; and slabFrame's sports fallback alternates a real slab with an empty one (line 2382), which is why the sports slab theme was dropped rather than shipped. Assets: the approved pool is 344 cutouts after the legacy filter; the fifteen verified-bad files (own-apple-deep-blue-09/-14/-18, own-apple-silver-11/-15, own-apple-cosmic-orange-03/-10/-17/-19/-21, strip-kit-meter, own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle) appear nowhere in this collection, and own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 is the only own-apple file that is a bare single unit.

looks.name: Cosmic Cast
looks.oneLine: One Cosmic Orange iPhone drawn large into a warm brown ground with a soft diagonal window shadow falling across it, the money word typewritten into the lit left third.
looks.groundSpec: Engine cast ground, pale branch. pp02's c1 #fdf4ee is lum 0.918, over the 0.55 gate, so: fill #fdf4ee, ink #4a3220 at 0.20 for body, a vertical accent #ac5d05 0.18 to ink 0.10, then a white sheen 0.12 from the top-left. The hero is drawn at min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h), rotated -0.12rad, centred at 66%/52%, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset +24/+30, alpha 0.92. Two blurred diagonal shadow planes fall upper-right to lower-left at strength 0.58, and the whole thing takes a scrim of ink #4a3220 at 0.30 (c2 #e5ddd5 is light, so the scrim takes the ink, not c2). Result: a warm brown handbill with an orange phone glowing out of the shadow, the money word in the LIT left third, never over the phone. io04 is the identical build - c1 #feece2 lum 0.866, ink #4b3122, accent #c46008, c2 #ead5c4 light so the scrim is again the ink - a slightly peachier brown. PALE VS DEEP: both palettes are pale because the 0.20 ink wash is what gives the card body; a deep palette skips that wash and the shadow has nothing to fall on, so deep palettes are out. ONE HONEST EXCEPTION: Special Elite is not on the glow-strip list at retheme_lab.mjs:1107, so the layout's soft halo behind the money word survives on this theme and on no other. On odd seeds the LONG line iPHONE - iPAD - MACBOOK is 23 characters, over Special Elite's 16-character limit, so the face drops to Oswald, Big Shoulders Display or Barlow Condensed by seed and the halo goes with it.

looks.name: Lot Lattice
looks.oneLine: Four car bodies striped down a 4x3 lattice under a deep indigo wash, with WE BUY / CARS in tall condensed caps and the number on its plate at the foot.
looks.groundSpec: 4x3 / 28px lattice on a pool of exactly four bodies. The arithmetic is worth stating because it is the design: cell (r,c) draws pool[(4r+c+sd) mod 4], and 4r is 0 mod 4, so each COLUMN holds one body repeated down three rows - four bodies, four stripes, a deliberate lattice rather than a pile. On du08 (c1 #5593ef, lum 0.290, under the 0.55 gate) the lattice light falls to neutral #eceef2 and the wash is c1 #5593ef at 0.6, so the card reads as one blue with the cars showing through as pale silhouettes; near-white accent2 #eff1ff carries the small print and accent #3c3e65 takes the money plate with #fbfaf8 on it. On jw01 (c1 #1f3e7a, lum 0.051) the lattice is #eceef2 washed with #1f3e7a at 0.6 and support #53b9e0 takes the plate. Panels solid at 0.9 with white sub-labels. THE WALL RUNS ON THE CARS DECK ONLY. retheme_lab.mjs:2802 rotates the cars templates across cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans; the trucks, vans and bikes subject pools are keys, a title document, a wheel and one vehicle, so after this theme's neverShow removes the paperwork each of those pools holds a single file - below the four-cell minimum. Those cards fall to the engine's cast, hero car-truck-front, car-van-cargo or car-motorcycle-side on the same blue; because the theme declares tile they are re-seeded once first, so most of them come back as cars cards.
looks.imagery: Wall cells, all four opened and checked: car-front (a silver sedan with a three-pointed star on the grille), car-sedan-front (a silver Toyota Crown, crown badge on the grille, cropped at the frame edges), car-sedan-rear (a silver Audi A6 rear three-quarter, boot de-badged) and car-suv-side (a black electric SUV, side-rear). Three silver sedans and one black SUV, washed to 0.6 - they read as bodies, not as makes, which is why this is the generic bill and no wordmark ever appears on it. No keys, no fob, no title document, no engine bay, no wheel, no damaged front, no classic. Truck, van and bike cards take the cast instead: car-truck-front (a white Ram 1500, front and tailgate badges out of frame), car-van-cargo (a white Sprinter panel van, nose cropped) or car-motorcycle-side (a modern naked bike whose tank and side-panel badges are unreadable).

a wordmark of any make on this card - it is the generic bill and its sibling Make Mark owns the brand line

looks.name: Make Mark
looks.oneLine: A de-badged car, truck, van or bike cast large into deep indigo under the diagonal shadow, its make set as the money word with the brand's own inked wordmark locked into the free corner.
looks.groundSpec: Cast ground on a DEEP palette, so the pale branch does not run: jw01 fills c1 #1f3e7a (lum 0.051), takes a white sheen at 0.10 from the top-left, draws the hero at min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) rotated -0.12rad with shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset +24/+30 at alpha 0.92, lays two blurred diagonal planes at strength 0.5 and scrims with c1 at 0.22 - a night-lot indigo with the vehicle carved out of it. Type is ink #d7deec; the money word takes accent #fdc3a0 flat (the engine deletes the layout gradient) or knocks out to accent2 #ffeee4; support #53b9e0 carries the number plate. jw09 is the identical deep build - c1 #054666 lum 0.054, ink #d2e0ea, accent #fdc0b7, accent2 #ffedea, support #3ebfc9. THE WORDMARK: the Commons PNGs are black on transparent and inkedLogo re-inks them to pure #ffffff on these deep grounds (pure #14161c on a light one) - never th.ink, which printed a brown Toyota mark on the amber palettes. It is placed by addElements in the first free corner of [top-right, top-left, bottom-right, bottom-left] at 230/190/150px wide, clear of every measured box, before any decorative mark. IT ONLY EXISTS ON HALF THE CARDS: retheme_lab.mjs:1141 prints a make word only when seed % 2 === 1, and __brandWord is what triggers the mark. On even seeds the card is the category bill in this theme's type and colour - the mark goes with the word, never without it - and because the theme declares ground cast, that branch takes the cast too and no photograph can reach it on either branch.
looks.imagery: HERO AND MARK MUST NOT ARGUE, so this theme uses only bodies that wear no legible badge of their own - opened and checked one by one. Cars deck: car-sedan-rear (an Audi A6 rear three-quarter whose boot has been de-badged - no rings, no wordmark) and car-suv-side (a black electric SUV, side-rear, tailgate text illegible at card size). Trucks: car-truck-front (a white Ram 1500 whose grille and tailgate are both out of frame). Vans: car-van-cargo (a white Sprinter, nose cropped). Bikes: car-motorcycle-side (a modern naked bike whose tank roundel and side-panel badge are smudged past reading). BARRED FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON: car-front carries a three-pointed star on its grille and car-sedan-front a Toyota crown - a Ford wordmark over either is the failure this theme exists to avoid. THE HONEST MARKS: logo:toyota, honda, ford, chevrolet, nissan, jeep, tesla, bmw, mercedes-benz, hyundai, kia and dodge over the two de-badged cars bodies; ram-trucks over car-truck-front; mercedes-benz over car-van-cargo. All sixteen wordmark files exist in assets/logos.
neverShow: car-front and car-sedan-front are barred because their own badge - a three-pointed star, a Toyota crown - argues with any other make word set beside it
HARLEYS as the money word: LONG.bikes offers it and BRAND_LOGO maps it to the Harley-Davidson mark, but car-motorcycle-side is a Japanese-style naked bike, not a cruiser

TRANSITS over car-van-cargo, which is a Sprinter: on the vans deck only SPRINTERS is honest

looks.copy: Trade voice, the make doing the shouting - on the half of the cards where a make prints. Headline WE BUY / TOYOTAS, and the items line follows the make: TOYOTAS reads Camry - Corolla - Tacoma - RAV4 - 4Runner. assets/bg-web/pokemon- as a full-bleed ground - the photograph lives in the window, never as the theme's identity

COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28 on 1080x1080 gives cells of 235 x 322.7, and each cell fits at k = min((235-24)/w, (322.7-24)/h) * 0.96. Every file on this shelf is width-limited, so every cell prints 203px wide and the heights are what vary: car-suv-side 203x83, car-sedan-rear 203x88, car-keys 203x145, car-title-docs 203x148, car-truck-front 203x173, car-van-cargo 203x180, car-wheel-tyre 203x225. The cars deck fills the wall with six of those (no truck, van or bike is on the cars shelf); the trucks deck fills it with four — the Ram, the transfer stack, the keys and the wheel. `light` resolves to the palette's own c1 on all three palettes (ck03 lum 0.929, ck09 0.931, pp06 0.920 — all clear the 0.55 test), so the board is a near-white the theme owns rather than the hard-coded #eceef2 a deep palette falls back to. Scrim: c1 and c2 are both pale, so `dark` is th.ink and the wash lands at 0.6. Over that wash the engine's panel pass (2997-3009) fills every stat tile at rgba(ink,0.9) with white copy, which is the only reason 4.9 / 200+ LOCAL REVIEWS stays legible on a lattice. WHY EVEN THIS THEME REFUSES car-sedan-front: at 203px its Toyota Crown emblem would measure 9px and be safe, but line 3483 strips the Hero Product layer only on a CAST ground, so on a lattice the hero also stands on top at the template's own scale — where that emblem is legible again.
