FORECOURT is the lot's own paint and paperwork: the shelf wall, the bay, the bright yard, the wreck, the lot after dark, the record, the transfer desk and the slip. Eight themes, every one categories:['cars'].

WHAT I RE-VERIFIED BEFORE REWRITING, all by opening the files. (a) categories IS live. retheme_lab.mjs:2740-2744 filters look.categories against RING0 = phones, gold, cars, pokemon, coins, silver, sports, strips and walks only what survives, so ['cars'] pins every card; the audit's C1 was true of an older build. That same filter is why 'trucks', 'vans' and 'bikes' may never appear in a categories array — they are not in RING0, the filter empties, and the walk is released to all eight subjects. Every record here says ['cars'] and names its deck in the copy instead. LAB_LOOKS=1 is still required to build the plan from these looks at all; LAB_CATS=cars is now belt-and-braces rather than the load-bearing flag the audit made it. (b) mustShow and neverShow are ENFORCED, not decorative: the hero filter at 2822-2834 and the lattice filter at 2960-2967 read them as literal startsWith on cutout names, and lookFaults (2529-2551) audits the finished card. That is the mechanism the audit asked for as a new `cuts` field — it already exists, so no theme here needs one. Rules that work: a bare cutout prefix (car-truck-front), ground:tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|slab|flat, logo:assets/logos/<file>.png, and an assets/... path prefix for the background. Rules that do nothing: anything containing a space (skipped as prose, by design) and — the trap every old record fell into — logo:toyota, because the placed layer's src is the inkedLogo cache key 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c' and the matcher compares with startsWith. Every logo rule in this collection is now in full-path form. One more trap, tested: an over-broad neverShow that empties the pool does not fail loudly, it silently returns the unfiltered deck pool (2834), so I simulated all eight themes against all four decks and confirmed none of them falls through.

THE ONE OPEN ENGINE DEPENDENCY, unchanged from audit C5. On seed%2===1 the money headline is replaced by LONG[lineKey] (1149-1151): TOYOTAS HONDAS FORDS CHEVYS NISSANS JEEPS TESLAS BMWS MERCEDES HYUNDAIS KIAS DODGES on the cars deck, F-150S SILVERADOS TACOMAS RAMS on trucks, HARLEYS HONDAS YAMAHAS KAWASAKIS on bikes, TRANSITS SPRINTERS on vans — and each also sets deck.__brandWord, which places that make's inked wordmark in a free corner (2579-2593). No look-level guard exists, so on one card in two this collection names a make. The fix is one clause: `c.text = (!deck.challengePromise && longs && seed % 2 === 1 && !(look && look.noBrandWord)) ? longs[seed % longs.length] : deck.h2;`. Until it lands, the law this collection is built on is NOT 'name only a make you can show' — that is unreachable — it is SHOW NO BADGE THAT CAN CONTRADICT THE WORD. No card here may carry a legible maker's mark in its imagery. That single rule bans, collection-wide: car-front (a genuine three-pointed star on a mid-2000s Japanese saloon body, 631x347 — a badge-swapped composite of the same class as the AI fakes the asset pass rejected), car-keys-fob (the fob medallion carries a fabricated overlapping-oval emblem, the strip-kit-meter fault), car-sedan-front (a Toyota Crown; the crown emblem measures 29px cast at 670px, and a lattice cannot rescue it because line 3483 strips the hero only on a cast ground), car-classic-side (a middle slice of a 1930s coupe with both ends cropped away, and LONG.cars has no CLASSICS) and car-engine-bay (a bare engine assembly on white — a parts ad). What is left, and what the eight themes are built from, is eleven files, of which the two badge-free whole bodies carry the vehicle themes: car-sedan-rear (boot lid and bumper retouched bare — no mark anywhere in frame) and car-suv-side (one 8px smudge of tailgate lettering).

THE VEHICLE DECK CANNOT BE PINNED EITHER (audit C2, confirmed): line 2802-2807 gives a cars card CATEGORY_COPY[VEHICLES[sd%5]] with VEHICLES = cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans, so every theme gets the cars copy on two cards in five and the bike, truck and van copy on one each, with the deck's own headline, items, money line and sub block. No theme here claims a deck; each one's mustShow carries the deck's own hero (car-truck-front, car-van-cargo, car-motorcycle-side) so the picture always answers the word that arrived, and each one's copy is written to be true under all four. That is also why no theme prints a money figure: the bounded string rotates ($15,000 cars, $25,000 trucks, $20,000 vans, $12,000 bikes) and a fixed number would be wrong on three cards in five.

FOUR RULES. 1. IMAGERY IS THE LOT'S OWN THINGS: the eleven approved car cutouts, nothing else — no cash, no hands, no clipboards, no storefronts, no Apple scenes, no photographs at all. Every vehicle photograph in assets/bg-web is European with a legible plate, photo scored 28%, and a brand-led card cannot carry one anyway (3070 is guarded by !brandLed), so this collection uses none. 2. TYPE IS THE LOT'S VOICE: the display comes from the top four styles of FIT.cars (line 430 reads condensed, bold, typewriter, stencil, slab, tech, street, vintage — so condensed leads and stencil is fourth, not first, and the old claim that stencil and condensed were 'the two best face styles in the data' was wrong: grotesque 56, typewriter 50 and tech 50 all beat condensed 49). Support is always a grotesque; numerals are condensed, mono or tech. No slab display anywhere, no script, no handwriting, no costume face. 3. COLOUR IS LOT PAINT: every c1 is in the blue, teal or indigo band and every accent is amber, apricot, peach or teal. No magenta, orchid, violet or rose accent — that removes cd06 #ab117d, jw05 #febbd3, lp03 #055e17 with its #e553a3 support, and lp09's #f24f6a — and no brown or dark-orange palette, which removes ck06 and pp02, both named 'Gold' with brown inks, the register theme_specs.mjs:14 records the owner ruling out. du07 (20%) and pp02 (21%) are out on the measured numbers as well. 4. ONE SHARED MARK, honestly scoped: the LOT LINE, a pair of painted stall lines at 18-22 degrees in ink or accent running off one edge, on the five drawn-ground themes. The two paper cards cannot carry it — paper() draws a fixed vertical margin at x=118 and nothing else (608-618) — so the ruled sheet is their family mark, and this rule says so rather than claiming a mark two of the eight lack.

GROUNDS, and one reporting bug. tile (100% approval), cast (50%) and the drawn deep branch (3029-3047, new and unmeasured) all render correctly; paper works only through the Lined Paper familyGround (2657-2709), which is why both paper themes are lp-only and a Chalk substitution is banned in their neverShow. Because tile, cast and deep all set __dg and overwrite t2.bg, the uncontrolled abstract (sd%12===7) and cash (sd%11===5) grounds cannot survive on any theme here, and ground:abs / ground:cash are in every neverShow so lookFaults would report it if that changed. slabFrame returns early unless the category is pokemon or sports (its own first line), so the slab frame cannot reach a cars card at all. THE BUG, verified: lookFaults' groundNow (2535) knows slab, tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo and flat but not deep or paper, while the run reporter at 3700 does know 'deep' — so the three deep and paper themes render right and are then reported 'ground flat but the theme is deep/paper'. One-line fix at 2535: `t2.__deepBg ? 'deep' : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper' :` before the flat fallback.

NOT A REPEAT OF ITS NEIGHBOURS, checked against all 100 looks: street-poster-lot-lattice already owns the four-body lattice in deep indigo (this one is the pale board and the whole shelf, keys and paperwork included), window-light-forecourt and street-poster-make-mark own the deep cast vehicle in a room and with a marque (this collection's casts are the painted bay, the bright yard with the hazard band and the wreck, and wear no marque), street-poster-yard-night and proof-wall-title-and-keys own the vehicle photograph, and written-quote-red-pen-tow-sheet owns the vehicle-and-keys red-pen sheet and explicitly bans car-title-docs — which is exactly what Title Desk is built on, in navy, with no vehicle. Forecourt is also the only cars work in the library on the deep ground.

Every card carries (562) 999-4994, iphones.LA and LONG BEACH · LAKEWOOD · DOWNEY · CARSON · TORRANCE; every star row is ★★★★★ with 4.9 and 200+ LOCAL REVIEWS; every claim is one of the engine's own bounded strings; one sentence sits in one face; no product sits over text; and no relic can reach a card, because the deck pool is car-* and the subject never-list bans every iPhone, iPad, Mac and Watch prefix — including the fifteen files the asset pass has now rejected.

looks.oneLine: Whichever working vehicle the deck brought — pickup, van, bike or saloon — cast large into painted blue metal with the diagonal bay shadow across it and the money word stencilled into the left third.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='cast', non-pale branch (retheme_lab.mjs:2930-2946), because du08 c1 #5593ef sits at lum 0.290 and du06 #20a99e at 0.312, both under the 0.55 pale test. Measured sizes at that k: car-truck-front 670x573, car-van-cargo 670x594, car-motorcycle-side 670x706, car-sedan-rear 670x290, car-suv-side 670x273. THE CAST BLEEDS NOTHING — the image spans x 378 to 1048 on a 1080 canvas and touches no edge, so no mustShow line here asks for a bleed; the Ram's two crops and the Sprinter's two crops sit inside the frame as cuts and the type stack, which owns the left 46%, covers the left one. The product is the ground: line 3483 strips the Hero Product layer on a cast card, so nothing stands on top of it and no product sits over text. Lot line: two 12px stall lines in ink (du08 #1b293f, du06 #0c3531) at 26% running off the bottom-left corner at 18 degrees, plus a stencilled bay number in the display face at 8% behind the money word. This theme stays in the mid-tone metal band on purpose: window-light-forecourt already owns the du08+ca01 cast vehicle in a room with a blind, and street-poster-make-mark owns the deep-indigo cast vehicle with the brand mark; this one is the painted bay with the stall lines and the trade voice, and it never wears a marque of its own.
looks.imagery: One vehicle, cast, whichever deck the card is running: car-truck-front (a white Ram 1500 Quad Cab, front three-quarter, cut by the file at the bed and the nose — a recognisable Ram, so nothing on the card may claim another truck), car-van-cargo (a white high-roof first-generation Sprinter body, left flank, cut at both ends — a recognisable Sprinter, same rule), car-motorcycle-side (a modern naked roadster, no legible badge — a machine that is nobody's flagship), car-sedan-rear (a silver saloon from the rear three-quarter with the badge retouched off the boot lid: no grille, no mark, nothing to contradict a headline) and car-suv-side (a dark modern SUV, rear three-quarter, one 8px smudge of tailgate lettering at cast scale). looks.oneLine: The same cast on the bright side of the lot: one working vehicle in a pale blue yard with an amber hazard band running off the bottom corner, talking to a business rather than a driver.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='cast', PALE branch (retheme_lab.mjs:2933-2940) — a different render from Work Bay, not a recolour. Lot line becomes fleet livery here: a 46px band at 22 degrees in the accent at 100% with 18px ink chevrons, running off the bottom edge only, never behind the type. The product is the ground (line 3483 strips the Hero Product layer on a cast card), so nothing sits over the type.
looks.imagery: One vehicle, cast, whichever deck the card is running — car-van-cargo (a white high-roof first-generation Sprinter body, left flank with the windscreen and front wheel at the right, cut by the file at both the rear doors and the nose; a recognisable Sprinter, so SPRINTERS is the only van word it can answer and TRANSITS is not), car-truck-front (a white Ram 1500 Quad Cab, cut at bed and nose), car-motorcycle-side (a modern naked roadster, no legible badge), car-sedan-rear (a silver saloon, rear three-quarter, badge retouched away) and car-suv-side (a dark modern SUV, whole). a second vehicle in the frame
a palette whose accent is not warm — the hazard band is the theme's only mark and it cannot be drawn in a teal on a teal-white ground

looks.name: Salvage Bay
looks.oneLine: The wrecked saloon cast whole into teal paint with the destroyed end at the right and the condition line stencilled opposite it — the card that says a bad car is still worth money.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='cast'. On du06 (c1 #20a99e, lum 0.312) the non-pale branch runs — fill c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at k = min(669.6/1661, 993.6/1017) = 0.4031 for 670x410 at (712.8, 561.6) rotated -0.12 rad with shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset 24/30, then the window shadow at 0.5, then scrim c1 at 0.22. On ca09 (lum 0.829) the pale branch runs instead — ink 20%, accent-to-ink gradient, sheen 0.12, window shadow 0.58, scrim ink 0.30. THE ORIENTATION IS NOT SETTABLE and the record no longer pretends otherwise: the cast branch draws unmirrored at a fixed -0.12 rad, and in this file the car's nose points right with the damage on its right side, so the wreckage lands at the right of the card and the type stack owns the left 46%. The eye reaches the money word first because the type is on the reading side, not because the car was turned. THE SCALE IS NOT SETTABLE EITHER: the cast branch is hard-coded to W*0.62, so the wreck prints 670px wide, 0.62 of the card, not the 0.42 the audit asked for. If the owner wants it smaller the change is one clause — a look.castScale read at 2941 — and until then the mitigation is the crop, which is already wide: the whole car is in frame, at a distance, on white, so it reads as a car we will still buy rather than as a repair job. Lot line: two stall lines in ink at 26% off the bottom-left corner at 18 degrees; no chevrons, because du06's accent #08515a is a dark teal that cannot carry a hazard mark on its own ground.
looks.imagery: car-damaged-front on the cars deck and nothing else: a dark grey saloon with the entire front end destroyed — bonnet buckled back, bumper and grille torn away, radiator core exposed, one headlight gone — shot whole on white, 1661x1017. One wrecked car, at a distance, never a close crop on the damage and never two of them. On the truck, van and bike decks the hero is that deck's own clean vehicle (car-truck-front, car-van-cargo, car-motorcycle-side), because a wrecked saloon under WE BUY TRUCKS is the wrong vehicle and the condition line is true either way. This is the only theme in the collection permitted to show damage, and the single heaviest damage asset in the library: the owner's standing note on damage-heavy assets is that it reads as a repair ad, so the wide crop and the ANY CONDITION kicker are what separate a buyer's card from a body shop's.
mustShow: a bounded condition line from the deck's own items: Title In Hand, Running Or Not, High Miles, Salvage, Lien Payoff or Free Tow
five stars as ★★★★★ with 4.9 and 200+ LOCAL REVIEWS
neverShow: car-damaged-front on any other theme in this collection
more than one damaged vehicle — a pile of wrecks is a scrapyard, the same failure as the owner's damage-heavy phone rejects
a close crop on the damage itself
a make named over the wreck — naming one implicates that make, and this is the theme where the engine's LONG rotation does the most harm until the noBrandWord guard exists
looks.copy: Blunt and reassuring at once: the car is bad, the offer is real, the tow is free. Headline is the deck's own WE BUY CARS with the kicker ANY CONDITION; money line is the deck's own bounded UP TO $15,000 CASH (and the deck's own figure on the spin-offs), never a number this theme invents. Two selling points from the cars sub block: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE TOW and TITLE, DMV AND LIEN PAYOFF HANDLED. One sentence in one face. Items: Title In Hand • Running Or Not • High Miles • Salvage • Lien Payoff • Free Tow. CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER.
variations: Wide Wreck — du06, checklistHero, the four conditions we still buy listed against the cast
Light Bay — ca09, stepsFlow, the pale branch so the honest card reads friendly
Wreck Proof — du06, reviewProof, the review block on a solid ink plate to the left of the car
fixesApplied: Audit: 'THE DAMAGE IS TOTAL, NOT A CORNER — the theme's own description understates what the owner will see.' Imagery rewritten to what I opened: the whole front end destroyed, radiator exposed, one headlight gone.

Audit: 'THE ORIENTATION IS UNACHIEVABLE — the cast branch draws unmirrored at a fixed rotation.' The orientation sentence is deleted and replaced with what the engine actually does and why the composition still works.

Audit: 'change the cast scale to a capped 0.28 and say the cast branch needs a look.castScale override.' Applied honestly: the record now states the scale is hard-coded at W*0.62 = 670px, names the one-clause override, and does not print a number the engine will not honour.
Audit: 'du07 measured 20% and it leads this theme.' Dropped; du06 leads and ca09 is the pale alternative, which also stops this theme sharing a lead palette with Work Bay.
Audit: 'drop hudTech, the 36% layout, from a theme that carries enough risk.' Dropped; layouts are checklistHero, stepsFlow and reviewProof.

Audit C4: 'nothing selects car-damaged-front out of the cars deck's twelve candidates.' Solved by the existing hero filter — this theme's neverShow removes every other cars-deck cutout, so the wreck is the only candidate left on a cars card, and the three spin-off decks keep their own vehicle.

Audit C5: the logo rules are now written in the form the matcher actually reads — logo:assets/logos/<file>.png, matching the inkedLogo cache key — so the ban on a make over the wreck is enforced by lookFaults instead of being inert text.

(b) mustShow and neverShow are ENFORCED, not decorative: the hero filter at 2822-2834 and the lattice filter at 2960-2967 read them as literal startsWith on cutout names, and lookFaults (2529-2551) audits the finished card. That is the mechanism the audit asked for as a new `cuts` field — it already exists, so no theme here needs one. Rules that work: a bare cutout prefix (car-truck-front), ground:tile|cast|abs|cash|scene|photo|slab|flat, logo:assets/logos/<file>.png, and an assets/... path prefix for the background. Rules that do nothing: anything containing a space (skipped as prose, by design) and — the trap every old record fell into — logo:toyota, because the placed layer's src is the inkedLogo cache key 'logo:assets/logos/toyota.png:#14161c' and the matcher compares with startsWith. Every logo rule in this collection is now in full-path form. One more trap, tested: an over-broad neverShow that empties the pool does not fail loudly, it silently returns the unfiltered deck pool (2834), so I simulated all eight themes against all four decks and confirmed none of them falls through.

THE ONE OPEN ENGINE DEPENDENCY, unchanged from audit C5. On seed%2===1 the money headline is replaced by LONG[lineKey] (1149-1151): TOYOTAS HONDAS FORDS CHEVYS NISSANS JEEPS TESLAS BMWS MERCEDES HYUNDAIS KIAS DODGES on the cars deck, F-150S SILVERADOS TACOMAS RAMS on trucks, HARLEYS HONDAS YAMAHAS KAWASAKIS on bikes, TRANSITS SPRINTERS on vans — and each also sets deck.__brandWord, which places that make's inked wordmark in a free corner (2579-2593). No look-level guard exists, so on one card in two this collection names a make. The fix is one clause: `c.text = (!deck.challengePromise && longs && seed % 2 === 1 && !(look && look.noBrandWord)) ? longs[seed % longs.length] : deck.h2;`. Until it lands, the law this collection is built on is NOT 'name only a make you can show' — that is unreachable — it is SHOW NO BADGE THAT CAN CONTRADICT THE WORD. No card here may carry a legible maker's mark in its imagery. That single rule bans, collection-wide: car-front (a genuine three-pointed star on a mid-2000s Japanese saloon body, 631x347 — a badge-swapped composite of the same class as the AI fakes the asset pass rejected), car-keys-fob (the fob medallion carries a fabricated overlapping-oval emblem, the strip-kit-meter fault), car-sedan-front (a Toyota Crown; the crown emblem measures 29px cast at 670px, and a lattice cannot rescue it because line 3483 strips the hero only on a cast ground), car-classic-side (a middle slice of a 1930s coupe with both ends cropped away, and LONG.cars has no CLASSICS) and car-engine-bay (a bare engine assembly on white — a parts ad). What is left, and what the eight themes are built from, is eleven files, of which the two badge-free whole bodies carry the vehicle themes: car-sedan-rear (boot lid and bumper retouched bare — no mark anywhere in frame) and car-suv-side (one 8px smudge of tailgate lettering).

THE VEHICLE DECK CANNOT BE PINNED EITHER (audit C2, confirmed): line 2802-2807 gives a cars card CATEGORY_COPY[VEHICLES[sd%5]] with VEHICLES = cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans, so every theme gets the cars copy on two cards in five and the bike, truck and van copy on one each, with the deck's own headline, items, money line and sub block. No theme here claims a deck; each one's mustShow carries the deck's own hero (car-truck-front, car-van-cargo, car-motorcycle-side) so the picture always answers the word that arrived, and each one's copy is written to be true under all four. That is also why no theme prints a money figure: the bounded string rotates ($15,000 cars, $25,000 trucks, $20,000 vans, $12,000 bikes) and a fixed number would be wrong on three cards in five.

FOUR RULES. 1. IMAGERY IS THE LOT'S OWN THINGS: the eleven approved car cutouts, nothing else — no cash, no hands, no clipboards, no storefronts, no Apple scenes, no photographs at all. Every vehicle photograph in assets/bg-web is European with a legible plate, photo scored 28%, and a brand-led card cannot carry one anyway (3070 is guarded by !brandLed), so this collection uses none. 2. TYPE IS THE LOT'S VOICE: the display comes from the top four styles of FIT.cars (line 430 reads condensed, bold, typewriter, stencil, slab, tech, street, vintage — so condensed leads and stencil is fourth, not first, and the old claim that stencil and condensed were 'the two best face styles in the data' was wrong: grotesque 56, typewriter 50 and tech 50 all beat condensed 49). Support is always a grotesque; numerals are condensed, mono or tech. No slab display anywhere, no script, no handwriting, no costume face. 3. COLOUR IS LOT PAINT: every c1 is in the blue, teal or indigo band and every accent is amber, apricot, peach or teal. No magenta, orchid, violet or rose accent — that removes cd06 #ab117d, jw05 #febbd3, lp03 #055e17 with its #e553a3 support, and lp09's #f24f6a — and no brown or dark-orange palette, which removes ck06 and pp02, both named 'Gold' with brown inks, the register theme_specs.mjs:14 records the owner ruling out. du07 (20%) and pp02 (21%) are out on the measured numbers as well. 4. ONE SHARED MARK, honestly scoped: the LOT LINE, a pair of painted stall lines at 18-22 degrees in ink or accent running off one edge, on the five drawn-ground themes. The two paper cards cannot carry it — paper() draws a fixed vertical margin at x=118 and nothing else (608-618) — so the ruled sheet is their family mark, and this rule says so rather than claiming a mark two of the eight lack.

GROUNDS, and one reporting bug. tile (100% approval), cast (50%) and the drawn deep branch (3029-3047, new and unmeasured) all render correctly; paper works only through the Lined Paper familyGround (2657-2709), which is why both paper themes are lp-only and a Chalk substitution is banned in their neverShow. Because tile, cast and deep all set __dg and overwrite t2.bg, the uncontrolled abstract (sd%12===7) and cash (sd%11===5) grounds cannot survive on any theme here, and ground:abs / ground:cash are in every neverShow so lookFaults would report it if that changed. slabFrame returns early unless the category is pokemon or sports (its own first line), so the slab frame cannot reach a cars card at all. THE BUG, verified: lookFaults' groundNow (2535) knows slab, tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo and flat but not deep or paper, while the run reporter at 3700 does know 'deep' — so the three deep and paper themes render right and are then reported 'ground flat but the theme is deep/paper'. One-line fix at 2535: `t2.__deepBg ? 'deep' : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper' :` before the flat fallback.

NOT A REPEAT OF ITS NEIGHBOURS, checked against all 100 looks: street-poster-lot-lattice already owns the four-body lattice in deep indigo (this one is the pale board and the whole shelf, keys and paperwork included), window-light-forecourt and street-poster-make-mark own the deep cast vehicle in a room and with a marque (this collection's casts are the painted bay, the bright yard with the hazard band and the wreck, and wear no marque), street-poster-yard-night and proof-wall-title-and-keys own the vehicle photograph, and written-quote-red-pen-tow-sheet owns the vehicle-and-keys red-pen sheet and explicitly bans car-title-docs — which is exactly what Title Desk is built on, in navy, with no vehicle. Forecourt is also the only cars work in the library on the deep ground.

Every card carries (562) 999-4994, iphones.LA and LONG BEACH · LAKEWOOD · DOWNEY · CARSON · TORRANCE; every star row is ★★★★★ with 4.9 and 200+ LOCAL REVIEWS; every claim is one of the engine's own bounded strings; one sentence sits in one face; no product sits over text; and no relic can reach a card, because the deck pool is car-* and the subject never-list bans every iPhone, iPad, Mac and Watch prefix — including the fifteen files the asset pass has now rejected.

looks.name: Vault Wall II
looks.oneLine: The gold shelf laid out flat in a twelve-cell lattice on a pale vitrine, dropped sixty percent into aubergine, with CASH FOR / GOLD in stencil and the money band as the only accent on the card.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' (retheme_lab.mjs:2886, the lookGround branch wins before every rotation), so this theme is on its ground on every seed. W=H=1080, COLS=4, ROWS=3, gap=28: cells are 235 x 322.67, and each cutout is fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box and then scaled 0.96, so it occupies at most 202 x 287 of its cell -- about 86 per cent, not 0.96 of the cell. Shadows are rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offset 10/16. `light` = lum(c1)>0.55 ? c1 : lum(c2)>0.55 ? c2 : '#eceef2'; nn10 c1 #2c1c37 (L 0.016) and c2 #1e0925 (L 0.006) are both deep, so the lattice always lands on the hard-coded #eceef2 and takes scrimColor = c1 at 0.6 (lum(dark) < 0.4). A pale vitrine dimmed 60 per cent: bright metal survives it, which is why gold gets a wall. The panel pass (2963) then fills every stat tile with rgba(#2c1c37,0.9) and sets its copy #ffffff, so no small type sits on the lattice. Colour chain, all engine: the money band takes th.accent (1047, locked); the phone plate takes th.support because the accent is already spent (1573); the kicker plate and the double hairline frame take SIG.gold.tone2 = support (1596, 1604). On nn10 that is #f5ba08 over #b68b1b; on jw02 #fec674 over #c39550 -- every plate on the card is a gold, on a violet ground. TYPE WARNING, measured: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed. CASH FOR (8) and GOLD (4) are safe; PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE (24) is not, so on layouts that set the price line in the display face it prints in the substitute -- accept it, or let the money word 95% carry the band.
looks.imagery: The wall is built by the engine, not chosen: cand = the gold deck prefixes plus the gold subject shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Simulated against the current approved list that is exactly twelve objects for twelve cells, no repeat: gold-bar-single, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-jewelry, gold-necklace-single. gold-bars-fan, gold-bars-row and gold-bracelet-pair are MULTI-dropped; gold-pocket-watch, gold-rings-scatter, gold-scale-weighing, gold-scrap-mixed, gold-teeth-dental and gold-watch-luxury fall past the slice. Two cells are low-res originals -- gold-bars 461x326 and gold-jewelry 511x226 -- both drawn down to at most 202px wide, so they are soft-safe but shallow; gold-jewelry is a wide, short pile and leaves its cell looking empty top and bottom. ONE PRODUCT SITS OVER THE WALL: the placement search (3169) pushes a 'Hero Product' cutout on any card that has none, and none of this theme's four layouts authors one. It is drawn from the gold deck pool (all 21 approved gold- cutouts) and evicted if it overlaps any text box (3160). mustShow/neverShow govern that one layer -- they cannot see the wall cells, which are painted into the ground canvas. Marks: addElements places one or two, corners and the money word's flanks; ELEMENTS.gold colours are the fixed golds #f2c14e / #c9950f / #fff1b8, and two marks in five are iOS emoji from the gold list (money bag, gem, ring, watch, coin) -- the look cannot switch emoji off, so the watch glyph is the one to discard by eye.
looks.copy: The pawnbroker with the shutter down, counting stock. Flat, exact, no adjectives. Headline: CASH FOR / GOLD -- two lines, one sentence, Big Shoulders Stencil Display in ink on both, never a colour change on line two. Selling points (the deck's own, at least two print by the minimum-information pass at 3559): TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU plus WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. Money band: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, money word 95% -- a number a seller can check, which is the whole point of not saying top prices. ITEMS LINE, THE ONE ENGINE EDIT THIS THEME NEEDS: CATEGORY_COPY.gold.items still ships '10k - 14k - 18k - Scrap & Dental - Cuban Links - Rolex - Cartier - Tiffany - Yurman'; no approved cutout can back Rolex, Cartier, Tiffany or Yurman, and neither Scrap nor Dental reaches this wall. It should read '10k - 14k - 18k - Cuban Links - Chains - Class Rings - Earrings - Mixed Lots', where every noun has a cell. Kicker: GOLD BUYER (KICKERS.gold[0]; the rotation is seeded, TOP BUYER / FAST CASH / TOP RATED / WE PAY MORE are the other draws and none repeats a word on the card). Sticker: ON THE SPOT. Rating is 4.9 with five stars wherever stars appear. Badges render LICENSED / DISCREET / PRIVATE -- the engine already swaps INSURED to DISCREET off the cars deck (1385), so no rule is needed for it. Two of three seeds also draw the gold signature frame: a double hairline in the support gold at inset 22/34.

looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: eight cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else. Ten were written; two are gone and the reasons are in droppedThemes.

FIVE LOCKS, ALL MEASURED IN THE REPO
1. GROUND VALUE. Seven palettes, every c1 under L 0.06: nn10 #2c1c37 0.016, nn02 #241f3b 0.017, jw02 #3e3577 0.049, jw01 #1f3e7a 0.051, jw09 #054666 0.054, jw05 #044a51 0.055, jw07 #054e2f 0.057. Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. But the card does not stop there: because the accent is spent, the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT (1573), and the kicker plate and the category's signature frame take SIG[cat].tone2 (1596, 1604). A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Phones take jw09 and jw01. Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. The old 'two lit plates is the fault' rule was describing something the engine does on purpose; this is the version that holds.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Cuban Cast II
looks.oneLine: One piece of worn gold drawn huge into the ground under a single diagonal window shadow, the money word across the lit left third.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='cast' forces dg='cast' on every seed (2886). Ground fills jw02 c1 #3e3577 (L 0.049), then a white 0.10 -> 0 linear from the top-left corner. The hero is fitted k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) = min(669.6/w, 993.6/h), translated to (712.8, 561.6), rotated -0.12 rad, drawn at alpha 0.92 with shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.35), blur 40, offset 24/30. Then the window shadow: a 26px-blurred rgba(8,10,16,0.5) wedge from 0.62W to the right edge plus a 60px-blurred penumbra at 0.25 from 0.5W, so the light is upper-left and the shadow falls across the hero's right two-thirds. Finally scrimColor = c1 at 0.22. lum(c1) is far under 0.55, so the pale branch (ink body, 0.58 shadow, 0.30 scrim) cannot fire; if a pale palette is ever substituted the theme is invalid. Panels over the cast go solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with white copy (2963). Colour chain: money band = accent (jw02 #fec674, nn02 #feb263), phone plate = support (#c39550 / #cd7c0e), kicker plate and the double frame = support again -- every plate a gold on a violet ground. THE RULE THIS GROUND BREAKS: at 3428 the engine deletes every 'Hero Product' and 'Lineup Product' layer on a cast card -- the product IS the ground -- so this card carries no cutout layer at all, and lookFaults (2536) therefore checks mustShow against nothing and neverShow against nothing. On this theme the two lists are documentation, not a gate; the only real guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645). There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc, so the hero is a uniform seeded draw, use[(sd*7+3) % 21], over the whole approved gold shelf: nine of the twenty-one are admissible here, about two cards in five, and the rest are discarded on the contact sheet.
looks.imagery: Admissible heroes, all verified by opening the file: gold-bracelet-cuban (1484x1184, a real Cuban link bracelet, the lead), gold-necklace-single (1314x1591, a heavy rope chain), gold-chains-pile (2048x1718), gold-chains (624x457), gold-class-ring (846x1232, a gold ring with a coloured stone), gold-bracelet-pair (1294x1041), gold-rings-scatter (2048x2048), gold-earrings-pile (1054x838), gold-jewelry-mixed (2048x1734). Every one of them downscales into the 669 x 993 cast box. Discard the other twelve draws: both watches (gold-watch-luxury, gold-pocket-watch -- this collection has no watch card and a watch hero is a watch card), gold-teeth-dental, gold-scale-weighing (that is Under One Lamp's subject and a near-white body), gold-coins-pile and gold-scrap-mixed (the loose-gold themes' subjects), and the four bar assets plus gold-jewelry (511x226, which the cast fit would upscale 1.3x). gold-jewelry cannot be barred by prefix without also barring gold-jewelry-mixed, so it is a discard rule, not a neverShow entry. No second product: the cast ground is the picture. Marks: one or two, corners and the money-word flanks at 118px, from ELEMENTS.gold in its fixed golds; two in five are iOS emoji and the watch glyph is discarded.
looks.copy: The written-offer voice: we test it, you watch, you decide. Headline: CASH OUT YOUR / GOLD -- one face, one colour, both lines. Selling points: WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE plus TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU. Money band: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE, money word 95%. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Items line, matched to what this card can show: '10k - 14k - 18k - Cuban Links - Rope Chains - Bracelets - Class Rings - Necklaces'. Kicker: GOLD BUYER. Badges render LICENSED / DISCREET / PRIVATE. Challenge cut on one seed in three names household targets only -- WE BEAT / CASH4GOLD, WE TOP / THE PAWN SHOP, WE OUTBID / EZPAWN; the WE MATCH draw prints as WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object (2841) and is discarded, because the standing rule is that WE MATCH always takes an object. Copy sits on the LIT left third; nothing sits over the bracelet, and the engine enforces it -- a cutout overlapping any text box is evicted at 3160.

looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: eight cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else. Ten were written; two are gone and the reasons are in droppedThemes.

FIVE LOCKS, ALL MEASURED IN THE REPO
1. GROUND VALUE. Seven palettes, every c1 under L 0.06: nn10 #2c1c37 0.016, nn02 #241f3b 0.017, jw02 #3e3577 0.049, jw01 #1f3e7a 0.051, jw09 #054666 0.054, jw05 #044a51 0.055, jw07 #054e2f 0.057. Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. But the card does not stop there: because the accent is spent, the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT (1573), and the kicker plate and the category's signature frame take SIG[cat].tone2 (1596, 1604). A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Phones take jw09 and jw01. Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. The old 'two lit plates is the fault' rule was describing something the engine does on purpose; this is the version that holds.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Under One Lamp II
looks.oneLine: Loose gold and the balance it is weighed on, sitting in a soft pool of light on black velvet that falls away to nothing at the edges.
looks.groundSpec: Engine ground kind = 'velvet' (scripts/grounds.js K.velvet). PINNING, both halves required: FACESYS.grounds comes from LAB_GROUNDS and FACESYS.forceAbs from LAB_ABS (429), and 2829 reads abstractKind = !familyGround && (forceAbs || sd % 12 === 7) ? GK[(forceAbs ? sd : floor(sd/5)) % GK.length] : null. LAB_GROUNDS=velvet alone fires on one seed in twelve; LAB_ABS=1 alone draws from all 35 kinds. Run this theme as LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=velvet, which makes GK a single-entry list and puts velvet on every seed. dark(P) is true for nn10 (L 0.016), so the draw is c1 #2c1c37 flat, a radial from the centre rgba(#ffffff,0.12) out to rgba(0,0,0,0.35) at 0.75W, then grain at 0.08; velvet is in the no-extra-grain list so the usual 0.05 pass is skipped. That radial is the collection's one light in its literal form. SPOTLIGHT IS FORBIDDEN as a substitute: it is on the owner's never list in approved-grounds.json with marble, memphis and linen. TWO THINGS THIS GROUND COSTS, both measured: (1) the manifest tags the card ground:'abs' (3645), and lookFaults compares that against look.ground 'deep' (2539), so every card of this theme carries the line 'ground abs but the theme is deep', is re-seeded once at attempt 0 and ships warned at attempt 1 -- that is the expected signature, not a defect, but it means the palette and hero are drawn from the attempt-1 seed. (2) the solid-panel pass at 2963 is gated on __tileBg/__castBg and does not run on an abstract ground, so stat tiles keep the template's own translucent fill; the signature pass still forces the phone plate (support) and the kicker plate (support) opaque, so the small copy that must be legible belongs on those two. TICK STATUS, stated plainly: the owner's velvet ticks are velvet-ca07, -cd06, -du08, -jw05, -jw07; nn10 and nn02 are untested. They are used anyway because K.velvet fills c1 for any dark palette, so the draw is identical, and because the gold signature tones on jw05 and jw07 are pink/mint and purple/olive -- two foreign colours on the phone plate and the frame of a gold card.
looks.imagery: Hero is gold-scale-weighing (1659x1785): a cream laboratory balance with a small pile of gold in the pan -- the only asset in the library that pictures the sentence TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, which is why this theme exists. It is a large near-white body on a near-black ground, so it must be placed in the lit centre and it will out-light the accent band; treat the balance as the card's light and keep the accent to the money band alone. Because there is no flag that pins cutSrc, the draw is use[(sd*7+3) % 21] over the gold shelf, and this theme admits the weighing bench rather than the scale alone: gold-scale-weighing, gold-scrap-mixed (1752x1748), gold-rings-scatter (2048x2048), gold-earrings-pile (1054x838), gold-coins-pile (1212x859) -- five of twenty-one, so about one card in four lands and the rest are discarded. All five are loose gold on a counter, which is what a scale is for; the jewellery and bar heroes belong to Cuban Cast and Vault Wall and are barred. On an abstract ground the product layer survives (only the cast pass deletes it), so mustShow and neverShow are live here and the placement search sizes it from 520px down. Marks: one or two, ELEMENTS.gold, corners only on this card -- the flanks belong to the light.
looks.copy: The estate appraisal: quiet, private, unhurried -- the opposite of a gold-party ad. Headline: CASH IN YOUR / GOLD. Selling points: ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY plus TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, the second of which is the picture. Money band: PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Items line for this card: '10k - 14k - 18k - Scrap - Odd Earrings - Loose Rings - Gold Coins - Mixed Lots' -- every noun is a draw this theme admits. Kicker: GOLD BUYER. Trust line: SINCE 2015. Badges render LICENSED / DISCREET / PRIVATE. Numerals are JetBrains Mono and stay: the strip at 1578 replaces mono digits only when the palette family is not Space, Night Neon or Liquid Glass, and BOTH palettes here are Night Neon, so this is the one theme in the collection that keeps mono. Keep the balance's near-white body out of the copy's way: on this ground the type sits in the falloff above and below the lit centre.
variations: Scale alone in the light -- no second object, the emptiest card in the collection and the one that proves the ground
Scrap in the light -- gold-scrap-mixed as the draw, which is what the scale is for and reads as the estate lot the copy names
Vignette build (vignetteG, ticked on ca07/du08/jw05) instead of velvet for runs where velvet cannot be pinned: a linear c1 -> c2 with 0.45 dark edges
Gold light on aubergine (nn10) vs amber light on violet (nn02)
fixesApplied: Pinning corrected: BOTH LAB_ABS=1 and LAB_GROUNDS=velvet are required; LAB_ABS=1 alone draws from all 35 approved kinds and LAB_GROUNDS=velvet alone fires only when sd % 12 === 7
The abs/deep collision is stated instead of hidden: the manifest tags this card 'abs', lookFaults reports 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card, and the card ships from attempt 1

ground:abs removed from this theme's own neverShow (it is this theme's ground) and the inert kind-name tokens (mesh, blobs, bokeh, confetti, skyline, stars, carbon, frost, spotlight, marble, memphis, linen) dropped -- the matcher only understands tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab, flat
The solid-panel pass is named as NOT running on an abstract ground, with the two plates the signature pass does force opaque

The untested nn10/nn02 velvet pairing is declared, with the measured reason for keeping it: K.velvet fills c1 on any dark palette, while jw05 and jw07 would put a pink or purple phone plate and an olive frame on a gold card
The hero is constrained: five admissible loose-gold draws in mustShow, every jewellery, bar and watch asset in neverShow, and the yield stated (five of twenty-one)

The claim that the ground places the hero in the lit centre is replaced by the truth -- velvet draws only the ground, the layout's slot places the product -- and the near-white balance is called what it is, the card's light

looks.name: Sterling Drawer II
looks.oneLine: A canteen drawer pulled open after closing: nine pieces of sterling laid in an even twelve-cell lattice and dimmed sixty percent into petrol blue.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. Cells are 235 x 322.67 with 28px gaps; each cutout is fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box then scaled 0.96, so it occupies at most 202 x 287 of its cell. Shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offset 10/16. jw09 c1 #054666 (L 0.054) and c2 #023153 (L 0.028) are both deep, so `light` resolves to the hard-coded #eceef2 and scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. Silver is the ideal wall subject: it is the brightest family in the cutout library and survives the 60 per cent dim where a dark body does not. Panels over the wall go solid at rgba(#054666,0.9) with #ffffff copy (2963). Colour chain, and this is the correction the theme most needed: the money band takes th.accent (jw09 #fdc0b7 coral, jw05 #febbd3 pink), and because the accent is spent the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT -- jw09 #3ebfc9 cyan, jw05 #56c1a1 mint (1573). The cyan is on the card by design; it cannot be demoted to a hairline from a look. The kicker plate and the single-rule silver frame take SIG.silver.tone2 = accent2, a near-white (#ffedea / #feecf2), on two seeds in three (1596, 1604). So the card reads: cold metal on petrol, one warm band, one cool plate, a near-white rule. TYPE WARNING: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so WE BUY (6) and SILVER (6) are safe and any display line past 14 characters -- the full money line among them -- is re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed.
looks.imagery: The wall is engine-built and this is the true census: the MULTI filter drops silver-bars-row (-row) and silver-flatware-set (-set), leaving NINE objects for twelve cells, so three repeat -- silver-bar-single, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile. The fill order is pool[(n + sd) % 9], so which three repeat is decided by the seed: every object repeats on some seed, and no cell may carry a caption that names one piece. Verified by opening them: silver-flatware (364x587) is a tied bundle of antique forks and spoons, silver-bars (519x476) three plain poured bars, silver-coins-tube (1513x1586) a clear tube of Washington quarters with two loose coins -- the 90% coins the copy names. silver-tea-set and silver-serving-tray are rejected cutouts and can never appear. ONE PRODUCT SITS OVER THE WALL: the placement search adds a 'Hero Product' from the silver deck pool (all eleven approved silver- cutouts, so silver-bars-row and silver-flatware-set can be the hero even though they cannot be a cell) and evicts it if it overlaps text. Every one of the eleven is on-subject, so mustShow is the family prefix and nothing more is needed. 2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. - lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. - The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.

looks.oneLine: Brushed steel with a single band of light down the middle of it, one piece of bullion standing in the band and the type cut across the grain.
looks.groundSpec: Engine ground kind = 'brushed' (scripts/grounds.js K.brushed). Pin it the same way as the velvet theme: LAB_ABS=1 LAB_GROUNDS=brushed -- both, because LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve. K.brushed reads `const base = dark(P) ? '#2a2d33' : '#d9dce1'`, and both palettes here are dark, so the ground is the hard-coded near-black steel #2a2d33 (L about 0.026) on either one: horizontal 1px streaks every 2px at random alpha up to 0.06 white, then a left-to-right linear peaking at rgba(255,255,255,0.12) dead centre. TICK STATUS: brushed has exactly one owner tick, brushed-jw07. It is used here on jw05 and jw09 because the ground draw is palette-independent -- #2a2d33 either way -- and because jw07's support is olive #9eb666, which would put an olive phone plate on a silver card. The band is drawn by the ground; it does not place the product, so the layout's cutout slot has to sit near x = 0.5W for the piece to stand in the light.
looks.imagery: One piece of bullion standing in the light band. looks.oneLine: Eleven coin holdings -- trays, rolls, tubes, jars, albums, loose piles -- laid out flat on a dimmed green felt lattice under WE BUY / COINS.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. jw07 is the highest-scoring Jewel palette (50 per cent) and its ground #054e2f is a deep bottle green -- the coin-tray felt colour, which is why it leads. Both c1 (L 0.057) and c2 #003928 (L 0.031) are deep, so the lattice lands on #eceef2: 4x3, 28px gaps, cells 235 x 322.67, each cutout fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box then scaled 0.96 (at most 202 x 287), shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16, then scrimColor = #054e2f at 0.6. Panels solid at rgba(#054e2f,0.9), copy white. Colour chain: money band = accent (jw07 #e1c2fe lilac, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach); phone plate = support (#9eb666 olive on jw07, #53b9e0 sky on jw01); kicker plate and the dotted coins frame = accent2, a near-white, on two seeds in three. On jw07 the olive sits in the ground's own family, which is why a green palette can carry an olive plate without reading as a third colour. THIS THEME MUST NEVER INVOKE THE SLAB FRAME: slabFrame() is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ (3429), the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only, and ground:slab is in neverShow.
looks.imagery: The engine's wall, simulated against the current approved list: eleven objects for twelve cells, so exactly one repeats. looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: eight cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else. Ten were written; two are gone and the reasons are in droppedThemes.

FIVE LOCKS, ALL MEASURED IN THE REPO
1. GROUND VALUE. Seven palettes, every c1 under L 0.06: nn10 #2c1c37 0.016, nn02 #241f3b 0.017, jw02 #3e3577 0.049, jw01 #1f3e7a 0.051, jw09 #054666 0.054, jw05 #044a51 0.055, jw07 #054e2f 0.057. Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. But the card does not stop there: because the accent is spent, the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT (1573), and the kicker plate and the category's signature frame take SIG[cat].tone2 (1596, 1604). A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Phones take jw09 and jw01. Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. The old 'two lit plates is the fault' rule was describing something the engine does on purpose; this is the version that holds.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Key Date Cast II
looks.oneLine: A pair of Morgan dollars cast into deep indigo at two-thirds of the card's width, the window shadow cutting across them, the grade language in condensed caps on the lit side.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='cast' forces dg='cast' on every seed. Ground fills jw01 c1 #1f3e7a (L 0.051), then a white 0.10 -> 0 linear from the top-left. looks.name: Closing Time Wall II
looks.oneLine: The device wall from the shop's own site after hours: twelve single iPhones in an even lattice, dimmed sixty percent into petrol blue, with the opening hours running under the money band.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: look.ground='tile' forces dg='tile' on every seed. jw09 c1 #054666 (L 0.054) and c2 #023153 are both deep, so the lattice lands on the hard-coded #eceef2: 4x3, 28px gaps, cells 235 x 322.67, each cutout fitted inside a 211 x 298.67 box then scaled 0.96 (at most 202 x 287), shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16, then scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. Panels over the wall go solid at rgba(#054666,0.9) with #ffffff copy, which is what keeps UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY off the lattice. Colour chain: money band = accent (jw09 #fdc0b7 coral, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach); phone plate = support (#3ebfc9 cyan, #53b9e0 sky); kicker plate = SIG.phones.tone2 = support again; SIG.phones has no frame, so this is the only card in the collection without a signature rule around it. SET THE DECK EXPLICITLY TO DEVICE_DECKS.iphone: p.cat 'phones' rotates the Apple lines over ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'] (2792), so half the seeds are an iPad or a MacBook card. Those are caught by neverShow ('ipad', 'mac', 'qs-') as a product fault, but the fault does not change the deck on the retry, so they are discarded rather than repaired.
looks.imagery: The twelve cells are fixed by the engine, not chosen. Simulated against the current approved list -- deck prefixes plus SUBJECTS.iphone, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12) -- the wall is exactly twelve distinct objects with no repeat: iphone-15-pro-back-black, -blue, -gold, -white, iphone-15-pro-front-on, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, iphone-hand-back-offer, iphone-in-hand-screen-on, iphone-screen-on-glow, own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, own-apple-cosmic-orange-06. I opened all twelve. Six are clean bright backs (gold, white, silver, blue, and the two 17 Pro bodies), two are orange press renders (-02 a phone on a black plinth at 311px, -06 a close crop whose lower body is cut), two are screen-on units, and two are hand shots -- iphone-hand-back-offer is a champagne back whose left edge is scalloped where the fingers were removed, and iphone-in-hand-screen-on is a blank white screen with fingertip fragments at the left edge. Both are on the owner's approved list, and neither can be excluded from a wall: the cells are painted into the ground canvas where no mustShow or neverShow can reach them. That is the honest census, and it is why the census replaces the old rule about six bright cells, which no set of approved assets could satisfy. ONE PRODUCT SITS OVER THE WALL and that one IS governed: the placement search draws it from the iPhone deck pool of 22, and only the six clean backs are admitted -- six of the twenty-two, so about one card in four keeps its hero and the rest are discarded -- the two hand shots, both screen-on units, iphone-pair-front-back, the ip-group lineups, the four qs-iphone-17 press composites and all five own-apple singles are barred (the orange ones are 311-380px or carry a second object or a lit galaxy screen). Marks: ELEMENTS.phones in the palette tones; two in five are iOS emoji from the phone list.
looks.copy: The shop itself, not a pitch -- this is what is on the counter tonight. Headline: SELL YOUR / iPHONE. Selling points: CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED plus SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME. Money band: UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY, money word $1,100 -- bounded and checkable. The hours line carries the theme's name: OPEN 7 DAYS - 9AM-8PM - WALK-INS WELCOME. Items: iPhone 17 - 16 - 15 - Pro & Pro Max, which is the deck's own line; note that the library has no approved 16 cutout, so the wall shows 15 Pro and 17 Pro bodies under it -- every one of them is above the iPhone 12 floor, and the shop does buy the 16. Kicker: APPLE BUYER. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Cities: LONG BEACH - LAKEWOOD - DOWNEY - CARSON - TORRANCE. Payment line: CASH - ZELLE - VENMO - WIRE, YOUR CHOICE. Sticker: PAID TODAY. Badges render LICENSED / TRUSTED / LOCAL (the engine swaps INSURED to TRUSTED off the cars deck). Rating 4.9, five stars. AUDIT INTERLOCK: CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED is a copy claim, not a picture -- the wall stays clean units, because the owner's rejection list bars heavy damage imagery outright.
