looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: eight cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else. Ten were written; two are gone and the reasons are in droppedThemes.

FIVE LOCKS, ALL MEASURED IN THE REPO
1. GROUND VALUE. Seven palettes, every c1 under L 0.06: nn10 #2c1c37 0.016, nn02 #241f3b 0.017, jw02 #3e3577 0.049, jw01 #1f3e7a 0.051, jw09 #054666 0.054, jw05 #044a51 0.055, jw07 #054e2f 0.057. Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE ACCENT, AND WHERE THE ENGINE PUTS THE REST. The accent fills exactly one plate -- the money band, set at retheme_lab.mjs:1047 and locked. But the card does not stop there: because the accent is spent, the phone plate takes th.SUPPORT (1573), and the kicker plate and the category's signature frame take SIG[cat].tone2 (1596, 1604). A look cannot change that, so the palettes are chosen BY IT. Gold's supports are all muted golds -- nn10 #b68b1b, nn02 #cd7c0e, jw02 #c39550 -- so every plate on a gold card is a gold on a violet ground. Silver's are the cool metal tones, jw09 #3ebfc9 and jw05 #56c1a1, against near-white kicker plates. Coins take jw07 (olive #9eb666 inside its own green) and jw01 (sky #53b9e0). Phones take jw09 and jw01. Night Neon's Indigo Cash (nn01) and Blue Value (nn09) are excluded for this reason alone: their supports are green #5bbf43 and lime #98b318, and that third hue would land on the phone plate of every card. The old 'two lit plates is the fault' rule was describing something the engine does on purpose; this is the version that holds.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display comes only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko (stencil scored 60 per cent and condensed 49 per cent in the Set 8 result); support is always a grotesque (56 per cent); the number is the display face when that face is plain and the support face when it is not, which is the engine's own pairing rule -- so the three stencil themes set their numerals in the support face and no card carries three families. MEASURED TRAP: LIMIT['Big Shoulders Stencil Display'] = 14 (1092), so any display line longer than 14 characters is silently re-set in Oswald / Big Shoulders Display / Barlow Condensed -- headlines are safe, a 24-character money line is not. Monospace numerals survive only where EVERY palette on the theme is Night Neon (the strip at 1578 is per card family, not per lead palette); that is one theme, Under One Lamp.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY: gold, silver, coins, phones -- four of the eight real donor categories. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches, and no slab frame (slabFrame is gated to look.ground==='slab' or /pokemon|sports/ at 3429, and the owner set slab framing as Pokemon and sports only). iPad, MacBook and Watch are decks that rotate inside phones, not categories: p.cat 'phones' walks ['iphone','iphone','iphone','ipad','ipad','macbook'], so half of the phone theme's seeds are not iPhone cards and are discarded.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. The cash- cutouts and the cash ground (33 per cent) are barred collection-wide; money-bag-sack and safe-open-cash are approved assets but no deck names them, so they cannot reach a card and are not written into a list as if a rule were catching them. The line-art cash and dollar MARKS in ELEMENTS.gold/coins/phones cannot be barred from a look -- see below -- so they are a discard rule, not a rule the engine enforces.

WHAT A LOOK CAN AND CANNOT CONTROL -- read this before trusting any list in this collection
- lookFaults (2519) reads exactly four kinds of neverShow entry: a literal startsWith against the names of CUTOUT LAYERS, a ground: token, a logo: token, and an assets/ path matched against the background src. Everything else -- mark:, treat:, seal:, and every prose token like two-lit-plates or hero-over-wall -- matches nothing. Those are gone from this collection; what is left is what bites.
- The only ground: values that exist are tile, cast, abs, cash, scene, photo, slab and flat. ground:mesh, ground:spotlight, ground:frost and the rest were inert: every abstract kind reports as 'abs'.
- Prefix matching is literal startsWith. 'sam-' does not match samsung-fold-open or samsung-galaxy-back, and 'watch-' does not match apple-watch-single, so both spellings are listed. It also means a neverShow prefix can shadow a mustShow name: 'silver-bars' would bar silver-bars-stack, 'coin-stack' bars coin-stack-silver, 'gold-jewelry' bars gold-jewelry-mixed. Every list here has been checked for that; where a prefix cannot separate two assets, the theme says which one it accepts.
- A TILE WALL'S CELLS ARE INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE. They are painted into the ground canvas, not added as layers, so mustShow and neverShow govern only the ONE product the placement search puts over the wall (3169) -- and the pool for the wall itself is fixed by the engine: the deck's prefixes plus the subject's whole approved shelf, minus MULTI, minus width<240, then slice(0,12). Each theme names the exact cells that produces today.
- A CAST GROUND DELETES THE PRODUCT LAYER (3428: the product is the ground), so on the two cast themes there are no cutout layers at all and mustShow/neverShow test nothing. There is no LAB flag that pins cutSrc; the hero is use[(sd*7+3) % pool] over the whole deck shelf. Both cast themes therefore name their admissible heroes and their yield, and the guard is the manifest's `product` field (3645), not the matcher.
- THE LOOK DOES NOT OWN ITS CATEGORY. The card's category is RING[(base + variant) % 8] over ['phones','gold','cars','pokemon','coins','silver','sports','strips'] (2735); the categories array is a statement of intent that the engine does not read. A card that lands off-category faults on neverShow, but `base` and the variant do not change on the retry, so it faults twice and ships warned -- it is discarded, not repaired. Plan for roughly one card in eight per theme landing on its own category, or restrict the run.
- Kicker text, mark choice, emoji-versus-line-art, the items line and the challenge opener are all seeded and unpinnable. Two marks in five are iOS emoji from ELEMENTS[cat].emoji unless the family is Lined Paper, so the 'line art only, never emoji' rule that was written here is not enforceable: the gold list contains a watch glyph and the phone list a battery, and those are the draws to discard. INFO.yes still contains 'WE MATCH REAL OFFERS, NO HOOPS' and the challenge opener draws WE MATCH one time in four, printing WE MATCH / CASH4GOLD with no object -- the standing rule wants an object, so those cards are discarded too.

GROUNDS: drawn only. tile x4 (100 per cent approval), cast x2 (50 per cent), deep x2 (the velvet and brushed procedural grounds, pinned with LAB_ABS=1 plus LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or brushed -- both flags, since LAB_GROUNDS alone fires on one seed in twelve). No photograph (28 per cent, and the coins photo theme it would have carried is in droppedThemes), no apple scene, no slab, no paper, no cash. The two deep themes report 'ground abs but the theme is deep' on every card because the manifest tags an abstract ground 'abs' while the studio's word for a dark drawn ground is 'deep' -- expected, and it means those cards ship from the second attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST DRAFT: Ink Pop is not a deep family (ik01-ik10 c1 runs L 0.865-0.878, near-white) and Duotone is mid-tone (du01-du10 L 0.270-0.318), so both stay out. Two claims from the first draft are withdrawn: 'seal:INSURED' guarded nothing -- 1385 already swaps INSURED to DISCREET, BONDED or TRUSTED off the cars deck -- and glow is not disabled by the condensed interlock, which is why neonNight is barred from every theme here (it has no gold, silver or coins donor either, and its headlines are authored with no fill and two different stroke colours).

ASSETS: the approved shelf is 349 ids, of which the LEGACY regex removes five (four ip-gen* AI renders and iphone-cracked-corner), leaving 344 files in ALLCUTS -- the brief's 345 counts iphone-cracked-corner, which LEGACY removes as well. Fifteen ids this collection once named are rejected and appear nowhere: own-apple-deep-blue-09 and -18, own-apple-silver-11 and -15 (all four are orange phones in 3D debris, mislabelled), own-apple-cosmic-orange-03 and -10, strip-kit-meter (a fabricated wordmark), own-stock-macbook-open, ipad-front, macbook-open, mac-air-open-angle, coin-slab-graded, silver-tea-set, silver-serving-tray, gold-nuggets-raw. The only clean own-apple singles left are cosmic-orange-02, -06, -07, -16 and -20, and none of them is good enough to build a card on -- which is what killed the orange cast theme.

looks.name: Blue Pen Estimate II
looks.oneLine: A cream ruled sheet with three punch holes down the left, an offer typed out in indigo ballpoint, one yellow highlighter across the money line, and a single Apple unit laid on the page with its own shadow.
looks.groundSpec: Sheet: paper:ruled — #fbf7ea stock, 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px from y=150, a 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes down the left at 18/50/82% of height, fibre noise and a 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10) to 0 binding shadow at the head. Painted as bg {type:'image', src:'paper:ruled', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001} so the palette never tints the paper; Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. THIS RECORD MUST CARRY key:'written-quote-blue-pen-estimate' and sheet:'paper:ruled', and needs the four collection-wide engine changes (key lookup, categories ring, look.sheet at line 2650, a paper branch in groundNow at 2525); without them the look never applies, the stock rotates on seed%5 and every card self-audits as a ground mismatch. PALETTES BY THE NAME THE OWNER SEES: lp01 Indigo Cash, accent #084f88, and lp08 Indigo Trade, accent #0c42ab — deep indigo ballpoint, not navy-the-adjective. THE PEN IS THE ONLY COLOUR: pen on the money word and the phone number, #26231f on kicker, sub, items, CTA, badges and website. The engine assigns headline ink by layer parity at 2691, which on bandKnockout puts both headline lines on #26231f and never shows the pen; assign by headline order instead — opener in ink, money word in pen. ONE HIGHLIGHTER, AND IT IS THE LAYOUT THAT GUARANTEES IT: checklistHero's only convertible rect is the 760x194 CTA card and bandKnockout's is the 1012x252 knockout band (a money plate at 1047, so it clears the 210px height test). Stroke at 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle plus or minus 0.8 degrees, with the Marker Overrun twin beneath at 0.30 opacity, 22px longer, angle minus 0.6, so the ends run past the words. Squares under 130px become solid pen boxes with white numerals; circles — checklistHero's three tick discs and trust()'s check — take the pen, which is right here. THE SNAP MUST MOVE THE ROW: line 2684 snaps single-line text to the 54px grid and leaves the tick disc behind, landing the three Point rows on 632/686/794 against discs at 566/662/758 with an uneven 54/108 gap. Until the snap carries circle, number box and label together, bandKnockout is the only safe layout on this stock, and checklistHero ships only after that fix. PALE VS DEEP: both palettes are pale (c1 #ecf4fd, #eef4fe) and the sheet is drawn rather than derived, so a pale palette changes nothing; a deep one would leave the cream cream and only darken the pen. The sheet is never inverted.
looks.imagery: One Apple unit, never a pile — the engine places exactly one cutout per card and assortments are off, so this is structural. Every own-apple- id is gone: I opened all five that survive the asset pass and they are AI fabrications rather than Apple press renders — own-apple-cosmic-orange-02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 adds an abstract orange blob beside the phone, and -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. The clean pool is seven cutouts, each one unit, screen off or back to camera, none bringing a second colour system. iPhone leads with iphone-17-pro-back-black, a single black unit at a three-quarter tilt, then iphone-17-pro-back-silver, a flat silver back, then iphone-15-pro-back-white. iPad takes ipad-with-keyboard, one iPad in a Magic Keyboard with the screen off and no home button, or ipad-with-pencil. MacBook takes mac-pro-open-front, screen off, function-row keyboard and a uniform-thickness body — the only approved Mac cutout that can be dated to the M-series — with mac-half-open-glow as the dark rear-three-quarter alternate. The qs- press renders stay off: qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3 and qs-device-macbook-pro are each either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render carrying a full iridescent wallpaper. DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose 'own-apple-cosmic-orange', and this record needs cuts overrides per Apple line — ['iphone-17-pro-back','iphone-15-pro-back-white'], ['ipad-with-keyboard','ipad-with-pencil'], ['mac-pro-open-front','mac-half-open-glow'] — or 19 of the iPhone deck's 22 cutouts fault. The unit sits lower right, clear of every text box, with a real cast shadow onto the sheet; one or two pen marks (phoneMark, bolt, check, dollar) in free corners in th.accent and th.ink, never emoji, never mid-card.
neverShow: more than one cutout layer on a card, or a cutout whose filename does not start with one of this theme's mustShow prefixes
a product cutout over any line of type — it yields to the words or it is dropped
handwriting faces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand, Shadows Into Light, Gloria Hallelujah, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Amatic SC, Cabin Sketch)
trustSeal, whose six converted panels would put six highlighter bands on the sheet
a second highlighter stroke, a second sticky colour, a second pen hue, a curved headline, a gradient fill, a glass rim, a neon glow, a vignette or a grain layer
looks.copy: Plain and specific, the way a counter clerk writes a figure down and hands the paper over. Headline: SELL YOUR iPHONE, the opener in #26231f and the money word in the pen. Selling points, three lines from the deck's sub: SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME / CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED / WE MEET YOU LOCALLY OR YOU MAIL IT IN. Items: iPhone 17 • 16 • 15 • Pro & Pro Max. Money, under the one highlighter: UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: PAID TODAY. The iPad and MacBook cards take their own deck copy unchanged — SELL YOUR iPAD with UP TO $850 PAID TODAY, SELL YOUR MACBOOK with UP TO $1,900 PAID TODAY and WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE — so the headline and the picture are never on different subjects. This record carries challenge:false: the competitor card belongs to Two Numbers Sheet.

looks.collectionNote:
Eight sheets of real stationery with an offer written out on them. Two of the original ten are gone (see droppedThemes) because their categories have no cutout that shows what the card talks about.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY OPENING FILES, and what it changed. All five surviving own-apple-* cutouts are AI fabrications, not Apple press renders: -02 and -07 stand a phone with a camera plateau Apple never shipped on a dark navy plinth and a metal wedge, -06 carries a raised rounded back panel and a melted logo, -16 puts an abstract orange blob beside the phone, -20 is screen-on with a full-colour galaxy wallpaper. Every own-apple- id is therefore banned collection-wide and DEVICE_DECKS.iphone.cuts must lose the 'own-apple-cosmic-orange' entry that leads it. Every qs- Apple render I opened (qs-iphone-17-pro, qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-device-macbook-pro) is either a two-up back-plus-front composite or a screen-on render with a full iridescent wallpaper, so none can appear on a sheet whose claim is one ink. iphone-15-pro-back-black is a macro crop of a camera corner, not a unit. car-keys-fob is a hand holding a fob whose badge is a garbled three-oval marque — a fabricated emblem of the same class as strip-kit-meter — and car-hand-keys-over, despite its name, is a plain unbranded flip key with no hand in it. The clean pool is small and it is named exactly in each theme.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY DOES, measured against scripts/retheme_lab.mjs and app.js, because six of the ten original recipes described behaviour the code does not have.
1. look.key: lines 554, 563 and 2764 look a record up by L.key; assets/looks.json entries carry only id. Until each record carries key === its id, no look applies at all and every card falls back to a random palette and the handwritten Lined Paper faces from pickFaces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand).
2. look.categories is dead. The plan at 549-562 reads only layouts, variations, palettes and key; wantCat comes from RING[(base + e.v) % 8] at 2731. Every look in this collection currently receives cards from all eight categories, so a silver look's mustShow fails on seven cards in eight and the re-seed cannot help (base does not include attempt). Seed the ring from look.categories.
3. look.sheet does not exist. Line 2650 rotates the four stocks on seed%5, so every 'this look pins X' claim holds one or two cards in five. Change to const sheet = (look && look.sheet) || [...][seed % 5] and give each record its sheet.
4. ground:'paper' now works one way and not the other: line 2886 makes a paper look skip tile, cast, photo, scene and slab grounds, but groundNow at 2525 has no paper branch, so bg 'paper:ruled' reads as 'flat' and every card in this collection self-audits as "ground flat but the theme is paper" and burns its one re-seed. Add : /^paper:/.test(bg) ? 'paper'.
5. The 54px baseline snap (2684) moves single-line text and leaves its furniture behind. On checklistHero the three Point rows land on baselines 632/686/794 while their tick discs stay at 566/662/758: the ticks detach and the row gap goes 54, then 108. Until the snap carries the row group, only bandKnockout is geometrically safe on ruled and legal stock — which is why the four ruled/legal themes here ship checklistHero and bandKnockout only, and the four grid/dot themes (no snap at all) carry stepsFlow and reviewProof.
6. The highlighter count is a property of the layout, not of the recipe. familyTreatment converts any rect that is a money plate, or 200px+ wide and 210px or less tall, into a highlighter. On the real templates that is one stroke on checklistHero (the 760x194 CTA card) and one on bandKnockout (the 1012x252 knockout band, which becomes a money plate at 1047 and so clears the height test), four on stepsFlow (kicker pill plus three step cards), four on reviewProof (rate pill plus three chips, with the 940x336 quote card becoming the sticky note) and SIX on trustSeal (status pill, four 442x148 tiles, phone plate). trustSeal is out of this collection entirely: six pastel bands on a paper sheet is the jumbled colour mess the owner rejects, and its seal circle would fill solid #accent under the circle branch at 2698. Dropping it also removes the only place a card showed a single '4.9★' glyph; the one star run left in the collection is reviewProof's ★★★★★, which is five.
7. Headline ink is assigned by layer parity (2691: fill = (k % 2 === 0) ? pen : inkDark). On bandKnockout both headline lines land on #26231f and the pen never reaches the headline. Assign by headline order instead: the opener takes the ink, the money word takes the pen.
8. looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH ONLY. jw05 c1 #044a51 (measured luminance 0.055) and jw06 c1 #014c44 (0.056) are far below the 0.55 pale threshold, so drawGround fills flat c1, lays a white diagonal sheen from 0.10 at the top-left to zero at 55% across, draws the hero at min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) centred on 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with a black 0.35 shadow (blur 40, offset 24/30), then the blind: a blur-26 parallelogram at 0.50 with its top edge at 0.62W and its bottom edge at 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at 0.25. Scrim is c1 itself at 0.22 — the room stays a saturated teal, no ink veil, no grey. The orange body is the only warm thing in the frame, against its split-complement; that is the whole picture idea. jw05's accent #febbd3 and jw06's #fdb6f2 carry the price plate and the sticker; the trust panel goes solid at rgba(c1, 0.9) with white copy, which the engine applies automatically once __castBg is set. THE PALETTE LIST IS CLOSED at [jw05, jw06]: a warm ground collapses the card to orange-on-orange mud, the owner's banned dark-orange card. looks.collectionNote:
WINDOW LIGHT, REPAIRED: EIGHT CARDS, EACH ONE OBJECT IN A COLOURED ROOM WITH A BLIND DRAWN ACROSS IT. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity (retheme_lab.mjs line 2882): fill c1, a white diagonal sheen 0.10 to zero across 55%, the hero fitted at k = min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) and drawn at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (black 0.35, blur 40, offset 24/30); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it (blur 26 at full strength from 0.62W to 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half); then a scrim. Line 3424 deletes every Hero/Lineup Product layer once __castBg is set, so the product IS the background and nothing is ever drawn over the type. Panels go solid over a cast ground (line 2959), so every card is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. Cast is measured at 50% approval — the second-best real ground — and this collection deliberately spends it rather than the 100% tile wall, because tile belongs to the device-wall, metal-wall and card-wall collections and a lattice cannot show ONE object at print scale. The one way a window-light card can lose its identity is the cast→tile fall-through at line 2891 when the hero image fails to load; lookFaults already catches that as "ground tile but the theme is cast" and re-seeds once.

ROSTER, EIGHT THEMES: Cosmic Orange Room and Titanium Daylight (iPhone line), MacBook Desk and iPad Desk (the split of the old Apple Silicon Desk), Gold On Velvet, Sterling Counter, Coin Stack Light (renamed from window-light-coin-tray; the tray it was named for is now barred, see that theme), Forecourt Light (Garage Night folded in as its bikes-deck cut). Dropped: Clinic Window and Slab Under Glass. Two categories therefore have no theme here — pokemon (poke-slabs-trio is the only approved file and it is three empty pastel slabs) and strips and sports for the reasons in droppedThemes. Shipping nothing beats shipping a 670px blank.

FOUR RULES THIS REPAIR ADDS, ALL PROGRAMMABLE, ALL RE-RUN AGAINST EVERY FILE I NAME. (1) NO UPSCALE: a cast hero must satisfy min(669.6/w, 993.6/h) <= 1 on a 1080 card, i.e. at least 670px wide OR at least 994px tall. All 24 heroes in the eight themes pass (the worst is own-apple-cosmic-orange-06 at 0.931). It is also what independently disqualifies every qs- press render (qs-device-macbook-pro is 381x230, k=1.76) and the five short-named legacy files below. (2) WHOLE UNIT, NEVER A MACRO CROP: it removes iphone-15-pro-back-black (I opened it — a tight crop of the camera corner, not a phone) and ipad-with-pencil (an iPad corner running off frame). (3) COOL INK, CLOSED PALETTE LIST: on a pale palette (lum(c1) > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room with th.ink at 0.20, an accent→ink gradient, and an ink scrim at 0.30 — about half the finished ground is INK — so a pale palette is chosen by its ink and the ink must be cool: ink red channel at least 16 below blue. Measured: pa05 -28, ca07 -40, ca01 -36, cd05 -38, cd06 -46 pass; cd04 (#263f2b) is -5 and FAILS, so the old collectionNote's claim that the test "passes cd04" was false and cd04 is gone from the collection. Every palette list below is closed. (4) ONE PRODUCT ARRANGEMENT PER CARD, not one product: one object or one deliberate group (a flatware fan, a candlestick pair, a chain coil, the owner's own stack of five MacBooks), never a lattice and never a repeat pattern — which is what removes gold-rings-scatter (thirteen near-identical bands bleeding off all four edges).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, NOT FROM THE RECIPE. Already applied, no action: the look lookup now reads (L.key || L.id) at lines 560/2731/2768, so looks.json entries keyed by `id` do bind; the category binding is in at 2729-2733 — `lookCats = look.categories.filter(c => RING0.includes(c))` — which is exactly why a theme's categories array may hold only phones/gold/cars/pokemon/coins/silver/sports/strips: "macbook", "ipad" or "bikes" filter to empty and the look silently walks all eight categories again; and slabFrame at 3425 is now gated `(!look && /pokemon|sports/…)`, so no look on a cast ground can be overwritten by a slab frame. STILL OUTSTANDING, and this collection is not correct without them: P2, the Apple-line binding — line 2797 `DEVICE_DECKS[APPLE[sd % APPLE.length]]` must become `DEVICE_DECKS[(look && look.line) || APPLE[…]]`, or half of every phones card is an iPad or a MacBook; P3, the pool binding — line 2805 `const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f))` must become `const allow = look && (look.mustShow||[]).filter(m => ALLCUTS.includes(m)); const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f) && (!allow || !allow.length || allow.includes(f)));` — read the allow-list off mustShow itself rather than adding a parallel `cuts` map, so the stated rule and the actual pool can never drift apart; P6, the enforcement gap — on a cast card line 3424 has already deleted the hero layer by the time lookFaults runs, so `names` is empty and BOTH mustShow and the cutout half of neverShow are vacuous: record `t2.__castCut = cutSrc.split('/').pop().replace(/\.webp$/,'')` at line 2916 and include it in `names` at line 2521, or every asset rule in this collection is advisory; P7, line 201 and the sub-deck at 325 — drop Ducati from the bikes items line, it is not an allowed marque and a look supplies no copy; P9, the no-upscale gate — in the cast branch skip a hero whose k > 1 and take the next candidate. P9 is not decoration: prefix matching is literal startsWith, so gold-chains, gold-jewelry, gold-bars, silver-flatware and coin-stack (624x457, 511x226, 461x326, 364x587, 555x276 — all upscales) CANNOT be barred by neverShow without also barring gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-bars-stack, silver-flatware-set and coin-stack-silver, which are the heroes. Those five files are the only holes left in the collection's neverShow coverage and P9 is what closes them. looks.name: Titanium Daylight II
looks.oneLine: A black, silver or white iPhone lying in a cool daylight room with the blind across it, the copy in the bright corner and a vermilion or magenta price plate as the only other colour.
looks.groundSpec: PALE BRANCH, DELIBERATELY. ca07 c1 #b9f7f6 (measured luminance 0.835) and cd06 c1 #80dafd (0.618) both clear 0.55, so the room is repainted: c1, then ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of accent 0.18 to ink 0.10, then a white sheen 0.12 to zero, then the hero, then the blind at 0.58 with its 0.29 penumbra, then a scrim of ink at 0.30 (scrimColor resolves to th.ink for both — c2 luminances 0.664 and 0.480 are above the 0.45 cut). Both inks pass the cool test with room to spare: ca07 #173f3f is R-B -40, cd06 #1b3d49 is -46, so the finished ground is a deep teal or deep petrol room, never taupe. The accent does the window light: ca07's #d8360a lays a vermilion wash across the top 40%, cd06's #ab117d a magenta one. This is the collection's answer to 'a pale palette goes grey': you are not lighting a white room, you are lighting a dark teal room whose highlights came from a pale palette. PALETTE LIST CLOSED at [ca07, cd06] — the cool-ink test rejects pp02 (+42), pp04 (+9), io04 (+41), gl02 (+35), cd04 (-5) and every su id.
looks.imagery: Three heroes, all opened, all whole units at print scale: assets/cutouts/iphone-17-pro-back-black.webp (1008x1837, cast scale 0.541 — the lead, the strongest silhouette under a rake), iphone-17-pro-back-silver.webp (799x1668, 0.596 — a whole silver body, front-on) and iphone-15-pro-back-white.webp (1430x1634, 0.468 — a white body at three-quarter with the frame catching the light). DROPPED FROM THE OLD LIST: iphone-15-pro-back-black is not a phone, it is a tight macro crop of the camera corner — at 670px it reads as an abstract lens cluster (I opened it); ip-angle-hero-tilt is a good picture but unreachable, the iphone deck's prefixes carry ip-group- and no ip-angle. Items line: iPhone 17 • 16 • 15 • Pro & Pro Max. Price plate: UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: CASH TODAY. Five stars from reviewProof. Only named wholesale buyers may be named — Gazelle, Best Buy, Verizon — never an unbounded 'any offer'.

looks.name: Gold On Velvet II
looks.oneLine: One Cuban bracelet, a coil of chain or a stack of bars lying large in a forest-green or wine room, the blind across it, a serif headline and the tested-and-weighed promise in the light.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw07 c1 #054e2f (measured luminance 0.057) is a jeweller's forest green; jw10 c1 #6a2245 (0.046) a wine. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with the black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. Gold is the only warm thing in the frame and the room is its complement, which is how a jeweller lays gold on a green or burgundy tray. The white diagonal sheen matters more here than anywhere else in the collection: it is what makes the link edges flash where the blind has not reached them. jw07's accent #e1c2fe (lilac) and jw10's #94e994 (mint) go on the price plate and the sticker only — never on the metal, never behind it. A PALE PALETTE IS BARRED: the pale branch would wash a 0.30 ink scrim over gold and turn it to brass, and the two palettes PALFIT prefers for gold (pp02 ink R-B +42, gl02 +35) both fail the cool-ink test. Palette list closed at [jw07, jw10]. jw10's own ink is warm at +11, which is admitted only because the deep branch never veils.
looks.imagery: Six heroes, every one opened at full size: assets/cutouts/gold-bracelet-cuban.webp (1484x1184, cast scale 0.451 — the owner's stated lead, a clean Cuban link bracelet), gold-chains-pile.webp (2048x1718, 0.327 — a coil of Cuban and Figaro chain, one arrangement), gold-necklace-single.webp (1314x1591, 0.510 — a single heavy Cuban necklace), gold-bars-stack.webp (2048x1555, 0.327 — six bars whose only legible stamp is the word GOLD, the rest soft and uncontradicted), gold-jewelry-mixed.webp (2048x1734, 0.327 — a contained heap of bangles, rings and a medallion) and gold-scale-weighing.webp (1659x1785, 0.404 — an analytical balance with gold actually on the pan, for the tested-and-weighed cut only, never the lead: the appliance is bigger than the metal). BARRED WITH REASONS I CHECKED BY OPENING THE FILES: gold-rings-scatter is about thirteen near-identical wedding bands bleeding off all four edges — a repeat pattern, not an object, which is what the collection refuses; gold-bars-fan (NEW FINDING, not in the audit) is stamped SS019 WORR GOLD and 200g with mirrored nonsense along one bar — legible fabricated text at 670px, the same fault that condemned silver-bars-row's WILD BOLD / 69906. gold-chains, gold-jewelry and gold-bars cannot be barred by prefix without blocking gold-chains-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed and gold-bars-stack; they are 624x457, 511x226 and 461x326, so patch P9's no-upscale gate is what stops them.

looks.name: Sterling Counter II
looks.oneLine: A row of tarnished sterling flatware, a pair of candlesticks or a heap of silver jewellery laid large in a near-black blue room with the blind across it and the spot-shown promise in the light.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH, THE DEEPEST IN THE COLLECTION. nn09 c1 #002838 (measured luminance 0.018) and nn05 c1 #002c20 (0.019) are near-black blue and near-black teal. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H, -0.12 rad, contact shadow black 0.35, blind at 0.50 with the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. Silver has almost no colour of its own, so the room has to supply all of it: on a pale ground tarnished sterling is literally grey on grey, the failure this collection was briefed to solve. At luminance 0.018 the flatware becomes the brightest thing on the card by a wide margin and the tarnish reads as depth rather than dirt. nn09's accent #fda8bb and nn05's #d4b2fd carry the price plate; the trust panel goes solid at rgba(c1, 0.9) with white copy. Both inks are cool (#d1e1e9 -24, #d2e3dc -10). Palette list closed at [nn09, nn05]. Night Neon has no measured approval data of its own, which is stated here rather than hidden: the case for it is the luminance, not a score.
looks.imagery: Three heroes, and only three, because the rest of the silver shelf is unusable at 670px. All opened: assets/cutouts/silver-flatware-set.webp (1989x1919, cast scale 0.337 — seven pieces of genuinely tarnished sterling laid in a row, the lead), silver-candlesticks.webp (1314x1640, 0.510 — a matched pair, one arrangement) and silver-jewelry-mixed.webp (2048x1681, 0.327 — bangles and chains in one heap). THE BULLION FILES STAY BARRED AND I RE-CHECKED WHY: silver-bars-stack is silver-coloured bars stamped GOLD, silver-bars-row is stamped WILD BOLD / 69906, silver-rounds-pile carries Bitcoin symbols and reads UNITED SATES OF AMERICA. Because the honest heroes are sterling and hollowware, the headline is sterling and hollowware — the imagery decided the copy, not the other way round. silver-flatware (364x587) cannot be barred by prefix without blocking silver-flatware-set; the no-upscale gate (it would be drawn at 1.69x) is what stops it.
looks.copy: Plain and weight-led — silver sellers are usually clearing a house, so the copy is about the process, not the shine. Headline: WE BUY STERLING SILVERWARE (one sentence, Saira Condensed, one weight, one colour). Selling point: WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN. looks.name: Forecourt Light II
looks.oneLine: One vehicle — a silver sedan, a white pickup, a cargo van or a naked motorcycle — parked large in a daylight-teal or midnight-navy room with the blind across its flank and a stencilled headline in the light.
looks.groundSpec: ONE PALE, ONE DEEP. ca01 c1 #baf8f1 (measured luminance 0.839) clears 0.55 and takes the pale path, so the room is repainted by its ink #183f3c (R-B -36, comfortably cool) at 0.20 plus a 0.30 scrim, with its accent #d9322b laying a crimson wash across the top at 0.18 — a deep teal shed with late sun coming through. nn01 c1 #0e253c (0.017) is a midnight navy on the unveiled path: flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero, black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22 — the garage at nine at night, with accent #fcaca5 as the one neon on the price plate. Every body in the pool is white or silver, which is why the room must carry the colour: a white van on a white ground is the grey card, a white van on a teal ground is a photograph. The blind is at its most literal here, reading as light through a roller door across the flank. Big Shoulders Stencil Display is the collection's one stencil face and it belongs on this theme — stencil is the top-scoring style at 60% and it reads as fleet marking rather than decoration. Palette list closed at [ca01, nn01]. nn04 (#39181e), the old Garage Night oxblood, is dropped: its ink is warm at R-B +16 measured, and an unenforceable 'fall back if it ever reads brown on a proof' is not a rule a run can apply.
looks.imagery: Four heroes, one for each deck the cars slot rotates through (line 2793, VEHICLES = cars, cars, bikes, trucks, vans), all opened: assets/cutouts/car-sedan-front.webp (2048x1366, cast scale 0.327 — a silver sedan in three-quarter front; the grille emblem is a Toyota Crown and Toyota is an allowed marque) for the cars deck, car-truck-front.webp (1869x1599, 0.358 — a white crew-cab pickup) for trucks, car-van-cargo.webp (1903x1689, 0.352 — a white high-roof Sprinter-shape body; Mercedes is allowed) for vans, and car-motorcycle-side.webp (1790x1886, 0.374 — a modern naked bike from the rear three-quarter, white tank, black engine and rear tyre; I zoomed the tank and the badge is an illegible emblem, so the card never implies a marque) for bikes. This one look therefore owns the whole cars slot instead of sharing it. BARRED WITH REASONS I VERIFIED AT ZOOM: car-sedan-rear is a C7-facelift Audi A6 and Audi is first on the owner's too-niche list; car-suv-side is a black Lincoln, a marque not on the allowed list, and a black body defeats the white-or-silver-against-a-coloured-room premise. Keys, titles, wheels, engine bays, the classic and the damaged front are all barred: the premise is the vehicle itself in the light, and a key fob at three-quarter scale is not the thing the headline names.
looks.copy: Flat and operational — a tow, a title, a number, no adjectives. Headline: WE BUY CARS, or WE BUY TRUCKS / WE BUY WORK VANS / WE BUY MOTORCYCLES, matched to the deck the card is running and to the vehicle in the ground (one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour). Selling point: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE TOW (bikes: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE LOAD IT). Second selling point: TITLE, DMV AND LIEN PAYOFF HANDLED (bikes: TITLE OR NOT, RUNNING OR NOT). Items line: Title In Hand • Running Or Not • High Miles • Salvage • Free Tow. Price plate: UP TO $15,000 CASH (trucks $25,000, vans $20,000, bikes $12,000). CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER. Sticker: SAME DAY. Five stars from reviewProof. NO MARQUE IS EVER PRINTED OR DRAWN: no wordmark (every logo: layer is barred, which is what stops the brand-led path inking a TOYOTA mark into a corner) and none of TOYOTAS, TACOMAS, TUNDRAS, HONDAS, FORDS, F-150S, TRANSITS, CHEVYS, SILVERADOS, NISSANS, JEEPS, TESLAS, BMWS, MERCEDES, SPRINTERS, HYUNDAIS, KIAS, DODGES, RAMS, HARLEYS, YAMAHAS, KAWASAKIS or DUCATIS in a headline — these live here in copy because an uppercase word in neverShow is tested against lowercase filenames and can never match. Patch P7 is required with this theme: the engine's own bikes items line at line 201 prints Ducati, which is not an allowed marque and which a look cannot overwrite. Comparative cuts are allowed on named wholesale buyers only, without an apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CARVANA, WE TOP CARMAX.

looks.name: Mint Counter Wall II
looks.oneLine: The engine's device wall drowned in pastel teal, with the shop's plainest counter copy on solid ink plates and a magenta money word.
looks.groundSpec: pa05 c1 #c6faeb has luminance 0.864, so the plane keeps the mint rather than falling back to #eceef2. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7; every unit is contain-fitted to its OWN cell at min((cw-24)/w,(chh-24)/h)*0.96, so the wall is not one scale and this recipe does not claim it is. One contact shadow per cell, rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, +10/+16. Veil is the palette ink #1b4037 (luminance 0.042, so the scrim is 0.60, not 0.72). The panel pass then fills EVERY rect between 150x60 and 0.92W x 0.92H with rgba(#1b4037,0.90) — several solid plates, not one counter-card; white on that tone measures 11.4:1, so the small print holds on all of them. Signature colour is pa05's magenta #c44fbd on the money word and the CTA rule, with support #638f49 on the small caps. The pa04 run is the same build one step warmer: plane #d9f7d3, veil #2b3e27, accent violet #9265ee. ground:'tile' is itself the enforcement — lookFaults raises a fault on any other ground, and the tile pass cannot fall through to cast because the Apple pools never drop below four.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for whichever Apple line the seed deals — twelve cells on the iPhone and MacBook decks, eight on the iPad deck. Foreground: this is the collection's baseline card and it takes any honest current single unit the deck offers — a 17 Pro back, a 15 Pro blue, gold or white body, a black-glass front, a current qs- press render, or one of the two upright orange 17 Pro renders. On one card in three the engine also lays a lineup of up to five singles from the same deck pool; both hero and lineup are governed by the lists below. Marks are the deck's own icons (bolt, check, dollar, sparkle, battery, cash, shield, and on the iPhone deck a phone glyph); they are placed only in clear space, never over a word, and no logo is placeable at all.
looks.copy: Plain counter talk, nothing raised. The headline is the deck's own — SELL YOUR iPHONE, SELL YOUR iPAD or SELL YOUR MACBOOK — one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour across both lines, and the items line, the money line and the badges follow the same deck. The two selling points come from the engine's pool in its own order (the deck's sub lines first, then FREE WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE, then WRITTEN OFFER IN MINUTES and CASH THE SAME DAY from INFO.yes); at least two land on every card and none of them is a claim this recipe invented. Money keeps its UP TO. One seal only, whichever of VERIFIED BUYER, CERTIFIED DEALER, TOP RATED LOCAL or LICENSED & BONDED the engine drops into the free corner — the three-seal strip in the first draft was not producible, and the deck's own badges are LICENSED / INSURED / LOCAL. The sticker is one of the engine's five by seed. On reviewProof the rating is five stars, always five, with a reviewer line of first name, initial and city. On one card in three the engine swaps in the challenge framing: with WE MATCH the possessive is stripped (WE MATCH ECOATM, no apostrophe-S), with WE BEAT the possessive lands on line two and the thing beaten on line three.
variations: Teal run (pa05: #c6faeb plane, #1b4037 veil, magenta money word)
Mint run (pa04: #d9f7d3 plane, #2b3e27 veil, violet money word)
Challenge card (one seed in three: the deck copy is replaced by WE MATCH / ECOATM or WE BEAT / ECOATM'S / iPHONE TRADE-IN VALUE)

Removed iphone-15-pro-back-black, ip-angle-hero-tilt and ip-angle-back-topdown from mustShow and imagery — I opened all three: a camera-bump macro cropped on four edges (1841x1663), a body lying near-horizontal (1414x1406, aspect 1.01) and a top-corner crop cut on three edges (1200x732, aspect 1.64). The first is now banned by name; the other two cannot reach a layer at all because ip-angle-* is not in any deck's cuts.
Deleted 'so all twelve share one scale': k is a per-image contain fit and the pool's aspects run 0.42 to 1.11.

Replaced 'badges LICENSED · LOCAL · TOP RATED — never INSURED, that seal belongs to the car deck' with one seal from INFO.seals; the claim was inverted, since all three Apple decks carry LICENSED / INSURED / LOCAL.

looks.name: Quote Sheet Wall II
looks.oneLine: The palest plane in the set, veiled to olive charcoal, with a typewriter headline, mono figures and a foreground held to natural and pale bodies.
looks.groundSpec: pp04 c1 #f2f8ef has luminance 0.922 — the palest plane in the collection, a paper white with a green cast, and well clear of the 0.55 gate that would drop it to #eceef2. Same lattice: 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit, one shadow per cell at rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16. Veil is ink #2e3d25 at 0.60, so the wall settles to olive-charcoal; the panel pass fills every qualifying rect with rgba(#2e3d25,0.90), white on it 11.5:1. The Paper family's plate is the hairline (30px radius, faint rim, no drop), which is why this card reads as a ruled quote rather than a shadowed slab. Accent green #4a8704 carries the money word and the rule, support #599a1c the small caps. Special Elite has irregular-width figures, so the numerals are set in JetBrains Mono and align to the hairline; the typewriter face carries the headline only. The pp07 run turns the same card blue-grey: plane #eff7fe, veil #253a4e, accent #0378c7.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for the deck the seed deals. Foreground rule, and it is enforced: NATURAL AND PALE BODIES ONLY, so the card reads like unopened stock — the white and gold 15 Pro bodies, the silver 17 Pro, the grey iPad backs and fronts, the silver MacBook. Black and blue bodies, the orange renders and the wallpapered qs-ipad press sheets are banned below, so a mismatched card re-seeds instead of shipping. No receipt, no paper curl, no ornament: the only non-device element on the card is the hairline rule. Marks are the deck's own icons in the accent, placed clear of every word.
looks.copy: The written offer, typed. Special Elite on the headline only; body copy stays Libre Franklin and the figures stay JetBrains Mono, because a typewriter face is not handwriting but it is still not body copy. The headline is the deck's own sentence — SELL YOUR iPHONE / iPAD / MACBOOK — one sentence, one face, one colour. Two selling points land from the engine's pool; on this card the ones that read best are WRITTEN OFFER IN MINUTES and NO MAIL IT IN AND WAIT WEEKS, both real INFO lines, and whatever the engine deals is a real line too. One seal from INFO.seals in the free corner. Money keeps its UP TO. Five stars where a rating appears. When the challenge form fires the headline is WE MATCH / ECOATM — two lines, one sentence, one face, one colour, and NO apostrophe-S after WE MATCH, because the engine strips the possessive for WE MATCH and there is no third line for it to land in.

Slate run (pp07: #eff7fe plane, #253a4e veil, blue hairline)

looks.name: Deep Glass Wall II
looks.oneLine: The neutral plane drowned in jewel green, a serif headline on glass-cap plates, and a foreground of single bodies only — no composites, no pairs.
looks.groundSpec: Jewel is the deep branch. jw07 c1 #054e2f has luminance 0.057 and c2 #003928 is 0.031, so both fail the 0.55 gate and the plane falls back to the neutral #eceef2 — which is exactly why this wall is the most saturated in the set while its devices stay pale and legible. The veil is the jewel itself, c1 at 0.60. Lattice 4x3, gutters 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-unit contain fit, one shadow per cell rgba(0,0,0,0.28)/26/+10/+16. Panels take rgba(#054e2f,0.90): white on that is 9.8:1, so the small print holds. The Jewel plate is the glass cap — 38px radius, specular hairline, soft drop — and the panel pass overwrites the tint with a solid fill, so the cap keeps its shape and loses its glassiness; that is the engine, not a recipe choice. Accent lilac #e1c2fe carries the money word, support #9eb666 the small caps. The jw05 run swaps to teal: veil #044a51, accent pink #febbd3, white on panel 10.0:1. jw07 measured 50% against jw05's 39%, so the green run leads.
looks.imagery: Ground: the engine's wall for the deck the seed deals. Foreground rule, enforced: ONE PHOTOGRAPHED BODY, NO COMPOSITES. The qs- press sheets are two-up renders (a back overlapping a front) and they stay off this card, which is the quietest in the set; the hero is a single body — a 15 Pro blue, gold or white, a 17 Pro black or silver, a black-glass front, an iPad back, front or tilt. The one licensed exception is qs-device-macbook-, because on the MacBook seed those two files are the only honest current laptops left on the shelf. Marks are the deck's own icons in the support green, small, flanking the money word.
looks.copy: Considered and quiet — the serif does the selling and the copy stays short. The headline is the deck's own sentence, one sentence in one face, one weight, one colour; no serif is ever set on a curve here and no glow sits behind it. Two selling points from the engine's pool; CRACKED OR LOCKED STILL PAID and PAID BEFORE WE LEAVE are real INFO.yes lines and read well under a serif, but whatever the engine deals is a real line too. One seal from INFO.seals. Money keeps its UP TO. On reviewProof the rating is five stars, always five, with a quote mark and a reviewer line of pin, first name and initial, city and state. On one card in three the challenge framing replaces the deck copy: WE MATCH / ECOATM with no apostrophe-S, or WE BEAT / ECOATM'S / iPHONE TRADE-IN VALUE.
variations: Green jewel (jw07: #054e2f veil, lilac money word)
Teal jewel (jw05: #044a51 veil, pink money word)
